findings.title: Login form ships the production super-admin password as a prefilled default
findings.detail: useForm is created with defaultValues: { email: 'admin@barkath.app', password: 'Barkath@123' } (commented 'Dev convenience: prefilled with the seeded super-admin for the emulator'). These are not emulator-only values: /home/h/barkath/scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:22-23 bootstraps the REAL project (barkath-25607) with exactly EMAIL = process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL || 'admin@barkath.app' and PASSWORD = process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD || 'Barkath@123', granting that account role 'super_admin' + fullPerms(). Nothing guards the defaults behind env.useEmulators, so the literals are compiled into the shipped bundle.
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone who opens the deployed admin URL finds email and password already filled and clicks 'Sign in' -> if the project was bootstrapped without ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD overrides they are signed in as a full super admin. Even with an overridden password, the working super-admin username is published in the JS bundle.
findings.fix: Remove defaultValues, or gate them: defaultValues: env.useEmulators ? {seeded creds} : { email: '', password: '' }. Also make scripts/bootstrap-real.ts hard-fail when ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD are unset instead of falling back to the shared literals.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real and unguarded. admin/src/features/auth/components/LoginForm.tsx:30-34 sets useForm defaultValues to {email:'admin@barkath.app', password:'Barkath@123'} with no condition — the codebase has a working guard (env.useEmulators in admin/src/config/env.ts:11, used at admin/src/lib/firebase.ts:19,26) that this call site simply does not use. The literals are not emulator-only: scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:22-23 uses exactly ADMIN_EMAIL||'admin@barkath.app' and ADMIN_PASSWORD||'Barkath@123' when creating the real barkath-25607 super_admin with fullPerms(). Both admin/.env.production and admin/.env.development set VITE_USE_EMULATORS=false and point at project barkath-25607, so even local dev submits these prefilled creds against production. The password is verifiably compiled into the build output: grep finds 'Barkath@123' in admin/dist/assets/index-DQ93d6D0.js:3829. No server-side re-check mitigates it (the creds are genuinely valid, so rules/claims grant super_admin). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list (which covers mocked MSG91 OTP for customer login, manual affiliate payouts, Razorpay test mode, App Check — not admin login defaults). Only partial mitigation: firebase.json has no hosting block yet, so the panel may not be publicly deployed today, but a built bundle containing the secret already exists and the fix is one line (remove the defaults or gate on env.useEmulators).

findings.title: No route-level permission guard - sidebar hiding is the only gate, and admin Firestore reads are open to every sub-admin
findings.detail: RequireAuth (admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx:6-23) only checks admin != null; it never inspects modulePermissions, and no route carries a module guard. The only client gate is Sidebar.tsx:11-12 (canView) which merely hides nav links. Grepping admin/src shows modulePermissions is referenced in exactly three places (Sidebar.tsx:12, dashboard/components/QuickActions.tsx:42, subadmin form) - no list/detail page checks it. Server-side, firebase/firestore.rules gates only WRITES per module (canWrite); reads are isAdmin(): customers (line 138), orders (line 71), payments (line 84), reviews, orderRequests, commissions, auditLogs all allow any admin. On top of that LoginForm.tsx:41-42 always navigates to '/' after sign-in.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only banner.view signs in -> lands on the full Dashboard (revenue KPIs, recent orders with customer names, low stock) even though 'Dashboard' is hidden from their sidebar. Typing /customers in the address bar renders the complete customer list with every name, phone and email; /orders, /payments, /refunds and /reports work the same way. Nothing on the client or in the rules stops the read.
findings.fix: Add a permission guard component wrapping each route (module key per route, redirecting to a real /403 screen), and land the user on their first permitted route after login instead of '/'. Tighten the isAdmin() read rules on customers/orders/payments/reports collections to can(module,'view').

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute. (1) admin/src/app/router.tsx wraps every page in RequireAuth -> AppShell only; no route has a module guard. (2) RequireAuth.tsx checks `ready` and `admin != null` and nothing else. (3) A full grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is read only in Sidebar.tsx:12 (nav hiding), dashboard/components/QuickActions.tsx:42 (button hiding), subadmin/routes/SubAdminFormPage.tsx + subadmin/api/subadmin.ts (the editor/type), and account/AccountDialogs.tsx:59 (echoes it back) - no list/detail page, hook, or loader consults it; CustomersListPage.tsx calls useCustomersList() unconditionally on mount. (4) firebase/firestore.rules uses can()/canWrite() exclusively on `allow write`; reads for orders (71), payments (84), customers (138) and its walletTransactions/coupons/notifications subcollections, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests, spinHistory, reviews, stockAdjustments, broadcasts and auditLogs are plain isAdmin(). isAdmin() is `role == 'super_admin' || role == 'sub_admin'` from the custom claim, and functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:38 sets that claim for every sub-admin, so a banner-only sub-admin passes all of them. Only admins/* and complianceLogs require isSuperAdmin(), so /sub-admin is the sole page that would error; /customers, /orders, /payments, /refunds, /reports and the Dashboard all render real data. The `view` permission is collected and stored by the sub-admin form but enforced nowhere but nav rendering. Not on the already-fixed list (those entries - adminModerateReview, rules canWrite tightening - are write-side) nor the known-intentional list. Only inaccuracy in the claim is cosmetic: LoginForm.tsx:41-42 is `location.state?.from ?? '/'`, not an unconditional '/', but a fresh sign-in still lands on the full Dashboard. Real, fixable defect: needs a route-level module guard plus can(module,'view') on the admin read rules.

findings.title: Revenue trend renders a fake ascending "growth" chart while loading and forever on error
findings.detail: `{(trend.data ?? Array.from({length: 12}, (_, i) => ({label: '', heightPct: 6 + i * 7, paise: 0})))}` — when `useRevenueTrend` has no data the panel paints 12 real-looking bars with heights 6%, 13%, 20% … 83%, i.e. a smooth upward revenue curve. There is no `trend.isLoading` / `trend.isError` branch anywhere in the file, and the x-axis label row (line 138) maps over `trend.data ?? []` so it renders nothing. `queryClient` (admin/src/lib/queryClient.ts:7) sets `retry: 1` with no global error handler, so after two failed attempts the query settles in an error state and `trend.data` stays `undefined` permanently.
findings.failure_scenario: A composite index for `orders(status, createdAt)` is missing, or the emulator/network drops one of the 24 aggregate calls fired by `useRevenueTrend`. The admin opens the dashboard and sees a clean 12-month chart trending steadily upward with no error, no spinner and no month labels. Every bar is actually ₹0. Hovering shows the title `₹0`, which reads as a tooltip bug rather than a dead chart. The admin reports revenue growth to the owner from a chart that is pure decoration.
findings.fix: Branch explicitly: render a skeleton/shimmer when `trend.isLoading` and an error row ('Could not load revenue trend — retry') when `trend.isError`. Never synthesize non-zero `heightPct` values. If a placeholder is wanted, use flat/zero-height bars plus the real month labels from `planBuckets(range)` so the axis is present.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. DashboardPage.tsx:129 falls back to a hardcoded 12-bar ascending ramp (heightPct 6,13,20…83, paise 0) rendered with the identical TREND_BAR gradient used for real bars, and the file contains no trend.isLoading/isError branch (trend is referenced only at lines 35, 129, 138) while its sibling panels do handle loading (KPI cards line 66/77/88/95, recent-orders table line 186). The x-axis row at line 138 maps trend.data ?? [], so no labels appear as a cue. The placeholder is provably not equivalent to real empty data: useRevenueTrend (dashboard.ts:451) emits heightPct 2 for zero-revenue buckets, so an empty store renders flat stubs, not a growth curve. The error state is terminal: queryClient.ts sets retry:1 with no global error handler, and grep for throwOnError/ErrorBoundary/useErrorBoundary across admin/src returns zero hits, so a rejection neither surfaces nor is retried and trend.data stays undefined. The failure is reachable because useRevenueTrend fires 2 aggregates per bucket via sumRealisedPaise (dashboard.ts:437-444) and sumTotalPaise/countOrders deliberately re-throw anything other than unimplemented/not-implemented (lines 52-55, 86, 99), so one failing call among the 24 rejects the whole Promise.all. heightPct is used nowhere else except ReportsPage, which renders its trend from real data with no synthetic fallback, so no other surface justifies the placeholder. Not on the already-fixed list (that covers query scoping, not this render fallback) and not on the known-intentional list. Extra symptom: the fallback is always 12 bars even when 30D/7D is selected. Fix is straightforward: add isLoading/isError branches and delete the synthetic array.

findings.title: Referral price & commission typed on a single-price product are silently thrown away on save
findings.detail: The pricing table's own hint (line 448-451) says "set price, offer, referral & commission for each. Leave Color/Size as '—' for a single-price product." But at save time only rows that pass `isVariantRow` (line 38-39: has a stored variant id, a colorId, a sizeId, or some other attribute) become variants. A single-price row has none of those, so `hasVariants` is false (line 200) and `variants: []` is written (line 264). `referralPricePaise` / `commissionPaise` (lines 256-257) only exist inside a variant object — there is no top-level product field for them and none is written by `saveProduct` (api/products.ts:124-154). Nothing warns the admin; the save reports success. Re-opening the product runs `productToRows` (line 62), which hardcodes `referral: '', comm: ''` for the non-variant branch, so the fields come back blank. No other admin screen edits these fields (grep over admin/src finds referral/commission only in this form and lib/pricing.ts).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens a simple product with no colour/size (e.g. a gift card), types Price 2499, Offer 1999, Referral 1799, Comm. 200, clicks "Save changes" and gets the "Changes saved" toast. Firestore stores mrpPaise/offerPricePaise only; referral and commission are gone. Re-opening the product shows both cells empty, and web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:213 (`product.isAffiliateEligible && referralPaise != null`, where referralPaise comes from `variant?.referralPricePaise`) never renders the AFFILIATE box for that product.
findings.fix: Either persist the single-row referral/commission on the product doc (add referralPricePaise/commissionPaise to the Product type + saveProduct and make web/app fall back to them when `variant` is undefined), or disable/grey the Referral and Comm. cells on a row with no Color/Size and explain why.

verdict.reason: Claim holds up. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx, isVariantRow (l.38-39) requires a stored variant id, colorId, sizeId or extra attribute; the single-price row the form's own hint (l.448-451) tells admins to create ("Leave Color/Size as '—' for a single-price product") has none, so hasVariants is false (l.200) and variants: [] is written (l.264). referralPricePaise/commissionPaise are produced only inside the variant map (l.256-257). I confirmed there is no fallback: packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts puts these fields on ProductVariant only (l.40-41) — Product has no top-level equivalent — and saveProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:124-154) never writes them. No other surface supplies them: grep over admin/src finds referral/commission only in this form, lib/pricing.ts (validation, which ironically validates the referral/comm ladder for the row it is about to discard) and csv.ts:128 (passes referral: ''); functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-69 accrues from the affiliate's commissionRate and never reads or backfills the variant field. Round-trip loss confirmed by productToRows l.62 hardcoding referral: '', comm: ''. A real consumer exists: web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:113-114 and :214 gate the AFFILIATE box on variant?.referralPricePaise, so a simple product can never display it. Reachable in practice: scripts/seed.ts:330 gives non-clothing products variants: [], and importProducts (api/products.ts:305-306) creates hasVariants: false products. The guard at l.195-204 addresses the inverse bug (wiping an existing variant set) and does not fire here. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderate rather than financial (the field is storefront-display only; commission accrual uses the affiliate rate), but it is a genuine, fixable silent data-loss/broken-CRUD defect that reports success.

findings.title: Per-variant commissionPaise is advertised to shoppers as guaranteed earnings but the commission engine never reads it
findings.detail: The form writes `commissionPaise` per variant (line 257) and `saveProduct` persists it (api/products.ts:139). web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:214-223 renders it verbatim: "Referral price ₹X · you earn ₹Y per sale". But the money that is actually paid is computed in functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-69 as `Math.floor(eligiblePaise * normaliseRate(affiliate.commissionRate))` — the referring customer's own rate on the whole merchandise value. Grep across functions/src finds zero reads of `variants[].commissionPaise` or of the product-level `affiliateCommissionRate` (which admin always writes as `null`, api/products.ts:181/322). So the number an admin types per variant has no effect on any payout whatsoever, while being shown to affiliates as a promise.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sets Comm. = ₹200 on the Green/M variant of a ₹1999 product. The storefront product page tells the affiliate "you earn ₹200.00 per sale". A referred customer buys one; placeOrder accrues `1999_00 * affiliate.commissionRate` (5% ⇒ ₹99.95) into `commissions`, and the affiliate dashboard shows ~₹100. The admin-entered ₹200 is never used and the affiliate is under-paid relative to what the storefront promised.
findings.fix: Make accrueCommission prefer the ordered variant's `commissionPaise` (and the product's `affiliateCommissionRate`) when present, falling back to the affiliate rate — or stop writing/displaying per-variant commission and remove the Comm. column and the web "you earn" copy.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real cross-surface defect. Admin ProductFormPage.tsx:257 persists per-variant `commissionPaise`, and web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:113-114,214-223 renders it verbatim as "you earn ₹Y per sale" (gate is effectively always open: admin hardcodes isAffiliateEligible:true at api/products.ts:180/321, and the banner is not restricted to affiliate viewers). The paid amount comes solely from functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:66-68 `Math.floor(eligiblePaise * normaliseRate(affiliate.commissionRate))`, invoked at functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:675-687 with eligiblePaise = subtotal - discount — a whole-order figure with no per-variant or per-product term. Exhaustive greps over functions/src, web/src, app/lib and packages/shared show no reader of variants[].commissionPaise outside the admin form and the web product page (all other commissionPaise hits are the unrelated field on commissions/{id} docs), and product-level affiliateCommissionRate is written as null by all four writers and read by nobody. Reachable in practice: scripts/seed.ts:338-339 populates both fields. Not on the already-fixed list; the "payouts are deliberately manual" exemption covers bank transfer, not accrual, which is automated. Only nuance: seed values coincidentally equal 5% of offer price, hiding the divergence in demo data for single-item, discount-free orders; any admin-typed value or multi-item/discounted cart diverges.

findings.title: Failed/timed-out adjustStock call leaves the deltas loaded → a retry applies the same stock delta twice
findings.detail: `adminAdjustStock` mutates stock relatively (`after = Math.max(0, before + delta)`, functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81 and :92) and carries NO idempotency key — the payload has only {productId, variantId, delta}. The client acknowledges this risk for exactly one path: `LedgerWriteError` (api/inventory.ts:58-63, 128-134), where it clears `deltas` so Save can't re-fire. Every OTHER failure falls into the `else` at AdjustStockPage.tsx:99-101, which shows the generic toast 'Could not save adjustments.' and leaves `deltas` fully populated and the Save button re-enabled. `httpsCallable` throws identically for 'the transaction never ran' and 'the transaction committed but the response was lost' (deadline-exceeded / internal / network drop), so the screen invites the operator to redo a write that already landed.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin sets +50 on SKU PERF-AMB-50 (stock 10) and clicks Save. The callable commits the transaction (stock now 60) but the HTTP response is lost on a flaky connection. The toast reads 'Could not save adjustments.', the stepper still shows +50, so the admin clicks Save again. Stock becomes 110 and two ledger rows appear (10→60 and 60→110) for one physical delivery of 50 units.
findings.fix: Give the callable an idempotency key: have the client generate a UUID per Save, pass it in the payload, and have adminAdjustStock record/short-circuit on `stockAdjustmentBatches/{key}` inside the same transaction. Failing that, clear `deltas` and force a reload on ANY error from `adjustStock`, and tell the operator to re-check the current stock before adjusting again.

verdict.reason: Every factual element checks out. adminAdjustStock mutates stock relatively (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81, :92) and its zod schema (lines 11-23) carries no nonce/idempotency field, so a replay compounds the delta. The client (admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:52-57) documents this exact hazard in a comment — "no idempotency key, so the caller must NOT offer a plain retry" — but wires the mitigation only into the ledger-batch catch (128-134, clearing deltas via LedgerWriteError). AdjustStockPage.tsx:99-101 handles every other failure with a generic toast, leaves `deltas` fully populated, and `finally` (102-104) re-enables Save. Firebase callables are a single POST with no auto-retry, so "transaction committed but response lost" (network drop / deadline-exceeded) is indistinguishable from "never ran", and the screen invites a human retry that double-applies. No server-side re-check, no reconciliation from stockAdjustments (explicitly "history, not the source of truth"), and the live product snapshot is incidental UX rather than a guard. The page is routed (admin/src/app/router.tsx:72). Not on the already-fixed list (which covers only the {before,after} return values) nor the known-intentional list. Fixable with an in-repo pattern: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:437-446 already claims idempotencyKeys/{uid}__{hash} inside the transaction from a client nonce. One caveat on framing: the correct fix is that server-side nonce, NOT clearing deltas in the else branch — most errors reaching it (not-found batch rejection at inventory.ts:108-113, permission-denied, invalid-argument) are definite non-commits where retry is the intended remedy. Confidence is medium because the trigger window is narrow (response lost after commit) and the claim anchors the fix at the wrong layer, but the underlying correctness gap is real.

findings.title: Saving a product from the Products form writes back the variant stock snapshot taken when the form opened, silently reverting inventory adjustments
findings.detail: `existingRef.current` is loaded exactly once per mount (ProductFormPage.tsx:107-135 — a `getProduct` inside a useEffect keyed on [isNew, routeId, navigate], not a live subscription). At save time each variant is rebuilt with `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` where `prev` comes from that stale ref, and saveProduct writes the whole array (`variants: values.variants`, products/api/products.ts:138). Nothing merges or re-reads stock at commit time, and the rule `products/{id}: allow write: if canWrite('products')` lets that client write through. Every stock change made after the form opened — an adminAdjustStock adjustment, a placeOrder decrement, a cancel restock — is overwritten.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin A opens 'Amber Oud 50ml' to fix a typo in the description at 10:00. At 10:05 Admin B receives 200 units and adjusts variant AMB-50 from 12 → 212 in Inventory (the stockAdjustments ledger records 12→212). At 10:10 Admin A clicks Save. The variants array is written with stock: 12. Inventory now shows 12 again, the history modal still shows the 212 entry, and 200 units of real inventory are invisible to the storefront.
findings.fix: Re-read the product inside a transaction at save time and merge only the form-owned variant fields (price/label/sku/attributes), never `stock`; or move the variants write into a callable that patches per-field instead of replacing the array.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real and fixable. `existingRef.current` in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx is a mount-time snapshot (one-shot `getProduct` in a useEffect keyed [isNew, routeId, navigate], line 107-136; no live subscription writes to it). At save, line 252 emits `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` (plus weight/visibility at 258-259) from that snapshot, and saveProduct's edit branch does a whole-array replace via `variants: values.variants` (products.ts:139, spread into updateDoc at line 198) with no stock merge — even though it already re-reads the doc at line 197 for bestSellerOrder/publishedAt, so the fresh data is right there. No server guard: firestore.rules:50-52 is an unrestricted `allow write: if canWrite('products')`, and there is no product document trigger in functions/src. Stock genuinely lives in the clobbered array: adminAdjustStock rewrites `update.variants` with `{...v, stock: after}` (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:86-96), placeOrder decrements `v.stock` (orders/checkout.ts:559-560), cancel restocks it (orders/cancel.ts:119). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Decisive counter-evidence to "intended": the identical stale-write hazard was explicitly recognised and fixed for the rating aggregate in this same function (ratingPatch, lines 213-222, and the ProductFormValues doc comment at products.ts:106-113) — stock simply did not get the same treatment. Only refinement to the claim: non-variant products are unaffected (top-level `stock` is not part of the edit payload); the loss is limited to variant products, which is the scenario described.

findings.title: Blocking a customer enforces nothing — no rule or Cloud Function ever reads isBlocked, and the Auth-disable failure is swallowed
findings.detail: `adminBlockUser` writes `customers/{uid}.isBlocked = true` and then calls `auth.updateUser(uid, {disabled:true}).catch(() => undefined)` and `revokeRefreshTokens(...).catch(() => undefined)`. Every failure is swallowed, and the Firestore flag itself is enforced NOWHERE: `grep -rn isBlocked` over functions/, web/src, app/lib and firebase/firestore.rules returns only (a) this file, (b) the admin UI badge/label, (c) `request.resource.data.isBlocked == false` on customer *create* (firestore.rules:152), (d) the two clients writing `false` at signup. `placeOrder` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts), `executeSpin`, `topUpWallet`, `createReturnRequest`, `linkReferral` and the write rules for cart/addresses/reviews/wishlist contain no block check at all. So the ONLY enforcement is the Auth `disabled` flag — and seeded/imported customers (scripts/seed.ts:412 writes `customers/cust_001..008` with no `auth.createUser`) have no Firebase Auth record, so `updateUser` throws user-not-found, is caught, and the callable still returns `{ok:true}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens /customers/cust_003 for a fraud account, clicks 'Block user', confirms. Toast says 'Yusuf Ali blocked' and the list badge flips to red 'Blocked'. Nothing happened: there is no Auth user to disable (error swallowed), no rule and no callable reads isBlocked, so the customer keeps placing COD orders, spending wallet balance, spinning and filing returns indefinitely. Even for a customer who does have an Auth user, an already-signed-in session keeps a valid ID token for up to an hour, and onCall does not check revocation, so checkout keeps working after the block.
findings.fix: Add an `isBlocked` guard to the privileged customer callables (checkout/spin/topup/returns/linkReferral) and to the client-write rules (e.g. `get(/databases/$(database)/documents/customers/$(uid())).data.isBlocked == false` on cart/address/review writes). Stop swallowing the Auth errors: if `auth.updateUser` fails with anything other than user-not-found, throw so the admin sees the block did not take.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo and could not refute. (1) functions/src/customers/moderation.ts:28 does `auth.updateUser(uid,{disabled:true}).catch(()=>undefined)` and `revokeRefreshTokens(...).catch(()=>undefined)`, then returns {ok:true} — every failure is silent, so the admin toast lies whenever the Auth call fails. (2) A full-repo grep for `isBlocked` (excluding node_modules/dist/.next) returns ONLY: moderation.ts (writes), firestore.rules:161 (`request.resource.data.isBlocked == false` on customer CREATE — a write-shape constraint, not an access gate), packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:119 (type), admin UI badge/label (CustomerProfilePage.tsx, CustomersListPage.tsx), and web/src/lib/customerDoc.ts:40 / scripts/seed.ts:428 / e2e returns.spec.ts:31 writing `false`. Zero hits in app/lib. (3) functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:28 `requireCustomer` is only `if (!req.auth) throw; return {uid}` — it never reads the customer doc, and all customer callables (placeOrder, applyCoupon, reserveStock, executeSpin, topUpWallet, createReturnRequest, linkReferral, affiliate requests) use it. firestore.rules has no blocked helper; cart/addresses/wishlist/reviews writes are isOwner-only. (4) No beforeUserSignedIn/beforeUserCreated blocking function exists in functions/src, and callableOpts (functions/src/_lib/admin.ts) adds no revocation check, so an existing ID token stays accepted by both rules and onCall for up to ~1h after a block. (5) scripts/seed.ts uses auth.createUser only in upsertAdmin (line 65); seedCustomers writes customers/cust_001..008 with no Auth record, so updateUser throws user-not-found, is swallowed, and nothing at all happens. Mitigation that softens but does not refute: real customers DO have Auth users (web/src/lib/otp/mockOtpService.ts uses createUserWithEmailAndPassword), so `disabled:true` does prevent future sign-in for them — the claim's 'enforces nothing' is overstated for that population, but the dead Firestore flag, the swallowed error, and the ≤1h live-session window are all real. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; fix is straightforward (read isBlocked in requireCustomer, surface the Auth failure).

findings.title: COD payments are never settled — delivered COD orders stay "Pending" forever, and are silently excluded from the GST export and the month total
findings.detail: `placeOrder` writes `payments/{orderId}` with `status: 'pending'` for every COD order (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:612 `paymentStatus = fullyWalletPaid ? 'captured' : 'pending'`, written to the payment doc at checkout.ts:708). The ONLY writers of that document afterwards are `verifyPayment` (razorpay only, checkout.ts:931) and `performCancellation` (cancel.ts:219). `adminChangeOrderStatus` → `delivered` (functions/src/orders/status.ts:122) updates `deliveredAt` and the customer stats and nothing else — it never touches `payments/{orderId}` and never flips `orders.paymentStatus`. returns/decisions.ts:43 even documents this ("the cash was collected even though paymentStatus stays 'pending'"). Consequence in this module: PaymentsListPage.tsx:34-38 only sums `status === 'captured'` into the month figure, and onExport(true) at line 55 filters `p.status === 'captured'`.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin marks a ₹2,400 COD order delivered and the rider hands in the cash. On /payments the row still shows the gold "Pending" badge, the header still reads "₹0 this month · 0 failed" for a COD-only day, and clicking "GST invoices" produces a CSV that contains no COD orders at all — i.e. for a COD-heavy store the GST export is empty and the revenue headline reads ₹0.
findings.fix: In `adminChangeOrderStatus`, when transitioning to `delivered` and the order's paymentMethod is `cod`, set `payments/{orderId}.status='captured'`, `capturedAt=now`, and stamp `orders.paymentStatus='captured'` / `amountPaidPaise=totalPaise` in the same transaction.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. Only three writers of `payments/{orderId}` exist across the whole repo: checkout.ts:698 (creates it with status 'pending' for COD, per checkout.ts:612 `fullyWalletPaid ? findings.title: Wheel editor can never produce a `better_luck` slice — the "==" toggle silently means free_shipping
findings.detail: `prizeTypeFor(kind, prev)` returns `prev === 'better_luck' ? 'better_luck' : 'free_shipping'` for the `special` kind. The row editor (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:431-444) renders exactly three buttons — `₹`, `%`, `==` — with no sub-choice between the two special prize types, and `newRow()` (CampaignDetailPage.tsx:103-118) always starts a row at `flat_discount`. Therefore clicking `==` on any newly added row always yields `free_shipping`, and there is no path in the UI to reach `better_luck` at all. `executeSpin` (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:129-132) classifies `free_shipping` as `isCoupon`, mints a real `customers/{uid}/coupons` doc with `discountType:'free_shipping'`, and `computeCouponDiscount` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:192-193, 331) sets `waiveDelivery = true` for it. The `==` glyph is also identical for both types, so an existing `better_luck` slice and a `free_shipping` slice are visually indistinguishable in the editor.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens a campaign, deletes the starter "Better luck next time" row, clicks "Add offer", types "Better luck next time", clicks `==`, sets weight 40, and saves. The wheel now has a 40%-weighted slice labelled "Better luck next time" whose `prizeType` is `free_shipping`. Every customer who lands on the losing slice is issued a free-shipping coupon (app shows "You won!" via SpinOutcome, prizeType != 'better_luck'), and delivery is waived on their next order. The admin has no way to see or fix this from the editor.
findings.fix: Split the `special` toggle into two explicit choices (e.g. a `🚚` free-shipping button and a `✕` better-luck button), or add a prize-type select for special slices. `prizeTypeFor` must be able to return `better_luck` from a non-better_luck previous value.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect; I could not refute it. prizeTypeFor(kind='special', prev) at admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:90 returns better_luck only when prev is already better_luck, and newRow() (admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:103-118) always starts at flat_discount, so the three-button toggle (lines 431-444, the ONLY prizeType writer in all of admin/src — verified by grep) can never produce better_luck on a new row. No downstream guard exists: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:129-132 treats free_shipping as isCoupon and mints a customers/{uid}/coupons doc, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:191-193 + 347 force waiveDelivery/freeDelivery. better_luck is not a dead enum: web/src/app/(shop)/spin/result/page.tsx:27 uses prizeType !== 'better_luck' to decide "won", and app/lib/features/spin/spin_screen.dart:112 + spin_reward_screen.dart:99 render "SO CLOSE" vs "YOU WON". findings.title: No editor for `discountMaxCapPaise` / `minCartValuePaise` — every spin-won percent coupon is uncapped with no cart minimum

Worse, personal spin coupons are also auto-applied without the customer entering a code (`autoBestOffer`, checkout.ts:299-318). The label placeholder even advertises constraints the form cannot store: "Reward text (e.g. ₹10 off · min ₹99)" (line 452).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin adds an offer, clicks `%`, types 50, labels it "50% off · min ₹999", weight 5, saves. A customer wins it, adds a ₹40,000 order to the cart, and checkout auto-applies the coupon with no cap and no minimum — ₹20,000 is deducted. The admin believed the '· min ₹999' text in the label constrained it; that text is purely cosmetic.
findings.fix: Add "Min cart (₹)" and "Max discount (₹)" inputs to each non-special row, converting with `paiseFromRupees`, and require a cap on `percent` slices before allowing save.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. The spin campaign editor (admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx) keeps minCartValuePaise/discountMaxCapPaise on Row (lines 59-60, self-described as "preserved (not surfaced in this editor)") and writes them back in rowToSlice (92-93), but renders no input for either; newRow() hardcodes 0/null (113-114) and starterSlices() in admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:126 does the same. CreateCampaignPage.tsx has no slice fields at all, so every slice an admin authors in the UI is permanently uncapped with no cart minimum (only scripts/seed.ts:751-756 contains real values, and they survive only via the round-trip). No backstop exists downstream: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:165-166 copies both fields onto the issued personal coupon verbatim, and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts treats absent as unlimited in all four sites (cap>0 guards at 199, 223, 292, 312; min-cart at 214 and 305). I grepped functions/src for any settings-level default cap and found none. autoBestOffer (checkout.ts:299-317) does apply personal spin coupons with no code entered, so the failure scenario needs no customer action. Refutation attempts all failed: the fields are authored only by the promotional coupon form (admin/src/features/coupons/routes/CouponFormPage.tsx); web/ and app/ merely read/format them; the route is registered at admin/src/app/router.tsx:84 so the path is reachable; and it is on neither the already-fixed nor known-intentional list. Decisively, CouponFormPage.tsx:132-133 hard-blocks saving a percent coupon without a cap ("A max-discount cap is required for percentage coupons."), so the spinner path can only ever produce exactly what the project's own rule forbids, with Math.min(discountPaise, eligiblePaise) as the sole limit (up to 100% of cart). The placeholder "Reward text (e.g. Rs.10 off, min Rs.99)" at line 452 is cosmetic but reinforces rather than refutes the claim.

findings.title: Suspending a sub-admin does not stop CF-gated actions — requireModule never checks the stored status
findings.detail: requireModule() only calls requireAdmin() (which reads `status` off the *custom claim* in the ID token, guards.ts:21) and then reads `modulePermissions` from admins/{uid}; it never checks `snap.get('status')`. suspendSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:88-96) sets the claim, disables the Auth user and calls revokeRefreshTokens — but firebase-functions v2 `onCall` verifies the ID token WITHOUT checkRevoked (callableOpts in functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25 sets no such option), so an already-issued ID token stays valid for up to an hour. firestore.rules `can()` (firebase/firestore.rules:23-29) *does* check `adminDoc().status == 'active'`, and functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:29-31 explicitly re-checks the stored status with the comment "Suspended sub-admins are rejected on the stored doc, not only on the (cacheable) custom claim" — requireModule is the one gate that was never given that check.
findings.failure_scenario: A super admin discovers a rogue ops sub-admin and clicks Sub Admin → ⋮ → Suspend. The toast says "Arjun Rao suspended" and his row flips to Suspended. With his browser tab still open (token minted <60 min ago) he can still call adminDecideReturn (refunds.approve), adminAdjustWallet (customers.edit) and adminUpdateOrderStatus (orders.edit) — i.e. he can keep pushing wallet refunds and money-moving return approvals for up to an hour after being suspended, while the admin UI shows him as locked out.
findings.fix: In requireModule(), after fetching admins/{uid}, reject when `!snap.exists || snap.get('status') !== 'active'` (exactly as requireReviewModeration does), and do the same in requireSuperAdmin by reading the stored doc rather than trusting claims.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — the claim holds on every point I checked.

1. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/_lib/guards.ts:42-57 — requireModule() calls requireAdmin() (line 47), which only inspects `claims.status` off the ID token (guards.ts:21), then fetches `admins/{uid}` (line 49) and reads ONLY `modulePermissions`. It never reads `snap.get('status')` and never checks `snap.exists`. The doc read is already being paid for, so the missing check is a one-line fix.

2. Token staleness is real, not theoretical. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:88-96 sets the custom claim, calls auth.updateUser({disabled:true}) and revokeRefreshTokens — but firebase-functions v5.1.1 verifies callable tokens at /home/h/barkath/node_modules/.pnpm/firebase-functions@5.1.1_firebase-admin@12.7.0/node_modules/firebase-functions/lib/common/providers/https.js:330 with `verifyIdToken(idToken)` and no checkRevoked argument. Without checkRevoked, verifyIdToken ignores both revocation and the disabled flag, so an already-minted ID token (stale `status:'active'` claim) passes for the remainder of its ~1h life. callableOpts (/home/h/barkath/functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25-33) sets no option that would change this.

3. The stored-status re-check exists on the two other surfaces, which makes requireModule the odd one out: firebase/firestore.rules can() requires `adminDoc().status == 'active'` for sub-admins, and /home/h/barkath/functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:29-31 does `if (!snap.exists || snap.get('status') !== 'active') throw` with a comment explicitly stating suspended sub-admins must be rejected on the stored doc rather than the cacheable claim. Same code shape, one gate missing.

4. Blast radius is money-moving, matching the scenario: requireModule is the sole gate on adminAdjustWallet (src/wallet/adjust.ts:23, customers.edit), adminDecideReturn / the second refunds callable (src/returns/decisions.ts:19 and :197, refunds.approve), affiliate withdrawal approve/pay (src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:18,84,98,134), order status/shipment (src/orders/status.ts:54, src/orders/shipment.ts:22), spin grant (src/spin/grant.ts:19), inventory (src/catalog/inventory.ts:26), broadcasts and invoices. None of them re-check status themselves.

5. Not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED list (that list mentions the reviews-only adminModerateReview callable, which is precisely the one that DID get the check) and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list (App Check being unenforced is unrelated — this is authorization of an authenticated admin, and enforceAppCheck:false is not what lets the stale token through).

Only nuance worth noting: the window is bounded by the token's remaining lifetime (≤1 hour), not indefinite, and the admin client will fail to refresh afterwards. That limits duration, not severity — wallet refunds and return approvals inside that window are irreversible money movement while the UI reports the account as locked out.

findings.title: updateSubAdmin changes role/permissions but never revokes refresh tokens — demoted super admin keeps super_admin for up to an hour
findings.detail: updateSubAdmin calls `auth.setCustomUserClaims(uid, {role, status})` and updates the doc, but unlike suspendSubAdmin (line 92) it never calls `auth.revokeRefreshTokens(uid)`. Custom claims only land in a new ID token, so the target's existing token still carries `role: 'super_admin'`. firestore.rules short-circuits every gate on that claim (`isSuperAdmin()` at line 13, used first in `can()` at line 24) and every CF guard does the same (guards.ts:35, 48), so the stale claim is full authority.
findings.failure_scenario: Super admin A opens Sub Admin → edits super admin B → changes Role to "Sub admin" and leaves only Dashboard on → Save changes. The list immediately shows B as Sub admin. B, still signed in, is unaffected for up to 60 minutes: `isSuperAdmin()` is still true in rules so he can rewrite settings/GST, products and coupons, and `requireSuperAdmin` still passes so he can call createSubAdmin and mint himself a brand-new super-admin account — permanently defeating the demotion.
findings.fix: Call `await auth.revokeRefreshTokens(uid)` in updateSubAdmin whenever role (or modulePermissions) changes, and stamp tokenRevokedAt, mirroring suspendSubAdmin.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:67 updateSubAdmin only calls setCustomUserClaims + ref.update — no revokeRefreshTokens, no disable, and it never stamps tokenRevokedAt (that field is written solely by suspendSubAdmin at line 95, which does revoke at line 92), so the asymmetry is real. findings.title: NotificationBell is never mounted, and nothing ever writes adminAlerts

findings.failure_scenario: A super admin creates a sub-admin, the sub-admin signs in daily for a week, then the super admin opens Sub Admin -> the 'Last active' column (SubAdminListPage.tsx:140, which falls back lastActiveAt -> lastLoginAt) still shows the value stamped at creation time and never moves. findings.fix: In signInAdmin, after the admins doc check, updateDoc(doc(db,'admins',uid), { lastLoginAt: serverTimestamp(), lastActiveAt: serverTimestamp() }) - the rules already permit exactly these two fields with request.time.

findings.title: Login page advertises two-factor authentication that does not exist anywhere
findings.detail: The sign-in card renders a shield badge reading 'Protected by two-factor authentication'. There is no MFA anywhere in the codebase: signInAdmin (features/auth/api/auth.ts:18-52) does plain signInWithEmailAndPassword with no multiFactor resolver, no TOTP/SMS challenge screen exists, and there is no enrollment UI. findings.failure_scenario: An admin (or a security reviewer) reads the login screen and believes accounts are protected by a second factor; in reality a leaked or guessed password is the only credential needed. The mfaEnrolled column stays false for every admin forever with no way to enrol.
findings.fix: Either remove the badge text, or implement Firebase Auth multi-factor (TOTP) enrolment in the Profile dialog and a challenge step in signInAdmin, and start reading/writing mfaEnrolled/mfaMethod/mfaEnrolledAt.

verdict.reason: Claim verified; refutation attempts failed. admin/src/features/auth/routes/LoginPage.tsx:65-68 renders the present-tense assertion "Protected by two-factor authentication" under the sign-in form. signInAdmin (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:18-52) is plain signInWithEmailAndPassword plus an admins/{uid} status check — no getMultiFactorResolver, and its error switch does not even handle auth/multi-factor-auth-required, so if Identity Platform MFA were enforced project-side login would dead-end on the generic "Could not sign in" branch.
