One inaccuracy in the claim: there is no rendered mfaEnrolled column (admin/src never references the field), so that half of the failure scenario overstates; the substance holds. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the finding is misleading UI copy plus dead schema rather than broken logic; the underlying facts are certain. Fix: delete LoginPage.tsx lines 65-68, or implement enrolment and drop the three dead fields if the schema slot is not being reserved deliberately.

findings.title: KPI cards render ₹0 / 0 as real values when the KPI query fails
findings.detail: `const k = kpis.data;` and every card falls back with `?? 0` (lines 65, 76, 87, 94). `kpis.isError` is never read — only `kpis.isLoading` is passed to `KpiCard`, which shows an em-dash. Once react-query exhausts its single retry, `isLoading` flips to false and `isError` to true, so `formatMoneyCompact(0)` → "₹0" and `String(0)` → "0" are painted in the same bold KPI type as genuine numbers. The delta line falls through to the null-baseline branch and shows the neutral 'vs yesterday' / 'across 0 orders' text, which looks like a legitimate quiet day. `useDashboardKpis` fires 21 aggregate queries in one `Promise.all` (dashboard.ts:155-169) — any single rejection (index missing, quota, transient) nukes all four cards at once.
findings.failure_scenario: One of the 21 aggregate queries throws `failed-precondition` (missing index) at 9am. The admin opens the dashboard and sees Today's revenue ₹0, Total orders 0, Pending orders 0 (green 'all clear'), Avg order value ₹0. They conclude the store took no orders and that there is nothing to pack, while real accepted orders sit unpacked in the Orders queue.
findings.fix: Read `kpis.isError` in `DashboardPage` and render an explicit error tile per card (or one banner) with a retry button; never substitute `0` for 'unknown'. Same treatment for `products.error` (the `useLiveCollection` snapshot already carries `error`).

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. DashboardPage.tsx:44 takes `kpis.data` and every KPI card falls back to `?? 0` (lines 65, 76, 87, 94) while only passing `kpis.isLoading` to KpiCard; `isError` is read nowhere in the file, and a grep across admin/src/**/*.tsx finds no `isError` usage at all. The project is on @tanstack/react-query ^5.51.0, where `isLoading = isPending && isFetching`, so once retry:1 is exhausted `isLoading` flips false with `data` still undefined — KpiCard.tsx:20 then paints `value` (formatMoneyCompact(0)="₹0", String(0)="0") in the same 26px extrabold type as real figures, and the pending-orders card shows a green "all clear". There is no safety net: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/queryClient.ts declares no QueryCache onError and no throwOnError, and there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src, so a failed KPI fetch is surfaced nowhere. The fan-out count is exact — the Promise.all at dashboard.ts:155-169 has 13 entries but sumRealisedPaise/countRealisedOrders each issue 2 aggregates (lines 118-132) = 21 server aggregates, any one of which rejects the whole promise. Reachability is real, not theoretical: isAggregateUnsupported (dashboard.ts:52-55) deliberately re-throws everything except unimplemented/not-implemented, so failed-precondition (missing status+createdAt index), permission-denied (orders read is isAdmin()-gated in firebase/firestore.rules:69) and resource-exhausted all propagate — and that function's own comment states errors must surface, an intent the UI never completes. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list ("Dashboard queries were scoped" is about query scope) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL. Only partial mitigation: the Recent-orders live listener would still list orders under an index/quota failure, giving a contradicting signal; under permission failure both go blank and the display is consistently wrong.

findings.title: Dashboard is reachable by any sub-admin regardless of the `dashboard` module permission, and Firestore rules let them read every order
findings.detail: `{ path: '/', element: <DashboardPage /> }` sits under `RequireAuth` only (admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx), which checks that an admin doc exists and nothing else — there is no module guard on any route. `Sidebar.tsx:12` hides nav items whose `modulePermissions[module].view !== true`, so `dashboard` looks gated, but `LoginForm.tsx:41-42` redirects every successful login to `'/'`. On the server side `firebase/firestore.rules:69` allows `read` on `orders/{orderId}` for `isAdmin()` — any sub_admin — with no module check, and `products` (line 51) is world-readable. So the dashboard's revenue aggregates succeed for a sub-admin who has `dashboard.view === false` and `orders.view === false`.
findings.failure_scenario: A super-admin creates a reviews-only moderator with every module unchecked except `reviews`. The moderator logs in, is redirected to `/`, and immediately sees Today's revenue, lifetime Total orders, Average order value, the 12-month revenue trend, the five most recent orders with customer names and totals, and the low-stock list — all data their permission matrix explicitly denies. The Dashboard link is missing from their sidebar, which makes the exposure invisible to the admin who provisioned them.
findings.fix: Add a module-permission route guard (wrap each route element in a `<RequireModule module="dashboard" />`-style component keyed off the same `navConfig` mapping the sidebar uses) and redirect users without `dashboard.view` to their first permitted route after login instead of `'/'`. Optionally tighten the `orders` read rule to `can('orders','view') || can('dashboard','view') || ...` so the client-side gate is backed by rules.

verdict.reason: Verified end to end and could not refute it. (1) admin/src/app/router.tsx wraps every route in RequireAuth -> AppShell only; RequireAuth.tsx checks just `ready` and `admin` truthiness. A grep of all of admin/src for modulePermissions|canView|RequireModule|hasModule finds module checks ONLY in Sidebar.tsx:11-12 (nav visibility) and QuickActions.tsx:42 (button visibility) plus the sub-admin editor — there is no route-level guard component in the codebase. (2) LoginForm.tsx:41-42 sends every cold login to '/', and router.tsx:107 `{path:'*', element:<Navigate to="/" replace/>}` funnels any unknown URL to the dashboard as well, so landing there is unavoidable. (3) 'dashboard' is a real permission module (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:254 MODULE_KEYS, subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:37 label, navConfig.tsx:45 maps '/' to module 'dashboard'), so unchecking it carries a real expectation of enforcement. (4) Server side, firestore.rules isAdmin() is only role()=='super_admin'||'sub_admin' from claims, and `match /orders/{orderId} allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(...) || isAdmin())` has no can('orders','view'); the can()/canWrite() helpers are, per their own comment, scoped to direct-write collections, so reads were never module-gated (same for payments, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests). (5) dashboard/api/dashboard.ts genuinely queries collection(db,'orders') with getAggregateFromServer/sum plus a paged getDocs fallback, and DashboardPage renders useRecentOrders(5) with customer names and totals — these succeed for any sub_admin claim. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that list covers report/dashboard query scoping and adminModerateReview, which itself confirms reviews-only sub-admins are a provisioned persona) and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Two minor overstatements that do not sink the claim: the low-stock list derives from `products`, which is world-readable by design and therefore not a leak; and a sub-admin could equally type /orders directly, so the dashboard is the most visible instance of a broader missing-route-guard defect rather than a unique hole. Real, functional, and fixable (module-aware route guard, ideally plus can(module,'view') on the order/payment read rules).

findings.title: Adding the first variant to an existing simple product wipes its stock to zero
findings.detail: Save flips `hasVariants` to true as soon as one row carries a colour/size (line 200 → api/products.ts:138). Each new variant is built with `stock: prev?.stock ?? 0` (line 252); `prev` is looked up by the generated variant id, which cannot exist yet, so every new variant starts at 0. The product's existing top-level `stock` (set by Inventory / CSV import) is neither carried over nor cleared — it is simply ignored from then on, because every reader keys off hasVariants: web/src/components/catalog/ProductDetail.tsx:210 (`stock = variant ? variant.stock : product.hasVariants ? 0 : product.stock`), admin totalStock (api/products.ts:29) and buildSkuRows (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:197-212). The reverse direction (variants → none) IS guarded with an explicit toast at line 201-204; this direction has no guard and no warning.
findings.failure_scenario: A published product has stock 50 and is selling. Admin edits it to add a Green/M variant with its own price and saves. Instantly the product list badge flips to "Out of stock", Inventory shows one SKU at 0, and the storefront shows "Currently out of stock" with Add-to-bag disabled — 50 units of real inventory become invisible until someone re-enters them in Inventory.
findings.fix: When hasVariants goes false→true, seed the first variant's stock from the product's existing `stock` (and zero the top-level field), or block the save with the same style of explicit warning used for the variants→none direction.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, not refuted. In ProductFormPage.tsx onSave, adding any colour/size row to a previously simple product sets hasVariants=true (line 200 → api/products.ts:122,138). Each new variant is built with stock: prev?.stock ?? 0 (line 252), and prev is looked up by a freshly generated id against existingRef.current.variants, which is empty for a simple product — so prev is always undefined and stock is 0. saveProduct's update path (api/products.ts:194-206) never writes or migrates the top-level stock, so the product's real stock (e.g. 50 from CSV import at :314 or from adminAdjustStock's update.stock) is silently orphaned. I looked for a compensating handler and found none: functions/src has no products/{id} write trigger; adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:87-101) reads variant stock only when hasVariants && variants.length > 0 and never falls back to p.stock. Every reader keys off hasVariants and therefore reports 0: admin totalStock (products.ts:29) driving the "Out of stock" badge (:39), buildSkuRows (inventory/api/inventory.ts:200-212), web ProductDetail.tsx:110-111 ("Currently out of stock", Add-to-bag disabled at :295), ListingView.tsx:25, app product.dart:87, dashboard.ts:265. The reverse conversion IS explicitly guarded with a toast (ProductFormPage.tsx:201-204), which shows the direction is deliberately protected — this direction has no guard, no warning, and no carry-over. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Real, functional, and fixable (carry existing product.stock into the first variant, or block/warn like the reverse direction).

findings.title: Product load has no error path — a failed read leaves the edit page on a spinner forever
findings.detail: `getProduct(routeId!).then((p) => { ... setLoading(false); })` has no `.catch`. `setLoading(false)` only runs inside the fulfilled branch. If `getDoc` rejects — offline, an expired token, or a rules denial — the promise rejects unhandled (console-only) and `loading` stays true, so the component returns the spinner block at lines 279-285 permanently. This only bites when the products cache is empty (`seed` null at line 77-79), i.e. a hard refresh or a deep link to /products/{id}, which is exactly the flaky-network case.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin pastes/bookmarks a product edit URL and loads it while the connection is dropping. The page shows a spinner and never resolves — no error message, no retry, no way back except the browser Back button; the console logs an unhandled rejection.
findings.fix: Add `.catch((e) => { toast.error('Could not load this product.'); setLoading(false); })` (and ideally render an inline retry) to the getProduct call.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by direct inspection. ProductFormPage.tsx:107-136 calls getProduct(routeId!).then(...) with no .catch/.finally, and setLoading(false) occurs exactly once in the file (line 133) inside the fulfilled branch — nothing else can clear `loading`, so the spinner early-return at lines 279-285 becomes permanent on a rejected read. getProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:79-82) is a bare `await getDoc` that does not swallow errors. There is no global safety net: no ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch/unhandledrejection handler anywhere in admin/src, and no persistent Firestore cache configured (no initializeFirestore/persistentLocalCache), so an offline getDoc rejects instead of falling back to disk. Reachability holds: /products/:id is a deep-linkable route (admin/src/app/router.tsx:66) and the seed cache is an in-memory Map (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts), so a hard refresh or pasted URL yields seed=null and loading=true. Not on the already-fixed list (that covers the auth listener, not this read) nor the known-intentional list. Two minor overstatements in the report that do not change the verdict: (a) a rules denial is not a realistic trigger since firestore.rules:50-51 allows product reads with App Check unenforced — the realistic trigger is network unavailability; (b) the admin shell/sidebar still renders, so navigation away is possible. The same missing-catch pattern also exists in CouponFormPage.tsx:87-90, corroborating it as an oversight. Fix is a straightforward .catch that toasts and clears loading (or a retry/error state).

findings.title: Every product mutation control is shown to view-only sub-admins, and the rules cannot separate create from delete
findings.detail: Nothing in features/products checks `modulePermissions` — grep for modulePermissions across admin/src hits only Sidebar.tsx:12 (which gates on `view` alone), QuickActions.tsx:42 and the sub-admin editor. So a sub-admin with products.view=true and create/edit/delete=false sees Import (line 160), + Add product (163), and the row menu's Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete (280-288). firebase/firestore.rules:52 gates the collection on `canWrite('products')` = `can(create) || can(edit) || can(delete)`, so every one of those writes is denied and the user only gets the generic catch-all toasts ("Could not delete X.", "Could not save the product.", ProductsListPage.tsx:122/133/143, ProductFormPage.tsx:273). Conversely, because canWrite collapses all three verbs (firestore.rules:31-33), a sub-admin granted only products.create can delete or archive any product — the server has no way to reject it.
findings.failure_scenario: A catalogue-viewer sub-admin opens Products, hits Delete on a product, confirms, and gets "Could not delete Amber Oud." with no explanation (looks like a bug, not a permission). Meanwhile a data-entry sub-admin granted only 'create' opens the same menu and successfully deletes a live product plus all its Storage images.
findings.fix: Gate the Import/Add/Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete controls on `modulePermissions.products.{create,edit,delete}`, surface permission-denied errors distinctly, and split the rules gate for /products/{id} into create/update/delete clauses instead of one canWrite().

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. (1) admin/src/features/products contains zero permission references (grep for usePermission/useAdminStore/authStore/admin?. across features/products, hooks, stores returns nothing), while QuickActions.tsx:42 shows the codebase's own correct pattern (gates on `create`) and Sidebar.tsx:12 gates only on `view` — so a products.view-only sub-admin legitimately reaches ProductsListPage and sees Import, + Add product, and the row menu's Edit/Duplicate/Archive/Delete, all unguarded. (2) firebase/firestore.rules has a single `match /products/{id} { allow write: if canWrite('products') }` with `canWrite(m) = can(m,'create') || can(m,'edit') || can(m,'delete')`, so those writes are denied for the viewer (surfacing only the generic catch-all toasts in ProductsListPage onDelete/onArchive/onDuplicate and ProductFormPage), and conversely a create-only sub-admin can update, archive, and delete any product. deleteProduct (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:44-50) also wipes products/{id} in Storage, and firebase/storage.rules:13 guards that with only isAdmin() — so the Storage-image half of the scenario holds too. Refutation attempts all failed: there is no server-side re-check (products are a direct-Firestore module; functions/src/catalog has no product save/delete callable, only inventory), no route-level module guard in admin/src/app/router.tsx, and the per-action permission model is real and enforced elsewhere (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts provisions modulePermissions; requireModule(req, module, action) is used with distinct 'create'/'edit'/'approve' verbs across orders, affiliate, notifications, customers, returns), so the granularity is a first-class product concept that the products module discards. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two imprecisions worth noting but which do not refute: the title says rules "cannot" separate the verbs — they can (split into allow create/update/delete), they simply don't; and the gap is systemic rather than products-specific, since canWrite is used identically for settings, content, categories, coupons, banners, flashSales, newArrivals, spinCampaigns and pincodes. That widens the fix rather than invalidating the finding.

findings.title: Duplicate copies the source product's stock and reuses its Storage folder, so deleting the original breaks the copy's images
findings.detail: `duplicateProduct` spreads the whole source doc (`...rest`, line 230) and only resets rating/soldCount/order/publish fields (lines 240-249). Two things ride along that should not: (a) `stock` and `variants[].stock` — the copy claims the original's physical inventory; (b) `images`, whose URLs point at `products/{sourceId}/gallery-*` in Storage (uploadProductImage, line 212). `deleteProduct` (line 44-50) deletes the doc and then calls `deleteStorageFolder('products/' + id)`, which recursively deletes every object under the ORIGINAL's prefix (lib/storage.ts:15-24) — including the objects the copy still references. The copy's `images[].url` then 404s on the list thumbnail, the edit form and the storefront gallery, and `variants[].sku` is duplicated too.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin duplicates "Amber Oud" (stock 40, 3 photos), edits the copy and publishes it — the storefront now offers 40 units that do not exist and will oversell. Later the admin deletes the original; the copy's product page and every product card render broken/blank images with no way to recover them.
findings.fix: In duplicateProduct, zero `stock` and each `variants[].stock`, and either re-upload the images under `products/{newId}/` or reference-count the folder before deleting it in deleteProduct.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Verified in /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:

1. Shared-Storage-folder bug is real and unmitigated. `uploadProductImage` (line 210-216) writes to `products/{productId}/gallery-...` and returns a `getDownloadURL` for that exact object. `duplicateProduct` (line 223-255) spreads `...rest` and never touches `images`, so the copy's `images[].url` point at objects under the SOURCE's prefix. `deleteProduct` (line 44-50) hard-deletes the doc and then calls `deleteStorageFolder('products/' + id)`, which (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/storage.ts:15-24) recursively `deleteObject`s every item under that prefix — including the ones the copy still references. Nothing re-uploads or rewrites the copy's URLs: ProductFormPage seeds `images` straight from the loaded doc (line 101/130) and `saveProduct` writes `values.images` verbatim (line 134), so opening/saving the copy does not migrate anything. No Cloud Function participates — grep of functions/src shows no product-write/delete trigger doing image copying, and no soft-delete path. The URLs simply 404 afterwards.

2. Stock ride-along is also real and reachable. `stock` and `variants[].stock` are copied. They are not fixable from the product form: `ProductFormValues` has no `stock` field, `saveProduct`'s `base` never writes top-level `stock`, and ProductFormPage deliberately preserves per-variant stock (`stock: prev?.stock ?? 0`, line 252, with the comment "per-variant stock/weight/visibility live in Inventory, not here"). Stock is authoritative at checkout — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:479/544/567 re-reads and decrements product/variant stock inside the txn — so a published copy really can sell inventory that does not exist. The only mitigation is that the copy is created as `status: 'draft'` and checkout rejects non-published products (checkout.ts:59), which merely delays the problem until the admin publishes the copy, exactly as the failure scenario states.

Both paths are reachable from the UI: ProductsListPage.tsx:129 (`deleteProduct`) and :139 (`duplicateProduct`). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. The duplicated `variants[].sku` is the weakest sub-point (SKU uniqueness isn't enforced anywhere I could find), but the images and stock issues stand on their own as functional, fixable defects.

findings.title: Variables screen can create variants/groups that nothing can ever use — only ids 'color' and 'size' are consumed
findings.detail: `onCreate` persists any variant the admin names: a direct-units variant or a group, with `id = unitId(name)` (VariablesTab.tsx:53-70), and `AddUnitsModal` happily saves units into it. But the ONLY consumer of `settings/variables` in the whole repo is the product form, which hardcodes the two ids it understands: `variables?.directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color')` and `variables?.groups.find(g => g.id === 'size')` (admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140), and writes only the `color`/`size` attribute keys (ProductFormPage.tsx:261). Grep confirms no other reader: web (`/home/h/barkath/web/src`), app (`/home/h/barkath/app/lib`) and functions never read `directUnits`/`groups` at all; the only other hits are the shared type and the seed. The seeded `material` group (scripts/seed.ts:168) is already unreachable data proving the point, and `GroupVariable.enabled` is written `true` at creation and never read or toggled anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Settings ▸ Variables ▸ Create variant, picks "Group (units inside)", types "Material", adds units Cotton/Linen/Silk, sees "Units saved". They then open a product to tag it as Cotton — the product form only renders Color and Size dropdowns, so Material never appears. The units sit in Firestore forever, unusable. Same for a colour variant named anything other than exactly "Color" (e.g. "Colour" → id `colour`): the swatches are saved but the product form's colour dropdown stays empty.
findings.fix: Either drive the product form's variant dropdowns off the whole `directUnits`+`groups` arrays (render one Select per variable, key attributes by variable id) and honour `GroupVariable.enabled`, or lock the Variables screen down to editing units inside the two supported variables and remove the free-form Create-variant flow.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 persists any admin-named direct variant or group (CreateVariantModal only blocks duplicate ids, and its own help text invites "Material"), and AddUnitsModal saves units into it with a "Units saved" toast. The sole consumer of settings/variables in the repo is ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140, which hardcodes d.id === 'color' and g.id === 'size', and writes only those two attribute keys (line 261), builds SKU/label from only those two (246, 249) and renders chips only for those two (445-446). Repo-wide grep: web/src, app/lib and functions/src contain zero references to directUnits/groups/attributes — customer surfaces show the pre-baked variant.label that admin composes from color+size names only; other hits are just packages/shared types, scripts/seed.ts and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts. The seeded 'material' group (seed.ts:168) is proof-by-example of unreachable data, and GroupVariable.enabled is written true and never read anywhere. No guard, fallback or server-side re-check exists (saveVariables is a plain setDoc merge). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. The path is the screen's primary CTA (Create variant defaults to kind='group'). The design prototype shows a Material group on Variables yet only Color/Size columns on the product form, which supports the gap rather than excusing it. Additional reachable variant of the same bug: confirmDelete permits deleting the color/size entries when no unit is in use, and recreating them under any other spelling ("Colour" -> id 'colour') silently leaves the product form's dropdowns empty. Fixable either by constraining the create flow to the supported axes or by rendering a column per configured variant/group. Confidence medium only because one could argue two-axis variants are intended product scope — but even then the free-form create flow is a dead control that persists permanently unusable data.

findings.title: category.productCount is written 0 on create and never maintained — web home shows "0 products" for every admin-created category
findings.detail: `saveCategory` writes `productCount: 0` on create and never touches it again (there is no update path, no CF trigger, and `fanOutCategoryTint` doesn't touch it). The admin list papers over this by computing a live aggregation (CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42) and falling back to the stored value only on failure. The web home tile reads the stored field directly: `web/src/components/home/CategoryCard.tsx:35` renders `{category.productCount === 1 ? '1 product' : `${category.productCount ?? 0} products`}`. The Flutter app already worked around it — `app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63` literally comments "the stored `category.productCount` is never maintained by any Cloud Function (it's always 0)" and derives counts client-side. Only the seed masks it (scripts/seed.ts:293 hardcodes 3).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates category "Prayer Mats", publishes 12 products into it. Admin's Categories list shows "12". The web home page tile for Prayer Mats shows "0 products" forever. Even the seeded categories drift: Perfumes permanently reads "3 products" no matter how many are added or deleted.
findings.fix: Either stop writing/reading the denormalised field (drop it from the create payload and make web derive the count like the app does), or maintain it — increment/decrement in the product create/delete/category-reassign paths (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts) the same way `soldCount` is maintained.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:94 writes productCount:0 only on create; the update branch spreads `base` which omits the field, and setCategoryVisibility/updateSubCategories/fanOutCategoryTint never touch it. A grep of every write to the `categories` collection across admin/src, functions/src and scripts shows the only writers are those five calls plus the seed — functions/src has zero references to productCount and no Firestore trigger or scheduled sweep on categories. The consumer has no compute-on-read fallback: web/src/components/home/CategoryCard.tsx:35 renders the stored value directly and is live on the shop home (web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:99, top-4 tiles), so every admin-created category shows "0 products" permanently and seeded ones are frozen at 3. Admin's own list only hides it via a live aggregation (CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42, stored value used only as ?? fallback at line 124), and app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63 documents the same bug and works around it client-side. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Extra evidence the claim missed: the same rot is visible inside the admin panel for sub-categories — SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:83 create subs with productCount:0, and SubCategoriesPage.tsx:131 renders {s.productCount ?? 0} raw with no aggregation (countSubCategoryProducts is used only for the delete guard at line 61), so that column is permanently 0. Fixable either by maintaining the denormalized field on product create/update/delete or by deriving counts on the web side as app and admin-list already do.

findings.title: Tint fan-out writes to `products` — denied for a categories-only sub-admin, and its failure is reported as "Could not save the category" after the category already saved
findings.detail: `fanOutCategoryTint` batch-updates `products/*` documents. firestore.rules:53-55 gates `products` writes on `canWrite('products')`, while the categories screens are gated on `canWrite('categories')` (rules line 49) — two independent module keys in MODULE_KEYS. In `CategoryFormPage.onSave` (CategoryFormPage.tsx:159-170) the fan-out runs inside the same try block *after* `saveCategory` has already committed, and the catch emits the blanket `toast.error('Could not save the category.')` without navigating. Nothing is rolled back and `initialTint` is never updated, so every retry re-enters the same failing path.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose permission matrix has Categories(edit) but not Products opens Perfumes, changes the tint, clicks Save changes. The category document IS updated (new tint on the category tile) but the batch on products throws PERMISSION_DENIED; the operator sees "Could not save the category.", stays on the form, and clicks Save again — same error, forever. Products keep the old tint, so product cards and the category tile disagree. Same misleading message hits a super-admin whenever the fan-out fails midway (>400 products = multiple batches; batch 2 failing leaves half the products on the old tint and reports a total failure).
findings.fix: Run the fan-out only when the caller has products-write permission (or move it to a Cloud Function that checks the categories module and writes with admin credentials), and separate the toasts: report "Category saved, but product tints could not be updated" instead of "Could not save the category", and navigate/refresh `initialTint` so the retry is idempotent.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. Verified: firestore.rules:49 gates categories on canWrite('categories') while :50-57 gates products on canWrite('products'); MODULE_KEYS (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:253) treats them as independent, and SubAdminFormPage.toggleModule lets an operator enable Categories without Products, so the state is configurable. admin/src/app/router.tsx has no per-route module guard whatsoever (only RequireAuth), and Sidebar.tsx:12 surfaces Categories on categories.view, so the form and its unconditional Save button are reachable. No server-side fallback exists: there are zero Firestore triggers in functions/src, and functions/src/index.ts:15 explicitly states the categoryTint fan-out is a client-side batch by design. The field is live, not dead: web/src/components/product/ProductCard.tsx:37,72 renders product.categoryTint and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:83 snapshots it onto order lines. Code path confirmed at CategoryFormPage.tsx:159-170 — saveCategory commits, then fanOutCategoryTint runs in the same try, and one catch emits the blanket 'Could not save the category.' with no navigate; initialTint is only assigned in the mount effect (line 65) behind seededRef, so it never refreshes and every retry re-enters the failing branch. The 400-doc sequential loop in categories.ts:117-121 has no rollback, so a super-admin hitting a mid-loop failure gets half-migrated products plus a total-failure message. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.

findings.title: Adjust stock can only be changed ±1 per click — there is no numeric entry, and it is the only way to set stock at all
findings.detail: The Adjust column renders only two buttons calling `bump(r.key, r.stock, -1)` / `bump(..., +1)` (lines 149-157); the delta is a read-only <span> (line 152), not an input. There is no other path to set stock: the product form has no stock field, saveProduct writes `stock: 0` on create (products.ts:172) and never touches root stock on edit, and only the CSV importer can seed a non-zero stock (products.ts:314). So every unit of a newly created product must be clicked in one at a time, each click a separate setState + re-render of the whole (unpaginated) SKU table.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates 'Kashmiri Saffron 5g' and receives 500 units. To record it they must click the + button 500 times on /inventory/adjust; there is no way to type 500, no way to type an absolute target count, and the click storm re-renders every SKU row each time.
findings.fix: Replace the stepper span with a numeric input bound to the delta (accepting negatives), keeping the ± buttons as convenience, and optionally offer a 'set to' absolute mode that computes the delta client-side.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. AdjustStockPage.tsx:149-157 renders only two ±1 buttons; the delta is a read-only <span> (line 152) and `bump` (line 37) adds a hardcoded step of ±1 — there is no numeric or absolute-value entry anywhere on the page. I verified there is no alternative write path: saveProduct writes `stock: 0` on create (products.ts:174) and its edit branch never updates root `stock`; ProductFormPage explicitly preserves variant stock (`stock: prev?.stock ?? 0`, line 252) with a comment that stock 'lives in Inventory, not here'; InventoryListPage only reads stock and its row menu just links back to /inventory/adjust; ProductsListPage/FilterPage only filter on it. The CSV importer is not an escape hatch — importProducts always calls newProductId() and batch.set()s a new draft doc, so it can seed stock only for newly created products, never update an existing one. The backend is not the limit either: adminAdjustStock (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts) validates `delta: z.number().int()` and accepts any magnitude, so this is purely a UI gap and trivially fixable with a numeric input. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers adminAdjustStock's before/after return, a different issue) nor the known-intentional list. It is a usability/data-entry defect rather than data corruption, but since it is the only way to set stock for any product not created via CSV, recording a 500-unit intake genuinely requires 500 clicks.

findings.title: Order detail shows no totals or payment card at all — every money field on the order is unread by admin
findings.detail: The detail grid renders exactly four cards: Items (line 187), Shipment·AWB (215), Timeline (241) and Customer (263). Nothing on the screen renders subtotalPaise, discountPaise, spinRewardPaise, walletUsedPaise, deliveryPaise, codSurchargePaise, taxPaise, totalPaise, amountPaidPaise, appliedCoupon, paymentMethod, paymentStatus, razorpayPaymentId, cancellationReason or placedAt. A grep of the whole admin app (`totalPaise`) finds it only in the orders LIST (OrdersListPage.tsx:152), the customer profile and the reports/dashboard aggregates — never on the order it belongs to. The module even exports a ready-made `paymentPill(order)` helper (api/orders.ts:62) that is imported only by OrdersListPage. Meanwhile the web customer sees a full breakdown (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:177).
findings.failure_scenario: A customer phones about order #BRK-48219: 'I was charged ₹1,299 but the coupon should have taken ₹300 off and ₹200 came from my wallet.' The admin opens /orders/<id> and sees only per-line amounts — no subtotal, no discount, no coupon code, no wallet used, no amount actually paid, and no indication of whether the payment was captured, is COD, or was refunded. There is no way to reconcile the order against what the server computed, which is the whole point of the screen.
findings.fix: Add a Totals card (subtotal, discount + coupon code, wallet used, delivery, COD surcharge, GST, total, amount paid) and a Payment card (method, status pill via the existing paymentPill(), razorpayPaymentId, cancellation reason when cancelled), all read straight off the order document so the displayed numbers are the server-computed ones.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. OrderDetailPage.tsx (328 lines, the only order-detail component) renders exactly four cards — Items, Shipment·AWB, Timeline, Customer — and no money summary. Grep over all of admin/src returns ZERO hits for subtotalPaise, walletUsedPaise, spinRewardPaise, amountPaidPaise, discountPaise, deliveryPaise, taxPaise, appliedCoupon, razorpayPaymentId and cancellationReason; totalPaise appears only in the orders list, dashboard, customer profile and reports aggregates; paymentPill (api/orders.ts:62) is imported only by OrdersListPage.tsx:17. The fields are live data — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:353-363,585 writes walletUsedPaise and web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:163 shows the customer a full breakdown — so admin is the only surface blind to them. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and trivially fixable from the already-loaded order doc. Two mitigations shave severity but do not refute: (1) the Invoice button generates an HTML invoice (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:50-56) containing Subtotal/Discount/Delivery/COD/GST/Total plus 'Payment: method · status' — but in a separate tab, and still missing wallet used, amount paid, spin reward and the coupon code; (2) PaymentsListPage shows amountPaise/method/status and links Payments→order, but not the reverse and with no breakdown. The design prototype also lacks a totals card, so this is an inherited gap rather than a deliberate omission. Confidence is medium rather than high only because the invoice path covers part of the reconciliation story; the wallet/coupon/amount-paid fields remain unreadable anywhere in admin, so the core defect stands.

findings.title: Cancel is a one-click, unconfirmed, reasonless action that refunds money and restocks inventory
findings.detail: 'Cancelled' is just another entry in the Update-status dropdown (rendered at line 163-171) and `onSetStatus` calls `changeOrderStatus({ orderId, status })` with no confirmation step and no `note`. That call routes to performCancellation (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts) which restocks every product, credits the customer wallet with amountPaidPaise, writes a wallet ledger row, cancels affiliate commissions and releases the coupon — all irreversible (cancelled has no outgoing transitions, enums.ts:56). The `note` parameter exists in the admin API type (api/orders.ts:110) and in the CF schema (status.ts:28) but no caller ever supplies it, so cancellationReason is always the literal fallback 'Cancelled by admin' (status.ts:74). That string is displayed to the customer (app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:295). The codebase already has a ConfirmDialog component used by sub-admin suspend and affiliate allocation.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin means to click 'Packed' but hits 'Cancelled' one row below: the order is instantly cancelled, ₹1,299 is credited to the customer's wallet, stock is restored and the affiliate's commission is reversed, with no confirm prompt and no undo. The customer's app shows the cancellation reason as 'Cancelled by admin' with no explanation, and the admin can never record why it was cancelled.
findings.fix: Route 'Cancelled' through a ConfirmDialog that requires a typed/selected reason and pass it as `note` to changeOrderStatus so it lands in cancellationReason and the timeline note.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact verifies. OrderDetailPage.tsx:166 wires the dropdown item straight to onSetStatus, which at line 88 calls changeOrderStatus({orderId, status}) with no confirmation and no note — I read the whole file; there is no modal or window.confirm anywhere in it. 'Cancelled' sits directly adjacent to 'Packed'/'Shipped' in the menu because ORDER_STATUS_TRANSITIONS lists them as siblings (packing: ['packed','cancelled'], packed: ['shipped','cancelled']), so the misclick scenario is concrete. The `note` parameter is provably dead: grep for changeOrderStatus across admin/ yields only the import, the one call site, and the definition, so status.ts:74's `reason: note ?? 'Cancelled by admin'` always takes the fallback, which cancel.ts:230 persists to cancellationReason and app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:295 shows to the customer. The consequences are irreversible and monetary: cancel.ts restocks, credits the wallet plus a walletTransactions ledger row, flips pending commissions to 'cancelled' and decrements affiliate.pendingBalancePaise, releases the coupon, and marks payments/{orderId} refunded — and cancelled has no outgoing transitions in either the CF TRANSITIONS map or enums.ts. Refutation attempts all fail: the server-side check only validates that the transition is legal (a misclick satisfies it), permissions don't discriminate since requireModule(req,'orders','edit') is the same permission used to mark an order Packed, and the path is the only status UI so it is plainly reachable. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. The fix is trivial and already idiomatic here — ConfirmDialog exists at admin/src/components/ui/ConfirmDialog.tsx and is used in nine less-consequential places (sub-admin suspend, affiliate allocation, spinner/content delete), and the note plumbing is already present end-to-end and just needs a reason input.

findings.title: The Orders list streams the entire orders collection with a live listener and no limit
findings.detail: `useOrdersList` attaches `onSnapshot(query(collection(db,'orders'), orderBy('placedAt','desc')))` with no `limit()` and no date window, while the page renders only 10 rows at a time (PAGE = 10, OrdersListPage.tsx:22). Every order document now embeds its full `items` array (checkout.ts:617-626), so each doc is several KB. The same hook is also imported by the Payments screen (PaymentsListPage.tsx:15,23) purely to build a shortId lookup map, doubling the exposure. The tab counts and the pending count are computed client-side over the whole array (countByTab, api/orders.ts:94).
findings.failure_scenario: After a year at ~200 orders/day the admin opens /orders (or /payments) and the browser downloads ~70k order documents including every line item on first paint, then holds them all in memory with a live listener for the whole session — multi-second blank table, heavy read billing, and a re-render of the full list on every single order that changes anywhere in the store.
findings.fix: Bound the listener (e.g. limit(200) plus cursor pagination, or a date-window query), and derive tab counts from a server-maintained counter or a per-tab count query instead of the full collection.

verdict.reason: Verified and confirmed. admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:18-22 attaches onSnapshot over collection('orders') with orderBy('placedAt','desc') and no limit/where/cursor, while OrdersListPage renders PAGE=10 rows. useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:99-124) materializes every doc into a module-level cache that survives unmount, and admin/src/lib/firebase.ts uses plain getFirestore with no persistent local cache, so each fresh session re-downloads and re-bills the whole collection. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:617-627 confirms the full items array is embedded on each order doc, none of which the list view uses. No archival/TTL job exists for orders in functions/src, and firestore.rules:68-70 permits admins to read the whole collection, so nothing truncates it server-side. The already-fixed 'Reports/Dashboard queries were scoped' item is a different path: dashboard.ts:77,211,448 do carry limit(), orders.ts does not. Also not on the known-intentional list and not unreachable. One detail of the claim is wrong but immaterial: PaymentsListPage does not double the exposure, because both screens share the same ORDERS_KEY cache entry and therefore one listener; it still pulls every order doc just to build a shortId map, since the Payment type (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:130-137) carries no shortId. The fix is non-trivial (tab counts, pending count, search and CSV export all scan the full array, so it needs a bounded window plus aggregate counts), but it is a real, fixable scalability defect.

findings.title: No route-level permission gate: any sub-admin can read every customer's PII at /customers, because rules allow any admin to read the whole customers collection
findings.detail: `/customers` and `/customers/:id` sit under `RequireAuth` only (RequireAuth.tsx checks a signed-in active admin, nothing else). Module permissions are applied purely cosmetically, in Sidebar.tsx:11-12 and dashboard QuickActions. firestore.rules:139 is `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(userId) || isAdmin())`, and `isAdmin()` is just `role == 'super_admin' || role == 'sub_admin'` (rules:12) — no module check. So the hiding is client-side only with no server enforcement.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only reviews.view types /customers in the address bar. The nav item is hidden but the route renders: they get the full live list of every customer's name, phone, email, wallet balance and blocked status, and can open /customers/<uid> and click 'Export data' to download the whole customer document (addresses, bank accounts, cart) as JSON.
findings.fix: Add a permission guard element around the module routes (e.g. `<RequireModule module="customers" action="view">`) redirecting to /, and tighten the rule to `can('customers','view')` for the non-owner branch of the customers read.

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute. (1) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/app/router.tsx nests every route, including /customers and /customers/:id, under a single <RequireAuth/> + <AppShell/> pair with no per-route guard or loader. (2) /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx only waits for hydration and redirects when no admin is loaded — no module check. (3) A full grep of admin/src for modulePermissions shows only three functional consumers: Sidebar.tsx:12 (hides nav), QuickActions.tsx:42 (hides dashboard buttons), AccountDialogs.tsx:51 — i.e. purely cosmetic hiding. CustomersListPage.tsx and CustomerProfilePage.tsx contain zero permission checks, and CustomerProfilePage.tsx:98 onExportData serialises the entire customer doc to JSON unconditionally. (4) Server side does not re-check: firebase/firestore.rules:148 is `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isOwner(userId) || isAdmin())`, and isAdmin() (rules:12) is just role()=='super_admin' || role()=='sub_admin'. Crucially the rules DO define a per-module gate can(module,action)/canWrite(module) (rules:29-42, added per its own comment so a dashboard-only sub-admin could not rewrite the GST rate), but grepping shows can('...') is used exclusively on allow-write lines — can(module,'view') is never used anywhere, so no admin read is module-gated. (5) The scenario is reachable: emptyModulePermissions() in admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:59 starts new sub-admins all-off, so a reviews-only sub-admin has customers.view=false yet still satisfies isAdmin(). (6) Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (which covers adminModerateReview for reviews-only sub-admins, not read gating) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL (App Check non-enforcement is a separate issue from isAdmin() lacking a module check). Only inaccuracies in the report are cosmetic: the rules line is 148 not 139, and RequireAuth does not itself verify 'active' status (that lives in the auth store). Systemic note: orders, supportTickets, reviews and the customer subcollections have the same isAdmin()-only read, but customers is the worst instance given the PII plus one-click full-document export.

findings.title: Approving a return refunds the customer but never settles payments/{orderId} — the Payments page keeps showing "Success" for the full amount, and 'partial_refund' is a status nothing ever writes
findings.detail: `adminDecideReturn` (approve path) increments `orders.refundedPaise`, flips `orders.paymentStatus` to 'refunded' only on a full auto-wallet refund, credits the wallet and reverses commissions — but there is no `db.doc('payments/'+orderId)` reference anywhere in returns/decisions.ts (grep for `payments` across functions/src returns only checkout.ts:698/931 and cancel.ts:79). So the payment row keeps `status:'captured'` and the original `amountPaise`. Separately, `paymentStatusPill` (admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:25) renders a "Part refund" badge for `partial_refund`, but no writer in functions/, seed.ts or admin ever assigns `partial_refund` to a payment doc — the branch is dead.
findings.failure_scenario: Customer returns one ₹900 item from a ₹3,000 captured Razorpay order; admin approves it in Refunds and ₹900 lands in the customer's wallet. /payments still shows that txn as green "Success · ₹3,000.00" and the "GST invoices" export still bills ₹3,000, so the exported GST figure overstates net revenue by every refund ever approved. A fully-returned order likewise never shows "Refunded" on the Payments screen.
findings.fix: In the approve branch, also `tx.update(db.doc('payments/'+r.orderId), { status: amount >= receivedPaise ? 'refunded' : 'partial_refund', refundedPaise: FieldValue.increment(amount), updatedAt: now })` (guarded on the doc existing, as cancel.ts does).

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. functions/src/returns/decisions.ts (adminApproveOrderRequest, tx.update at :157) updates orders.refundedPaise/paymentStatus, credits the wallet and reverses commissions, but never touches payments/{orderId}. Grep across functions/src, admin/src, web, scripts shows the only payments/ writers are checkout.ts:698, checkout.ts:931 and cancel.ts:79 — and firestore.rules:82-85 makes payments CF-only-write, so there is no client fallback. There are no Firestore triggers in functions/src and no sweep touches payments, so nothing settles it asynchronously. findings.failure_scenario: An accountant clicks "GST invoices" at quarter end expecting a GSTR-1-shaped file, opens barkath-gst-invoices.csv and finds rows like `pay_R8x2K3,BK-1042,Online,Razorpay,captured,129900` — no date, no tax, no GSTIN — so nothing in it can be filed, and (per finding 1) every COD sale is missing.

findings.title: No route-level or rules-level permission gate on Payments — any sub-admin can read the whole payments ledger by typing the URL
findings.detail: Sidebar.tsx:12 hides nav items unless `admin.modulePermissions[item.module].view === true`, but router.tsx registers `{ path: '/payments', element: <PaymentsListPage /> }` behind `RequireAuth` only, and RequireAuth (features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx) checks nothing but `admin != null`. Server side, firebase/firestore.rules:82-84 is `match /payments/{id} { allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (isAdmin() || isOwner(resource.data.customerId)); }` — `isAdmin()` is true for ANY sub_admin regardless of `modulePermissions.payments.view`, unlike the `can(module, action)` helper used for the directly-written collections. Nothing else in this module (page, hook, query) checks the permission either.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin created with only `banner.view` (Sidebar shows them just Banner) types /payments into the address bar. The route renders, the unfiltered `payments` listener succeeds because the rules only check isAdmin(), and they see every transaction, gateway reference and amount in the store — plus both CSV exports.
findings.fix: Add a module guard component around the permission-scoped routes (redirect to / when `modulePermissions[module].view` is false) AND tighten the rule to `allow read: if hasAppCheck() && (can('payments','view') || isOwner(resource.data.customerId))`.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. admin/src/app/router.tsx:77 registers /payments under RequireAuth + AppShell only; RequireAuth.tsx checks nothing but `ready` and `admin != null`, and AppShell.tsx is pure layout. No RequireModule/usePermission/403 guard exists anywhere in admin/src — grepping `modulePermissions` yields only Sidebar.tsx:12 (nav-link filtering), QuickActions (button visibility), SubAdminFormPage/AccountDialogs (editing perms), and a type. PaymentsListPage and features/payments/api/payments.ts do no permission check: usePaymentsList() opens an unfiltered live listener on collection('payments') ordered by createdAt. Server-side, firebase/firestore.rules:82-84 gates payments reads on `isAdmin()`, which (rules line 11) reads only the role custom claim — it never consults admins/{uid}, so neither `status` nor `modulePermissions.payments.view` is considered. The `can()`/`canWrite()` helpers that DO read modulePermissions are applied exclusively to write rules, and functions/src/_lib/guards.ts requireModule() is only ever invoked with create/edit/approve, never 'view' — so there is no read-side module gate on any surface. `payments` is a real MODULE_KEY and `view` a real PERMISSION_ACTION in packages/shared/src/enums.ts, so an intended gate is genuinely unenforced. Nothing on the ALREADY-FIXED list covers route or read gating, and nothing on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list applies (App Check is moot here — hasAppCheck() returns true and the rule would pass on isAdmin() regardless). The stated failure scenario reproduces exactly. One scoping caveat: the same read exposure applies to orders, orderRequests, commissions, withdrawalRequests and every other admin route, so the correct fix is a shared route guard plus a can(module,'view') read rule rather than a payments-only patch; payments is simply the highest-severity instance.

findings.title: placeOrder ignores settings/paymentGateway — the COD toggle, COD max amount and the online/wallet switches are client-side only
findings.detail: PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:41-48 writes `codEnabled`, `codMaxAmountPaise`, `walletEnabled`, `onlinePaymentEnabled` to `settings/paymentGateway`. Both clients honour them (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158, app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-345). But `placeOrder` only loads `settings/delivery` and `settings/tax` (checkout.ts:431-432) — grep for `paymentGateway` across functions/src returns nothing. The paymentMethod from the request is accepted verbatim and written straight onto the order and the payment doc.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin turns off "Cash on delivery" (or sets COD max to ₹2,000) and saves; the toggle reports success. A customer on an already-loaded app screen, or any direct callable invocation, places a ₹40,000 COD order — placeOrder accepts it, stock is decremented and a `payments/…` row with method `cod` appears on the Payments screen for an amount the admin explicitly banned.
findings.fix: Load `settings/paymentGateway` in placeOrder and reject with failed-precondition when the chosen method is disabled or when a COD order exceeds a non-zero `codMaxAmountPaise`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real server-side validation gap. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:430-432 loads only settings/delivery and settings/tax; a grep for `settings/` across functions/src shows the only other reads are settings/affiliate and settings/returns — settings/paymentGateway is never read anywhere in the backend, and codEnabled/codMaxAmountPaise/onlinePaymentEnabled appear nowhere in functions/src. paymentMethod is only shape-checked by the zod enum (line 393) and then passed verbatim into effectivePaymentMethod (line 611), the order doc (line 649), the payments/{orderId} doc (line 726) and the callable response (line 790); useWallet is similarly honoured with no walletEnabled check. The setting is live, not dead: written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:41-48, typed in packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:44-52, seeded in scripts/seed.ts:184 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:114, and enforced purely client-side in web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158-174 and app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-345. No rules-level substitute exists because the order is written by the callable with admin credentials, so a stale client screen or a direct callable invocation can place a COD order that the admin disabled or that exceeds codMaxAmountPaise, decrementing stock and creating a payments row. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list and not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list; it also contradicts the project rule that money decisions are server-authoritative. One small correction to the claim's wording: settings/delivery.codSurchargePaise IS read for COD at line 349, but that is pricing, not the availability/limit gate, so the defect stands.

findings.title: Approve confirmation and drawer hardcode "credited to the wallet" — the module never reads settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet
findings.detail: The confirm dialog body (lines 218-226) states "{amount} will be credited to {customer}'s {refundTargetLabel(refundMethod)}" and, because requestReturnOrReplacement always writes refundMethod:'wallet' (functions/src/returns/requests.ts:133), refundTargetLabel() returns the hardcoded string 'Normal wallet' (api/returns.ts:50) for every pending request. The drawer repeats it unconditionally: "Approving credits this amount to the customer's wallet immediately and can't be undone." (lines 332-336), and the list 'To' column (line 178) shows 'Normal wallet' for every pending row. None of this is true when settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet is false — decisions.ts:107-108 then sets toWallet=false and rewrites refundMethod to 'gateway'. There is no import of the settings doc anywhere under admin/src/features/returns (the only reader/writer of autoRefundToWallet in admin is StorefrontTab.tsx:279-296), so the screen cannot know which mode it is in. The destination is also display-only: the module offers no control to pick wallet vs original method, even though the design prototype shows both ('Normal wallet' and 'Original' rows in designs/Barakath Admin Prototype.dc.html).
findings.failure_scenario: Auto-refund is OFF. Admin opens #RP-000123, the drawer says 'Approving credits this amount to the customer's wallet immediately', the confirm says '₹899 will be credited to Aisha Khan's Normal wallet'. Admin clicks 'Approve & refund' believing the customer is paid, and sees the success toast 'Refund approved for #RP-000123'. Aisha's wallet balance is unchanged and no walletTransactions entry exists; the admin only discovers the discrepancy if the customer complains.
findings.fix: Subscribe to settings/returns in the returns module; when autoRefundToWallet is false, change the destination label to 'Original payment method (manual payout)' and the confirm/drawer copy to 'This approves the return but does NOT move money — you must pay ₹X back manually.'

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute the core. admin/src/features/returns/ contains only api/returns.ts and routes/ReturnsListPage.tsx, and neither reads settings/returns — the sole admin reader/writer of autoRefundToWallet is settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx (ReturnsCard, persisted toggle, defaults true). functions/src/returns/requests.ts:133 hardcodes refundMethod:'wallet' on every request, so refundTargetLabel() yields 'Normal wallet' for every pending row, while decisions.ts:28,107-108 sets toWallet=false and rewrites refundMethod to 'gateway' when the toggle is off — no wallet write, no walletTransactions doc, refundedAt null. The drawer text (ReturnsListPage.tsx:332-336) and confirm body (218-226) render before the call, so nothing server-side can correct them; and the CF explicitly returns {amount, creditedToWallet} (decisions.ts:182) which approveReturn() (api/returns.ts:60-63, typed Promise<void>) discards before doApprove fires an unconditional 'Refund approved' toast. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers the CF honouring autoRefundToWallet, which it does — the admin UI was never wired) and not known-intentional. Confidence is medium, not high, because the claim ignores real post-hoc mitigation: after approval the 'To'/Destination cell flips to 'Original' and the drawer timeline renders the CF's statusHistory note 'Approved — refund to be paid out manually (auto-refund to wallet is off).', so the discrepancy is discoverable without a customer complaint. Two sub-claims should be dropped: the 'mock-data' category is a mislabel (unconditional copy, not fixture data), and the missing wallet-vs-original picker is a design-parity wish, not a defect (destination is policy, not per-request). What remains is a genuine, cheaply fixable defect: pre-decision copy and the success toast assert money movement that does not occur when autoRefundToWallet is false.

findings.title: Approving with auto-refund OFF tells the customer their money was refunded — app and order doc both claim a refund that never happened
findings.detail: decisions.ts:157-167 increments order.refundedPaise by the full amount unconditionally, even in the manual-payout branch where no wallet credit and no gateway refund occurred (the Razorpay refund API is never called anywhere in functions/src). Downstream, app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:209 defines `wasRefunded => refundedPaise > 0 || paymentStatus == 'refunded'`, and the app's return card at app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:529-531 branches purely on request status: `if (r.isApproved) _refundLine('$refund refunded to your wallet', brandGreen, check_circle)`. ReturnRequest.isApproved is `status == 'approved' || status == 'completed'` (return_request.dart:36) — it never looks at refundedAt or refundMethod. So the moment the admin approves, the customer app shows a green tick and the words '₹899 refunded to your wallet' even though the wallet was untouched, and the admin reports screen counts the order as refunded (admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:233,248).
findings.failure_scenario: Auto-refund is OFF. Admin approves the return. The customer opens the order in the app, sees '₹899 refunded to your wallet' with a green check, opens the Wallet screen and finds the balance unchanged and no refund entry in the ledger — a direct contradiction between two screens of the same app, triggered by an admin click.
findings.fix: Only increment order.refundedPaise (and only claim a refund to the customer) when money actually moved; in the manual branch write a distinct marker (e.g. refundPendingPaise / statusHistory-driven copy) and make the app's refund line read refundedAt/refundMethod so it says 'Approved — refund will be paid to your original payment method' until settlement.

verdict.reason: Confirmed reachable and real. With settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet=false (a live admin toggle written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/StorefrontTab.tsx:296,329), functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:107-108,139 approves the return with toWallet=false, refundedAt=null, refundMethod='gateway', no walletTransactions entry, and no gateway refund (no Razorpay refund API exists in functions/src). The app then asserts the opposite: app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:529-531 renders a green check plus '<amount> refunded to your wallet' branching only on ReturnRequest.isApproved (return_request.dart:36 = status approved|completed), and :568 hardcodes the timeline label 'Approved · refund issued'. The model parses refundMethod (return_request.dart:30,59) but grep shows no screen reads it, and refundedAt is not parsed at all — so the data needed to render truthfully is present and ignored. The customer sees 'refunded to your wallet' on the order screen and an unchanged balance/empty ledger on the Wallet screen, triggered by one admin click. Not covered by the already-fixed item ('autoRefundToWallet is honoured' — the CF does honour it; the app does not) nor by the intentional list. Two sub-claims are overstated but do not rescue it: (a) the CF's statusHistory note 'Approved — refund to be paid out manually' IS rendered in small secondary text below the green line (order_detail_screen.dart:610), so the card self-contradicts rather than being silently wrong; (b) order.refundedPaise -> Order.wasRefunded (order.dart:209) only surfaces at orders_screen.dart:288 inside an `status == cancelled` branch, unreachable for returns, and admin reports.ts:248 would flag the order as refunded anyway via refundedOrderIds() (reports.ts:232) regardless of the increment — so the decisions.ts:158 increment itself is defensible as the documented over-refund guard. The genuine, fixable defect is the app's unconditional 'refunded to your wallet' copy (and 'refund issued' timeline label) on an approval that moved no money.

findings.title: Category restriction is written but ignored by the web (and mostly by the app) offer list, advertising discounts the server refuses
findings.detail: The admin writes `applicableCategories` as category slugs (CouponFormPage.tsx:328-343, api/coupons.ts:130) and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:114-119 correctly restricts the discount to matching `product.categorySlug` lines. The web mirror does not: `PromoCoupon` (offers.ts:31-47) does not even declare applicableCategories, `promoDiscount` (lines 50-79) computes the discount over the whole subtotal, and `listAvailableOffers` (lines 141-158) prints the sub-line as 'On any order' / 'Min cart X'. The app (app/lib/features/checkout/data/offers.dart:107-111) only hints at the restriction when exactly one category is selected and still computes the discount over the full subtotal.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates SWEETS20 (20% off, capped Rs.200) and taps only the 'Sweets' chip. A customer with a bag of only Dry Fruits opens checkout: the offers list shows 'SWEETS20 - 20% off, up to Rs.200 - On any order' as a qualifying offer. Tapping it applies it, then the applyCoupon re-validation returns failed-precondition ('This coupon does not apply to the items in your bag'), the coupon is torn back off and an error toast fires. For a mixed bag the headline discount is inflated versus what the server actually grants.
findings.fix: Add `applicableCategories` to PromoCoupon and mirror `discountableSubtotal` in offers.ts (and offers.dart), filtering cart lines by categorySlug before computing the discount and the qualifies/shortfall values.

verdict.reason: Verified real. `applicableCategories` is written by the admin as category slugs (admin/src/features/coupons/api/coupons.ts saveCoupon, chips keyed by c.slug in CouponFormPage.tsx) and is enforced server-side by discountableSubtotal in functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:134-140, used by both computeCouponDiscount (lines 205-208, 235-238) and autoBestOffer (line ~305), throwing failed-precondition 'This coupon does not apply to the items in your bag.' A repo-wide grep for `applicableCategories` hits only packages/shared, admin, functions and scripts/seed.ts — nothing under web/. web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts PromoCoupon (31-48) omits the field, promoDiscount ignores it, and listAvailableOffers (141-161) labels such a coupon 'On any order'/'Min cart X' with qualifies = subtotal >= min, so checkout/page.tsx:567-577 renders an active Apply button. Tapping it calls applyOffer, the revalidation effect (page.tsx:190-213) calls applyCoupon, the server rejects, the coupon is torn back off and an error toast fires — a reachable, user-visible cross-surface mismatch, not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED entry (which is server-side only) or the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Two caveats that reduce severity but not validity: (1) the 'inflated discount' half is largely unreachable for admin-authored promos because saveCoupon always writes maxUsesPerUser: 1 and offers.ts:70 forces promoDiscount to 0, so bestOfferForCart never auto-applies them; (2) personal/spin coupons never carry applicableCategories (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:159-171), so only the promo list path misleads. Fix is feasible: declare the field on PromoCoupon, show 'Sweets only' in the sub-line and stop marking/auto-applying it as qualifying (the web cart line lacks categorySlug — web/src/lib/cart.ts:7-17 — so full client-side filtering needs the slug added to CartLine).

findings.title: Free-shipping coupons are auto-applied on web regardless of target users, expiry or min cart
findings.detail: `bestOfferForCart` calls `consider(c.code, promoDiscount(...), c.discountType === 'free_shipping')` and `consider` treats `waiveDelivery` alone as 'better' (line 200: `const better = discountPaise > 0 || waiveDelivery;`). All of promoDiscount's rejection rules — targetUsers != 'all' (line 53), validUntil past (line 58), min cart not met (line 60), usage limit exhausted (line 64) — only zero the *discount*, which is already 0 for free shipping. The waiveDelivery flag survives every one of them, so the coupon wins auto-apply. Because the server code-entry path also never checks targetUsers, the subsequent applyCoupon re-validation accepts it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates FREESHIPAFF, discount type 'Free shipping', Target users = 'Affiliates'. Every ordinary web customer who opens checkout sees the toast 'Best offer applied - FREESHIPAFF' and gets delivery waived; placeOrder honours it because computeCouponDiscount only checks active/status/validity, not targetUsers. The admin's targeting is completely bypassed and the store eats the delivery cost on every order. The same path also lets a min-cart-Rs.999 free-shipping coupon apply to a Rs.100 cart.
findings.fix: Have promoDiscount return an eligibility flag (or a `{discountPaise, waiveDelivery}` pair) so the targetUsers / validity / minimum / usage rejections zero waiveDelivery too, and pass that flag into `consider`.

verdict.reason: Real, reachable defect. In web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts, bestOfferForCart (line 206) computes waiveDelivery straight off the raw coupon doc, independently of promoDiscount, and consider() (line 200: `discountPaise > 0 || waiveDelivery`) treats that flag alone as sufficient to auto-apply. Every promoDiscount rejection (targetUsers != 'all' L53, autoApply false L54, validFrom/validUntil L56-59, minCartValuePaise L61, maxUsesTotal L64) only zeroes the discount, which is already 0 for free_shipping, so all of them are bypassed for that coupon class. listAvailableOffers (L141-148) pre-filters those same conditions correctly, showing the omission is unintended rather than by design. Reachability verified end-to-end: checkout page.tsx:162 queries `coupons` with only where('status','==','active') and no targetUsers filter; firestore.rules:74 lets any signed-in user read /coupons/{id}; the admin form genuinely writes both discountType 'free_shipping' (CouponFormPage.tsx:30/161) and targetUsers 'affiliates' (COUPON_TARGETS, enums.ts:81). Server does not rescue it: the auto-applied code is sent as couponCode (page.tsx:315) so placeOrder (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:454) uses computeCouponDiscount, whose promo branch (L171-223) checks active/status/validity/minCart/usage/firstOrderOnly/categories but never targetUsers, then sets waiveDelivery=true (L212) and summarise zeroes delivery (L367). Notably the server's own autoBestOffer DOES check targetUsers (L283), which is why the gap only shows on the explicit-code path. Two sub-claims are overstated but do not refute: the min-cart and expired cases are caught by computeCouponDiscount and cleared by the client revalidation effect (page.tsx:185-217), degrading to a spurious 'Best offer applied' toast then an error. The targetUsers bypass is unmitigated anywhere and yields placed orders with delivery waived. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.

findings.title: Banner edit swallows a failed load: getBanner has no catch, leaving a permanent spinner and an unhandled rejection
findings.detail: `getBanner(routeId!).then((b) => { ... setLoading(false); })` (lines 60-74) has no `.catch()`. `loading` is initialised to `!isNew && !seed` (line 39), and the component early-returns a full-page `<Spinner>` while loading (lines 137-143). If the read rejects — permission-denied for a sub-admin without banner view, offline, or a rules deploy blip — `setLoading(false)` never runs, no toast fires, and the promise rejection is unhandled. findings.title: Broadcast is recorded as fully 'sent' with full reach BEFORE the fan-out runs, and the fan-out is unbounded

findings.title: Deep-link product picker offers draft / archived / hidden products, and the app opens them without a status check

verdict.reason:

Admin picker is unfiltered. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/notifications/routes/NotificationCreatePage.tsx:47-54 builds productOptions from `useProductsList()` and categoryOptions from `useCategories()`. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:22-26 is `query(collection(db,'products'), orderBy('createdAt','desc'))` — no status/visibility/deletedAt filter, and its own doc comment says "All products (every status)". /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:25-29 is `orderBy('order','asc')` with no visibility filter. findings.title: Approve & pay never checks the confirmed balance — admin can pay out more than the affiliate has earned
findings.detail: `requestWithdrawal` validates `amountPaise > confirmed` only at REQUEST time (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:41). `approveWithdrawal` re-reads the customer inside the transaction but never re-validates: line 108 takes `amount = w.requestedAmountPaise`, line 115 does `Math.max(0, confirmed - amount)` (silently flooring at zero) and line 117 adds the FULL `amount` to `withdrawnBalancePaise`. The admin UI likewise renders the Confirmed column (admin/src/features/affiliate/routes/AffiliateListPage.tsx:170) purely as decoration — `doApprove` (line 99) never compares `confirmedOf(w)` with `w.requestedAmountPaise`, and the Approve button is never disabled. Meanwhile `reverseCommissionsForRefund` (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:150-176) legitimately decrements `confirmedBalancePaise` while a request is open.
findings.failure_scenario: Affiliate requests ₹5,000 while confirmed = ₹5,000. Before the admin acts, a referred order is returned and approved, clawing back ₹2,000 → confirmed = ₹3,000. Admin opens /affiliate, sees Confirmed ₹3,000 next to Amount ₹5,000, clicks Approve & pay. The CF succeeds: confirmed floors to 0, withdrawnBalancePaise jumps by ₹5,000, the request is marked paid, and the admin manually transfers ₹5,000 for ₹3,000 of earned commission. Ledger totals (confirmed + withdrawn vs lifetime) are now permanently inconsistent and nothing flags it.
findings.fix: In the transaction, throw `failed-precondition` when `amount > (aff.confirmedBalancePaise ?? 0)`, and mirror it client-side by disabling Approve (with an inline 'insufficient confirmed balance' hint) when `confirmedOf(w) < w.requestedAmountPaise`.

The admin UI confirms the cosmetic-only claim: confirmedOf(w) is rendered at AffiliateListPage.tsx:170 but doApprove (line 99) never compares it to requestedAmountPaise, the Approve button (line 175) is never disabled, and the dialog text at lines 201-204 asserts a deduction from confirmed commission that does not fully happen. findings.title: Approve dialog promises the gross amount; the affiliate is only ever paid netPayoutPaise
findings.detail: `requestWithdrawal` computes `processingFeePaise` from settings/affiliate and stores `netPayoutPaise = amount - fee` on the request (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:49-68). The web withdraw screen shows the affiliate 'You receive {net}' (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:186) and the activity list debits `w.netPayoutPaise` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/page.tsx:80). The admin panel never reads `netPayoutPaise` or `processingFeePaise` anywhere: the table Amount column (line 172) and the confirm dialog body ('{X} will be transferred to … bank', line 196) both use `requestedAmountPaise`. Since payouts are executed by hand off exactly this number, the admin transfers the gross figure.
findings.failure_scenario: Ops sets settings/affiliate.processingFeeType='percent', processingFeeValue=2. Affiliate withdraws ₹10,000 → request stores processingFee ₹200, netPayout ₹9,800, and the affiliate's app says 'You receive ₹9,800'. Admin sees only '₹10,000 will be transferred to Ramesh's HDFC ••4821' and NEFTs ₹10,000 — the business silently eats the fee on every payout, and the admin's screen and the customer's screen disagree about the paid amount.
findings.fix: Show `processingFeePaise` and `netPayoutPaise` in the withdrawals table and make the confirm dialog read 'Transfer {netPayoutPaise} (₹{requested} less {fee} fee)'.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:49-51,67-68 stores processingFeePaise and netPayoutPaise on each withdrawalRequests doc; web (web/src/app/(shop)/account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:41-42,183-187) and the Flutter app (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_repository.dart:25-33) both compute and promise the affiliate the NET amount. A repo-wide grep for netPayoutPaise|processingFeePaise returns zero hits under admin/: AffiliateListPage.tsx renders requestedAmountPaise in the Amount cell (line 172), the approve dialog body ('{X} will be transferred to …bank', line 196) and the 'pending payout' header stat (line 54). Since affiliate payouts are deliberately manual, that dialog number is exactly what ops transfers, so with a non-zero fee the business overpays and admin/customer screens disagree. Refutation attempts failed: no server-side recompute at approval (approveWithdrawal, functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:107,116-118, deducts the gross from confirmedBalancePaise — consistent with the affiliate absorbing the fee, which makes the admin copy the outlier), no other admin route shows net, field is not dead, and it is not on the fixed/intentional lists. Mitigation (hence medium, not high): the fee is 0 in both seed.ts:207-208 and bootstrap-real.ts:116 and admin has no UI writing settings/affiliate (useAffiliate() in admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25-27 is unused), so the defect is latent until ops sets a non-zero fee in the settings doc that web/app already read live. Fix is a one-liner: show netPayoutPaise (and the fee) in the table and dialog.

findings.title: Moderating one review overwrites the product's whole rating aggregate — wiping admin-entered / seeded ratings
findings.detail: adminModerateReview recomputes products/{id}.rating + ratingCount purely from the `reviews` docs whose status == 'approved' (lines 70-91) and writes the result on EVERY decision, including a reject of a review that was only 'pending' and therefore never contributed to the aggregate. But the admin product form deliberately lets an operator type rating/ratingCount by hand (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:405-431, saved at :217-222 with the explicit comment that it must not clobber moderation), and the seeder ships every product with rating 4 + i/10 and ratingCount 10 + i*3 (/home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:382-383) with zero review documents behind them. The first moderation action on any product therefore replaces that number with the count of real approved review docs — usually 0 or 1. Nothing warns the admin; the confirm dialog only says the review 'will go live … and update its rating'.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Reviews ▸ Pending, sees one spam review on 'Amber Oud EDP' (product card currently shows 4.0 ★ · 10 ratings) and clicks Reject → confirm.
