The CF flips the review to rejected AND writes ratingCount: 0, rating: 0 on products/1. On web (ProductCard.tsx:119, ProductDetail.tsx:193) and in the app (product_details_screen.dart:188/329) the gate is `ratingCount > 0`, so the product's star rating disappears from every card and the PDP. Rejecting a spam review silently deleted the product's rating, and there is no undo in the admin UI.
findings.fix: Only touch the aggregate when the review actually enters or leaves the 'approved' set (skip the product write entirely for pending→rejected), and either drop the manual rating/ratingCount inputs from the product form or seed real review docs so the recompute cannot destroy a number no review can reproduce.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real. functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts:82-91 writes products/{id}.rating + ratingCount from the approved-review set on any status change where the product exists, with no guard for decisions that don't alter that set. A pending->rejected transition (the review never contributed) therefore overwrites the aggregate with 0/0 when no approved review docs exist. Manual aggregates are a supported production feature, not just seed data: admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:401-431 exposes the fields and :213-222 deliberately omits them from the patch unless edited so as not to clobber moderation, i.e. the two are meant to coexist. The admin contract explicitly expects a reject to 'take back the rating it contributed, if any' (admin/src/features/reviews/api/reviews.ts:45) and the reject confirm dialog never mentions the product rating. firestore.rules:122-141 makes reviews client-immutable and customer-created as 'pending', so this CF is the only writer besides the product form; nothing in web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared compensates. Customer impact confirmed: ratingCount > 0 gates the star display in web ProductCard.tsx:119, ProductDetail.tsx:193, wishlist page:116 and app product_card.dart:94, product_details_screen.dart:188/329. Claim overstates slightly ('EVERY decision' — line 61 no-ops an identical status, and the write is skipped when the product doc is missing), and moderation.ts:9-11 arguably intends to override hand-edited ratings, which is why confidence is medium rather than high; but that intent cannot justify a destructive write on a transition that changes nothing. Minimal fix: skip the product update when neither the previous nor the new status is 'approved'.

findings.title: An approved or rejected review can never be re-moderated — no un-publish path exists anywhere
findings.detail: The Action cell renders Approve/Reject buttons only when `tab === 'pending'`; on the Approved and Rejected tabs it renders a static <Badge> (lines 148-157). There is no row menu, no bulk action and no detail view. firestore.rules:123 sets `allow update, delete: if false` on reviews for every client including admins, so the only possible path is the adminModerateReview callable — which does support flipping either direction (Payload accepts 'approved'|'rejected' and the stored-status guard at moderation.ts:59 only no-ops on an identical status). The UI simply never offers it, so a decision is irreversible from the admin panel.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin approves a 5-star review, then a customer complains it contains a competitor's phone number / abusive text. The admin opens Reviews ▸ Approved, finds the review, and there is nothing to click — only a green 'Published' badge. The review stays live on the web PDP and the app forever; the only remedy is a manual Firestore console edit (which rules also forbid from the client SDK).
findings.fix: Render 'Unpublish' on the Approved tab (call adminModerateReview with status 'rejected') and 'Publish' on the Rejected tab, reusing the existing confirm dialogs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. ReviewsListPage.tsx:147-158 renders Approve/Reject only when tab === 'pending'; the Approved and Rejected tabs render a static Badge with no row menu, bulk action or detail route, and a grep of admin/src shows this page (router.tsx:85, /reviews) is the ONLY reviews surface in the panel. firestore.rules:141 sets `allow update, delete: if false` on /reviews/{id} with an explicit comment that no client, admin included, may update a review directly, so no fallback path exists. Meanwhile the backend fully supports the reverse flip: functions/src/reviews/moderation.ts Payload accepts 'approved'|'rejected' with no 'must be pending' precondition, the guard at line 61 only no-ops on an identical stored status, and line 87 explicitly handles rejecting a previously-approved review by dropping it from the approved set and recomputing products/{id}.rating + ratingCount (audit action review.rejected included). So an abusive review that was approved can never be taken down from the admin panel even though the callable and rules were designed for it. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry only covers the callable existing for reviews-only sub-admins) and not on the known-intentional list. Fix is UI-only: offer the opposite action on the Approved/Rejected tabs reusing the existing setApprove/setReject confirm dialogs.

findings.title: Firestore read errors are captured but never rendered — a failed report is shown as a confident all-zero report, and Export CSV happily exports the zeros
findings.detail: `useFetchCollection` does populate `error` on failure (`reports.ts:119-122` — `.catch` sets `{ data: <stale>, loading: false, error }`). `ReportsPage` destructures only `.data` and `.loading` (l.63-68); `orders.error`, `products.error`, `customers.error` and `requests.error` are never referenced anywhere in the file (grep for `\.error` in ReportsPage returns only Tailwind tone strings). Because the catch also sets `loading: false`, the page leaves the loading state and renders `formatMoneyCompact(0)` = '₹0', Orders 0, New customers 0, Refund rate 0%, twelve 2%-high bars and 'No sales data yet'. The Export CSV button is gated only on `loading` (l.101), so it is enabled and writes a report full of zeros to disk. Every other admin screen surfaces failures via toast (e.g. admin/src/features/reviews/routes/ReviewsListPage.tsx:59); Reports swallows them.
findings.failure_scenario: A Firestore rules deploy briefly denies the `customers` collection query (or the network drops mid-fetch). The admin opens Reports, sees 'Total revenue ₹0 / Orders 0 / New customers 0 / Refund rate 0%' with no warning at all, clicks Export CSV, and mails the finance team a report stating the business did zero revenue for the last 12 months. Nothing on screen distinguishes this from a genuinely empty shop.
findings.fix: Surface the union of the four `error` values: render an inline error banner with a Retry that clears `e.started`/re-issues the fetch, and add `|| hasError` to the Export CSV `disabled` prop so a failed snapshot can never be exported.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. reports.ts:119-122 sets {data: <stale/empty>, loading: false, error} on a failed getDocs; ReportsPage.tsx:63-68 destructures only .data/.loading and never references .error (grep finds only Tailwind `tone === 'error'` strings). Because loading flips to false, KpiStat drops its `—` placeholder and renders formatMoneyCompact(0) = ₹0, Orders 0, New customers 0, Refund rate 0%, twelve 2%-height bars (computeTrend line 355) and 'No sales data yet' — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty shop. Export CSV (line 101) is gated only on `loading`, so it is enabled and downloadReportCsv writes `Total revenue,0.00` to a file. The path is reachable: firestore.rules:157 gates customers/orders/products/orderRequests reads on the isAdmin() custom claim, so an unpropagated token, a rules deploy, or an offline getDocs rejects. No error boundary, unhandledrejection handler, or global toast exists in admin/src to catch it. The codebase's own convention is the opposite: ReturnsListPage.tsx:105-114 renders read errors with the comment 'Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state' and special-cases permission-denied, and BannerListPage:77, SpinnerListPage, CouponsListPage, SubAdminListPage, NotificationsListPage and the settings tabs all consume `error` — useFetchCollection was deliberately given the same CollectionState shape. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Only imprecision: the cited precedent ReviewsListPage.tsx:59 is a mutation toast, not a read-error surface; the real precedent is ReturnsListPage.tsx:105.

findings.title: No Affiliate settings screen exists — settings/affiliate is read by 3 surfaces but writable by nobody
findings.detail: `useAffiliate()` (settings.ts:25-27) is exported and never imported anywhere in admin/src — grep for `useAffiliate` returns only its own definition. `SETTINGS_TABS` (components/SettingsShell.tsx:22-28) lists only variables / delivery / gateway / storefront / support, and `SettingsPage.VALID` (routes/SettingsPage.tsx:13) has no 'affiliate' entry, so there is no route, chip or form for it. Yet `settings/affiliate` is read live by: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 (`minWithdrawalPaise`, `processingFeeType`, `processingFeeValue`, `processingFeeMinPaise` — used at requests.ts:50-52 to compute the payout fee and reject under-minimum withdrawals), functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:41-42 (`defaultCommissionRate`), web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:55 + web/src/lib/affiliate.ts:40 (fee schedule shown to the customer), and app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_repository.dart:97. scripts/seed.ts:210-220 seeds all nine fields, so the values exist and silently govern real payouts. `commissionClearanceDays`, `maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise`, `enabled` and `shareMessage` are additionally never read by anything (functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11 explicitly says clearance happens at delivery instead).
findings.failure_scenario: An admin needs to raise the affiliate withdrawal minimum from ₹500 to ₹2,000 and add a 2% processing fee. They open Settings, cycle every tab (Variables, Delivery & tax, Payment gateway, Storefront, Support, plus the content-page chips) and find nothing for affiliates. The only way to change the value the requestWithdrawal callable enforces is to hand-edit the Firestore document in the Firebase console.
findings.fix: Add an 'affiliate' tab to SETTINGS_TABS + SettingsPage.VALID with a form over settings/affiliate (minWithdrawalPaise, processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise, defaultCommissionRate as a percent input converted to a fraction, enabled), wired to a saveAffiliate() using the existing useAffiliate() hook. Drop commissionClearanceDays/maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise/shareMessage from the schema, or make a surface read them.

verdict.reason: Verified in full. admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 exports useAffiliate() and nothing in admin/src imports it; there is no saveAffiliate writer, no 'affiliate' entry in SettingsShell.tsx:9-28 SETTINGS_TABS/SettingsTabId, and none in SettingsPage.tsx:13 VALID, so ?tab=affiliate silently falls back to Variables. admin/src/features/affiliate/ has only list + allocate pages, and grep for minWithdrawal|processingFee|defaultCommissionRate across admin/src returns zero hits — no surface writes settings/affiliate anywhere in the repo. The doc is nevertheless authoritative for money: functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 loads minWithdrawalPaise/processingFeeType/processingFeeValue/processingFeeMinPaise and uses them to compute processingFeePaise/netPayoutPaise and to hard-reject under-minimum withdrawals; functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:41-42 falls back to defaultCommissionRate; web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:55, web/src/lib/affiliate.ts and app/lib/.../affiliate_repository.dart:97 display the fee schedule; scripts/seed.ts:200-211 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:116 seed all nine fields. firebase/firestore.rules:56 already allows admin writes to settings/{docId}, so the gap is purely a missing admin form and is trivially fixable. The claim is not on the already-fixed list, and the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL note about manual affiliate payouts covers the absence of a bank-transfer API, not the absence of any way to configure the payout minimum/fee. Sub-claim also verified: commissionClearanceDays, maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise and shareMessage are referenced only by the shared type, the seeds, and a comment in functions/src/affiliate/commissions.ts:11.

findings.title: Turning off "Online payment" in admin does not disable online payment in the Flutter app
findings.detail: The admin writes `onlinePaymentEnabled` (PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:47) as an independent boolean. web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:161 honours it directly (`gateway?.onlinePaymentEnabled ?? true`). The app does not: app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:320 computes `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled || s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty;` — an OR against the key field. Because the Key ID field on the same admin card is almost always populated (scripts/seed.ts:185 writes 'rzp_test_XXXXXXXXXXXX'), the `|| razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty` branch keeps online payment permanently on in the app.
findings.failure_scenario: Razorpay goes down, so the admin opens Payment gateway and toggles 'Online payment (UPI / cards / net-banking)' off, then saves. Web checkout correctly hides the online option. App customers still see and select 'Pay online', get pushed into the Razorpay sheet, and their orders fail — the admin's kill-switch appears to have worked because they only checked the website.
findings.fix: Change app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:320 to `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled;` (matching web), or remove razorpayKeyId from the admin form entirely so the app has nothing to OR against.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real cross-surface defect. Admin writes onlinePaymentEnabled as an independent boolean (admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:47, toggle at :136). Web honours it alone: web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:238 `const onlineEnabled = gateway?.onlinePaymentEnabled ?? true;`. The Flutter app instead ORs it with the key field: app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:424 `final onlineEnabled = s.onlinePaymentEnabled || s.razorpayKeyId.isNotEmpty;` — so with a populated Key ID (scripts/seed.ts:185 'rzp_test_XXXXXXXXXXXX', and any live install) the admin kill-switch is inert in the app: the Razorpay tile still renders (line 490) and the draft can even be auto-switched TO 'razorpay' (lines 440-442). No rescue elsewhere: app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:208-209 parses both fields correctly with the intended `?? true` web-mirroring default (comment at 204-206 says exactly that), and there is no server-side re-check — grep for onlinePaymentEnabled/codEnabled/paymentGateway across functions/src returns nothing and functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:418 accepts z.enum(['cod','razorpay']) without consulting settings/paymentGateway. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists (Razorpay test-mode note concerns money flow, not the availability toggle). Only defect in the report is stale line numbers: the app expression is at :424 (claim said :320) and the web read at :238 (claim said :161); the code text quoted is exact. Fixable in one line (use && or drop the OR).

findings.title: COD / wallet / online toggles and the COD cap are enforced only in the clients — placeOrder ignores settings/paymentGateway
findings.detail: The four controls on this card (`codEnabled` :110, `codMaxAmountPaise` :121, `walletEnabled` :133, `onlinePaymentEnabled` :136) are written to settings/paymentGateway and then read *only* by the two clients (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:158-174, app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:317-321) to hide radio buttons. `grep -rn "paymentGateway" functions/src` returns zero hits: functions/src/orders/checkout.ts never loads the doc. Its placeOrder schema is `paymentMethod: z.enum(['cod','razorpay'])` (checkout.ts:393) and `summarise()` (checkout.ts:335-363) reads only settings/delivery and settings/tax; it adds `delivery.codSurchargePaise` for any 'cod' order (checkout.ts:349) and accepts any `useWallet` amount. So none of the four settings is a real switch.
findings.failure_scenario: COD fraud spikes, so the admin turns 'Cash on delivery' off and saves. Customers on an already-open app/web tab (their client still holds the previous settings snapshot for the life of the screen), or anyone calling the placeOrder callable directly, keep placing COD orders successfully — the server accepts them, prices in the COD surcharge, and they land in the Orders list as normal. The same applies to a ₹5,000 COD cap: a ₹40,000 COD order placed from a stale client is accepted.
findings.fix: Load settings/paymentGateway inside placeOrder and reject with failed-precondition when `paymentMethod === 'cod' && !codEnabled`, when `codMaxAmountPaise > 0 && subtotalPaise > codMaxAmountPaise`, when `paymentMethod === 'razorpay' && !onlinePaymentEnabled`, and when wallet is used while `walletEnabled === false`.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. functions/src/orders/checkout.ts reads only settings/delivery and settings/tax (lines 464-465); repo-wide grep for paymentGateway/codEnabled/codMaxAmountPaise/onlinePaymentEnabled across functions/src and firebase/*.rules returns zero hits (the sole walletEnabled hit is an unrelated affiliate field in functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:27). PlaceOrderSchema (checkout.ts:418) accepts paymentMethod 'cod' unconditionally and summarise() (checkout.ts:354, 369) prices in delivery.codSurchargePaise for any COD order with no enable/cap check. The doc is written by admin/src/features/settings/routes/PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:44-47 and read only by the two clients for UI gating (web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:46 + web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:235-251; app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:187,202-208), both defaulting absent flags to true. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and placeOrder already reads two other settings docs so the fix is the established pattern. One minor inaccuracy that does not change the verdict: useWallet is a boolean and the server reads the real wallet balance inside the transaction, so wallet spend is capped at the true balance — only the walletEnabled toggle itself is unenforced. The COD-off and COD-cap bypasses are real and reachable by any authenticated customer calling placeOrder directly or from a stale client tab.

findings.title: "Create variant" builds variants no screen can ever use — only ids 'color' and 'size' are consumed
findings.detail: The Variables tab lets an admin create arbitrary direct-unit variants and groups (VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 → variables.ts:38-52 writes settings/variables.directUnits/groups) and add units to each. But settings/variables has exactly one consumer in the entire monorepo: admin/src/features/products/routes/ProductFormPage.tsx:139-141, which hardcodes `directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color')` and `groups.find(g => g.id === 'size')`. Nothing in web/src, app/lib or functions/src reads settings/variables at all (verified by grep for 'settings/variables' and 'directUnits'). The product form persists only those two keys — `attributes: { ...r.attrs, color, size }` (ProductFormPage.tsx:261). The seeded 'material' group (scripts/seed.ts:167-176) with Cotton/Silk/Linen is already dead for exactly this reason. CreateVariantModal also blocks a duplicate id (CreateVariantModal.tsx:37), so the only usable variants are the two that already exist.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin clicks 'Create variant', picks 'Group (units inside)', names it 'Fragrance strength', adds units Light/Medium/Strong and saves — every step shows a success toast and the group renders in the Variables tab. They then open Products → New and find only Color and Size dropdowns; the new variant is unusable and invisible to web, app and every order/invoice.
findings.fix: Either drive the product form's variant axes off settings/variables generically (iterate directUnits + enabled groups instead of hardcoding 'color'/'size'), or restrict the Variables tab to editing the two supported variants and remove the Create-variant flow.

verdict.reason: Verified as a genuine dead control. VariablesTab.tsx:53-71 lets an admin create an arbitrarily-named direct-unit variant or group and persists it to settings/variables (admin/src/features/settings/api/variables.ts:43-46), and firestore.rules:56 permits the write, so the flow completes with success toasts and the new variant renders in the tab. But settings/variables has exactly one consumer in the monorepo — ProductFormPage.tsx:139-140 — which hardcodes directUnits.find(d => d.id === 'color') and groups.find(g => g.id === 'size'); the variant-row table renders only two MiniSelects (lines 468, 472) with no map over groups, and the save writes only those two keys (line 261, where r.attrs is mere carry-over since line 49 strips color/size on load). Grep confirms no reader of settings/variables, directUnits, or variant attributes anywhere in web/src, app/lib, functions/src or packages/shared runtime code; customer surfaces resolve variants by id/label/sku (e.g. app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:169-173). The seeded 'material' group (scripts/seed.ts:167-176 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts) is already inert, which is concrete evidence rather than a hypothetical. No guard, fallback, or server-side re-check mitigates it, and it is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. It is fixable either by rendering one column per enabled group in the product form or by constraining the Create-variant control. One narrowing nuance: the control is not entirely useless — a variant named exactly 'Color' or 'Size' produces the consumed ids, so it retains a recreate-after-delete purpose; that limits severity but does not refute the defect.

findings.title: GST rate is rounded to a whole percent on load, so any save of the Delivery & Tax tab silently rewrites a fractional rate
findings.detail: The form seeds the input with `setGstPercent(String(Math.round((t.gstRate ?? 0) * 100)))` (DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:57) and saves it back with `gstRate: (Number(gstPercent) || 0) / 100` (line 88). The round-trip is lossy for any non-integer percent — 0.125 → '13' → 0.13, 0.025 → '3' → 0.03. There is also no range validation: any number is accepted, so '18' typed as a fraction ('0.18') writes gstRate 0.0018 and '1800' writes 18. gstRate is consumed as a fraction by functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:351 (`Math.round(net * Number(tax.gstRate ?? 0))`), web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:119 and app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:210, so the value directly sets the tax charged on every order. Note that a single 'Save changes' button writes both settings/delivery and settings/tax (lines 77-97), so an unrelated edit triggers the rewrite.
findings.failure_scenario: GST is 12.5% (gstRate 0.125 in Firestore). The admin opens Delivery & tax only to change the standard delivery fee from ₹49 to ₹59. The GST field renders '13'. They click Save changes and the tax rate is silently rewritten to 0.13 — every subsequent order is taxed 13% instead of 12.5%, with nothing in the UI indicating a tax change was made.
findings.fix: Seed with the exact value (`String(+( (t.gstRate ?? 0) * 100 ).toFixed(2))`) instead of Math.round, and validate on save that the entered percent is a finite number in 0–100 before dividing by 100.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as a real, fixable defect. DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:57 seeds the GST field with Math.round(gstRate*100) while line 88 saves (Number(gstPercent)||0)/100, and the underlying Field component (admin/src/features/settings/components/fields.tsx) is a bare <input type="number" inputMode="decimal"> with no step/min/max and no onChange sanitiser — so the same form that persists 12.5 -> 0.125 will render it as '13' and rewrite it to 0.13 on any later save. The defect is reachable entirely through this one screen; no external writer is needed. No guard exists elsewhere: a repo-wide grep for gstRate finds only the shared type (unconstrained `number`), the 0.18 defaults in settings.ts/seed.ts/bootstrap-real.ts, and three consumers that use the stored fraction raw with no clamping or re-derivation (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:371 `Math.round(net * Number(tax.gstRate ?? 0))`, web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:119, app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:201/231). packages/shared/src/money.ts:58 inclusiveTaxPaise takes a percent but has zero call sites, so there is no alternate path that makes the rounding benign. The single 'Save changes' button does write settings/delivery and settings/tax together (lines 77-97), so an unrelated delivery-fee edit does trigger the tax rewrite. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderated by two facts: the checkout tax term only applies when gstEnabled && !pricesIncludeTax (defaults have pricesIncludeTax: true), and Indian GST slabs are usually whole percents — but 1.5% and 0.25% rates would be silently rewritten to 2% and 0%, and the missing range validation ('0.18' -> 0.0018, '1800' -> 1800%) is unguarded on every surface. Confidence medium rather than high only because of the real-world rarity of fractional GST rates, not because of any doubt about the mechanism.

findings.title: The subAdmin module permission is a dead toggle — granting it produces a nav item that always errors
findings.detail: The matrix exposes a "Sub Admin" toggle (MODULE_LABELS.subAdmin, subadmin.ts:55) and Sidebar.tsx:11-12 shows the nav entry whenever modulePermissions.subAdmin.view is true. But nothing honours that permission: firebase/firestore.rules:196-198 allows reading admins/{adminUid} only `if isSuperAdmin() || (role()=='sub_admin' && uid()==adminUid)`, so useAdminsList()'s collection query (subadmin.ts:19-21) is denied for every sub-admin; and all four callables (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:22, 52, 77, 102) use requireSuperAdmin, never requireModule(req,'subAdmin',…). No `requireModule` call anywhere in functions/src references 'subAdmin'.
findings.failure_scenario: A super admin turns on "Sub Admin" for a team-lead sub-admin and tells them to manage the team. The lead signs in, sees the Sub Admin nav item, clicks it and gets the permanent error row "Couldn’t load admins. Please try again." Clicking "+ Create admin" still renders the whole form; after filling name/email/password and every module toggle, Save produces "You don’t have permission to create this admin." The toggle can never do anything.
findings.fix: Either enforce the module server-side (rules: allow list on /admins if can('subAdmin','view'); callables: requireModule(req,'subAdmin', create|edit|delete) instead of requireSuperAdmin) or remove 'subAdmin' from MODULE_KEYS/the matrix and hide the nav item for non-super-admins.

verdict.reason: Every link in the claim checks out. `subAdmin` is a grantable toggle (SubAdminFormPage.tsx:210 maps all MODULE_KEYS with no filtering), and both client gates honour it: Sidebar.tsx:11-12 shows the nav item and RequireModule.tsx lets `/sub-admin` mount when `modulePermissions.subAdmin.view` is true. Nothing downstream honours it: firestore.rules admins block allows read only `if isSuperAdmin() || (role()=='sub_admin' && uid()==adminUid)`, which a collection list query (subadmin.ts:19-21) can never satisfy, so useAdminsList() is denied and SubAdminListPage.tsx:126 renders the permanent error row; and all four callables in functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts (lines 22, 52, 77, 102) begin with requireSuperAdmin, so create/update/suspend/delete throw permission-denied, which cfError renders verbatim as "You don't have permission to create this admin." requireModule exists (guards.ts:42) and is used for 7 other modules but never for 'subAdmin'. Greps across functions/, packages/shared/, web/ and app/ find 'subAdmin' only in enums.ts:272 (MODULE_KEYS) and the two admin UI sites — no other surface reads it, no server-side re-check, no fallback. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; the path is trivially reachable. Real, fixable dead-control defect: either gate the toggle/nav to super admins or teach the rules + callables to accept subAdmin module permissions.

findings.title: Permission/role changes never reach a live session - the auth store snapshots admins/{uid} once at boot
findings.detail: initAuthListener calls loadAdminDoc(uid) exactly once inside onAuthStateChanged and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot on admins/{uid}. Sidebar.tsx:12 and QuickActions.tsx:42 read modulePermissions from that frozen object. updateSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:52-73) changes role/modulePermissions and re-sets custom claims but does NOT call revokeRefreshTokens, so the client is never nudged to re-read.
findings.failure_scenario: A super admin revokes the 'Coupons' module from a sub-admin who is currently signed in. The sub-admin's sidebar keeps showing Coupons for the rest of their session; they open it, edit a coupon and hit Save, and only then get a 'You don't have permission' toast from the rules (can() reads the live doc). Conversely, granting a new module doesn't make the nav item appear until a hard reload, so the admin reports the grant 'didn't work'.
findings.fix: Replace the one-shot loadAdminDoc with an onSnapshot on admins/{uid} that updates the store (and signs the user out when status flips to 'suspended'), so nav and quick actions track permissions live.

verdict.reason: Verified in code and could not refute. admin/src/features/auth/stores/authStore.ts:28-52 does a one-shot getDoc via loadAdminDoc (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:54) inside onAuthStateChanged and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot/onIdTokenChanged/poll anywhere in admin/src for admins/{uid}, and initAuthListener is mounted once with [] deps in admin/src/app/providers.tsx:8. Sidebar.tsx:12 and QuickActions.tsx:42 are the only modulePermissions consumers and there is no route-level permission guard (RequireAuth only checks admin != null), so a revoked module stays clickable and a granted module stays invisible for the whole session until a hard reload. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:66-72 (updateSubAdmin) sets custom claims and updates the doc but never calls revokeRefreshTokens — unlike suspendSubAdmin (line 96), which does revoke + disable, so the security-critical suspension case IS handled but permission/role edits are not. That omission adds a real, non-cosmetic consequence the claim only hints at: demoting super_admin -> sub_admin leaves role:'super_admin' in the ID token for up to ~1h, and isSuperAdmin() short-circuits both can() in firebase/firestore.rules and requireSuperAdmin() in functions/src/_lib/guards.ts, so the demoted admin retains full super-admin write power (including self re-promotion) during that window. Mitigating context, hence medium confidence: server-side enforcement is live for module perms (rules can() and guards.ts:50 read the current admins doc), and module 'view' gating is already cosmetic because admin reads are gated only by isAdmin() — so the sidebar half is a UX/staleness defect rather than an access-control hole. Fix is trivial (swap getDoc for onSnapshot on admins/{uid}, and call revokeRefreshTokens in updateSubAdmin when role changes).

findings.title: Category performance silently swaps to lifetime unit counts and presents them under the same "%"
findings.detail: `if (totals.size === 0) { for (const p of products) bump(p.categoryId || p.categorySlug, p.soldCount ?? 0); }` — when the 90-day order aggregation yields nothing, the panel switches metric from 'revenue in paise over 90 days' to 'lifetime units sold from the current product catalogue', with no visual difference in the UI. `totals.size === 0` is true on every first paint (the `categoryOrders` query at line 225 is still in flight while `categoryPerformance` is called synchronously from render at DashboardPage.tsx:46), and stays true forever if that query errors — `categoryOrders.data ?? []` at line 237 swallows the error.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin opens the dashboard. For the first second the bars read 'Perfumes 100%, Dates 62%' from lifetime `soldCount`, then jump to completely different numbers when the order page-walk lands. If the 90-day order read fails (permission, missing index, timeout), the lifetime-units ranking stays on screen indefinitely and the admin makes a merchandising decision from a metric that ignores price, ignores the selected period, and excludes every unpublished product.
findings.fix: Thread the `categoryOrders` query state through instead of the module-level `categorySources` global: render a skeleton while `isLoading`, an error row on `isError`, and a genuine 'No sales in the last 90 days' empty state when the window really is empty. Delete the `soldCount` fallback — it is a different metric.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written (line drift only: the fallback is at dashboard.ts:353-357, not 348). The panel silently swaps metric from '90-day revenue in paise' to 'lifetime units sold from published products' with identical rendering. Verified: (1) DashboardPage.tsx:46 calls categoryPerformance synchronously from render and maps the rows unconditionally at 151-161 — no loading, empty, or error state for the category card, even though useLiveCollection exposes `loading` and it IS used for the recent-orders table at line 186; (2) dashboard.ts:244 does `categoryOrders.data ?? []`, so a failed 90-day order read is indistinguishable from 'no sales' and pins the fallback on screen forever; (3) useLiveCollection (firestoreCache.ts:99-124) returns data:[] while loading, and the products onSnapshot settles before the paged getDocs walk in forEachOrder, so the transient 'products loaded, orders pending' render really does paint soldCount-derived percentages that then jump; (4) the fallback reads products filtered by status=='published' (line 221), so it excludes unpublished SKUs and ignores price and the period — exactly the flaws the function's own doc comment at 303-314 says the soldCount roll-up was replaced for, and the error-swallowing contradicts the file's stated rule at 46-55 ('swallowing it turned a transient outage into a confidently-wrong KPI'). Single caller and single writer of categorySources (grep across admin/src); nothing in web/, app/, or functions/ compensates. Not on the already-fixed list (which covers soldCount increment/decrement only) nor the known-intentional list. Only inaccuracy in the report is the CATEGORY label 'mock-data' — this is real catalogue data used as the wrong metric, not fabricated data.

findings.title: Category performance reads only `order.items`, ignoring legacy orders whose line items live in the subcollection
findings.detail: `for (const it of o.items ?? [])` — the only line-item read. Orders written before the embedded-array migration carry their items solely in `orders/{id}/items`, which the shared type documents explicitly (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:42-47: "readers must fall back to it when this array is absent") and which the rules still expose (firebase/firestore.rules:71-75). Those orders contribute exactly 0 to every category bucket while still being counted in full by the revenue KPIs and the trend chart (which sum `totalPaise` off the order doc).
findings.failure_scenario: Any pre-migration order inside the 90-day window is invisible to the category split. Immediately after deploy, the dashboard shows Today's revenue ₹4.2L but a Category performance panel built from only the handful of new-format orders — so a category that drove most of the revenue reads near 0%. If every order in the window is legacy, `totals.size === 0` and the panel silently degrades to the `soldCount` fallback described above.
findings.fix: Fall back to `getDocs(collection(db, 'orders', o.id, 'items'))` when `o.items` is absent — or, better, source the split from a server-side rollup (see the perf finding) so the client never has to know about either shape.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: dashboard.ts:348 (`for (const it of o.items ?? [])`) is the only line-item read in categoryPerformance, and nothing upstream hydrates legacy lines. The orders are loaded by the `categoryOrders` queryFn in `useProducts` (dashboard.ts:225-237) as plain order docs; no `orders/{id}/items` read occurs anywhere in the dashboard feature. The legacy subcollection is unambiguously still live: admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35-45 falls back to it, functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:31-35 falls back to it, web/src/components/account/orders.ts:123,282 falls back to it, firestore.rules:71-75 still exposes it to admins, and no backfill/migration script exists in /home/h/barkath/scripts. OrderItem.category and lineTotalPaise exist, so the aggregation is right for embedded orders and simply blind to legacy ones — those orders still count in full toward the revenue KPIs and trend chart (both sum totalPaise off the order doc), so the panels disagree. CLAUDE.md makes both-path reading an architecture rule whose violation is a defect by definition. Mitigations exist but do not eliminate it: the `totals.size === 0` soldCount fallback only covers the all-legacy case, and normalising to top-category=100% hides rather than fixes skew in a mixed window. Fixability is real — unlike reports.ts:382-387 (which has the same omission but documents it as unavoidable inside a pure function), the dashboard's loader is async and can fetch the subcollection for orders lacking an embedded array. Confidence is medium, not high, only because the identical gap in reports.ts carries an explicit author comment accepting it, suggesting the aggregate surfaces treat this as a known tradeoff; it is not, however, on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists.

findings.title: Week-over-week orders delta compares an 8-day window against a 7-day window
findings.detail: `ordersThisWeek = countOrders([where('createdAt','>=',startOfDay(-7))])` is an open-ended window from midnight 7 days ago to *now*, i.e. 7 full days plus everything so far today = up to 8 calendar days. `ordersPrevWeek` (line 164) is `[startOfDay(-14), startOfDay(-7))` = exactly 7 full days. `pctChange` (line 172) then divides one by the other and the result is surfaced as '▲ X% this week' on the Total orders card (DashboardPage.tsx:81). The same asymmetry exists for the AOV windows at lines 165-168 ([-30, now) = 31 days vs [-60,-30) = 30 days), though the ratio partly cancels there.
findings.failure_scenario: The store takes exactly 100 orders every single day. `ordersThisWeek` = 700 + today's partial (say 50 by midday), `ordersPrevWeek` = 700. The card reports '▲ 7.1% this week' on a perfectly flat business, and the number drifts upward through the day, resetting at midnight. An admin tracking week-on-week growth is reading noise from the window definition.
findings.fix: Make the current window a closed 7 full days — `[startOfDay(-7), startOfDay(0))` — matching the baseline, or compare like-for-like partial windows (last 7 days ending now vs the 7 days ending exactly 7 days ago). Apply the same closure to the 30/60-day AOV windows.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts, ordersThisWeek is `where('createdAt','>=',startOfDay(-7))` with no upper bound (7 full days + today's elapsed portion), while ordersPrevWeek is the half-open `[startOfDay(-14), startOfDay(-7))` (exactly 7 full days). pctChange divides them and DashboardPage.tsx:81 renders it as '▲ X% this week', so a flat store shows a positive delta that grows through the day and resets at midnight (700+50 vs 700 = +7.1%). No guard, clamp, or server-side recomputation exists; pctChange only null-checks `before > 0`. Not handled elsewhere: ordersWeekDeltaPct appears only in dashboard.ts and DashboardPage.tsx (grep across web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared finds nothing). Not intentional: the interface doc comment in the same file says 'Orders in the last 7 days vs the 7 before that', which the code does not implement, and the sibling analytics screen /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts computeKpis deliberately uses equal-length windows (spanMs mirrored to build prevFrom, comparing [from, now) vs [prevFrom, from)) — so Dashboard and Reports will disagree on the same metric and the correct idiom already exists in-repo. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry covers query scoping and cancelled-order exclusion, which are handled correctly here) nor the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Reachable for any store with orders in the prior week. Severity is moderate — misleading KPI, no data corruption — and the AOV pair at lines using -30/-60 shares the asymmetry though the ratio largely cancels it. Fix is a one-liner: add `where('createdAt','<',startOfDay(0))` to the current window (or shift to [-6, now) vs [-13, -6)).

findings.title: Category performance panel has no loading, empty or error state — it renders as a blank box
findings.detail: `{cats.map((c) => …)}` is the entire body of the panel. `categoryPerformance` returns `[]` whenever there are no categories and no products (fresh store, or `useCategories`/`products:published` still loading, or either listener errored — `useLiveCollection` keeps `data: []` and only records the error on the snapshot, which the dashboard never reads). There is no `.length === 0` branch, unlike Recent orders (line 192) and Low stock (line 228) which both have one.
findings.failure_scenario: A brand-new store, or an admin whose `categories` snapshot fails: the right-hand column shows a bordered card containing only the heading 'Category performance' and roughly 200px of empty white. Nothing tells the admin whether it is loading, empty, or broken, so they wait for data that will never arrive.
findings.fix: Add the same treatment the sibling panels already use: a skeleton while `products.loading || categoryOrders.isLoading`, 'Could not load category performance' when either errors, and 'No sales in this period' when the result is genuinely empty.

verdict.reason: Verified accurate. DashboardPage.tsx:151 renders `{cats.map(...)}` as the panel's only body — no loading, empty, or error branch — while the two sibling panels in the same file do have them (recent orders at 186-197, low stock at 228). categoryPerformance (dashboard.ts:308) returns [] when there are no 90-day order line items and no published products; on every initial dashboard render both sources are empty (useLiveCollection seeds data: [] with loading: true, and the categoryOrders react-query starts undefined), so the card is blank until data lands, and permanently blank on a fresh store. The error path is real too: firestoreCache.ts:117-121 keeps data: [] and stores the FirestoreError on the snapshot, and DashboardPage never reads .error; there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src and no toast on listener failure, so a denied products/categories snapshot leaves a heading over empty space forever. Because the card is a grid item next to the 180px-tall Revenue trend card with default align-items: stretch, the blank region really is a few hundred px, and the trend card's own placeholder-bar fallback (line 129) makes the neighbour's blankness more conspicuous. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers query scoping, not panel states) and not on the known-intentional list. Low severity and UI-only, which is the only reason confidence is medium rather than high, but it is a genuine missing-state gap with a one-line fix.

findings.title: Sub-category Hide/Show toggle is dead on the Flutter app — the app model drops `visibility`
findings.detail: `toggle()` flips `visibility` inside the embedded `subCategories` array and persists it via `updateSubCategories`. The web honours it (`web/src/components/catalog/CategoriesView.tsx:50-52` and `ListingView.tsx:52-53` filter on `s.visibility === 'visible'`). The Flutter app does not: `app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart:31-36` builds `SubCategory` with only `slug` and `name` — the class has no visibility field at all (category.dart:3-7) — and `app/lib/features/catalog/category_products_screen.dart:122-123` renders a chip for every entry in `_subs`. Note also that on both surfaces hiding a sub only removes the filter chip; the products still list under "All".
findings.failure_scenario: Admin hides the "EDP" sub-category of Perfumes because the line is discontinued. On the website the EDP facet disappears as expected. In the app, the EDP chip is still on the category screen and still filters to those products — so the merchandising decision silently applies to one storefront only.
findings.fix: Parse and filter `visibility` in `app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart` (mirror the web's `!= 'hidden'` convention), and decide one behaviour for the products themselves: either exclude products whose `subCategorySlug` points at a hidden sub from the listing on both surfaces, or relabel the toggle so it clearly only controls the filter chip.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all surfaces. Admin (admin/src/features/categories/routes/SubCategoriesPage.tsx:50-56) persists sub-category `visibility` into the embedded `subCategories` array; web honours it (web/src/components/catalog/CategoriesView.tsx:50-52 and ListingView.tsx:52-53 filter `s.visibility === 'visible'`); the Flutter app does not — app/lib/features/catalog/data/category.dart:3-7 declares `SubCategory` with only `slug` and `name`, and `Category.fromDoc` (lines 31-37) drops `visibility` entirely, so category_products_screen.dart:48,122-123 renders a chip for every entry. Refutation attempts failed: grep of `visibility` across app/lib yields only product-level and category-level filters (catalog_repository.dart:28,54,74,88,135,163; checkout_repository.dart:144) — none inspects the sub-category array; the app reads categories directly from Firestore with no Cloud Function re-check; `subCategories` appears nowhere else in app/lib; and this is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Severity is moderate rather than high because, as the claim itself notes, hiding a sub only removes the facet/chip on either surface (products remain listed under "All"), so it is a merchandising inconsistency, not data exposure — but the admin toggle is genuinely inert on the app and the fix is trivial (add `visibility` to the Dart model and filter `_subs`).

findings.title: slugify() can return an empty string — category save fails with an opaque error and sub-categories/units save with empty ids
findings.detail: `slugify` strips everything outside `[a-z0-9]`, so a name written in Arabic/Urdu/Hindi (or pure punctuation) yields `''`. `saveCategory` then calls `setDoc(doc(db, 'categories', ''), …)` (categories.ts:89), which the Firestore SDK rejects synchronously; `CategoryFormPage.onSave` catches it and shows only `'Could not save the category.'` (CategoryFormPage.tsx:166-168). The name field itself only validates non-empty (CategoryFormPage.tsx:136). The sub-category paths are worse — they don't hit a doc path so nothing throws: `SubCategoriesPage.add` (line 42) and `CategoryFormPage.addSub` (line 83) persist `{ id: '', slug: '', name: 'عطور' }` into the array. The same hole exists in `unitId` (settings/api/variables.ts:25) used by CreateVariantModal and AddUnitsModal. Also, image upload on a new category with such a name hits the `if (!catId)` branch and tells the admin to "Enter the category name first" when they already have (CategoryFormPage.tsx:115-118).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin (this is an Islamic store) types "عطور" as a category name and clicks Save category → "Could not save the category." with no hint what is wrong; it will never succeed. On the sub-category screen the same name is accepted: a sub with `slug: ''` is stored, appears in the product form's Sub-category dropdown with value `''`, and selecting it then fails product validation with "Sub-category is required." A second non-latin sub is refused as a duplicate because both slugify to `''`.
findings.fix: Validate the derived slug before writing: if `slugify(name) === ''`, reject with a specific message ("Use at least one Latin letter or digit in the name") in CategoryFormPage, SubCategoriesPage, CreateVariantModal and AddUnitsModal — or fall back to a transliteration/random id and keep the display name as typed.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end; could not refute any link. (1) slugify (admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:31) returns '' for any name with no [a-z0-9] chars — confirmed by running the exact regex on 'عطور', 'इत्र', '&&&'. (2) Category create really fails: categories.ts:89 does setDoc(doc(db,'categories','')); in the installed @firebase/firestore 4.7.3, ResourcePath.fromString drops zero-length segments leaving ['categories'], and __PRIVATE_validateDocumentPath throws 'must have an even number of segments'. The throw is swallowed by the bare catch at CategoryFormPage.tsx:166-168 → generic 'Could not save the category.' The only name validation is !name.trim() (line 136), and the duplicate guard (line 143) can't help since no slug:'' category can ever exist. (3) Sub-categories are worse and silent: SubCategoriesPage.add:42 and CategoryFormPage.addSub:83 push {id:'',slug:'',name:…} into the embedded array; no doc path is involved so nothing throws. There is no server-side re-check — firebase/firestore.rules:49 is `allow write: if canWrite('categories')`, permission-only with zero content validation, and no Cloud Function touches category writes (correct per the architecture rules, so the client is the only place this can be fixed). (4) Downstream breakage confirmed: ProductFormPage.tsx:346 maps options to {value: s.slug}, so the empty-slug sub is selectable as '' and ProductFormPage.tsx:169 then fails with 'Sub-category is required.'; a second non-latin sub is refused as a duplicate because both slugify to ''. (5) The unitId twin (settings/api/variables.ts:25) is the identical regex feeding makeColorUnit/makeGroupUnit id fields — notably unitCode two lines below DOES have an `|| 'X'` empty fallback, showing the gap is an oversight rather than a convention. (6) The image-upload complaint is accurate (CategoryFormPage.tsx:114-118 tells the admin to enter a name they already entered). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; realistic input for an Islamic perfume store; small local fix (fallback slug + form-level validation message).

findings.title: Variant units can never be edited — a wrong colour hex or a typo'd name is permanent once a product uses it
findings.detail: AddUnitsModal only supports add and remove. Re-adding a unit with the same name is refused (`if (units.some(u => u.id === id))` line 53-56, and the id is derived from the name), and removing a unit that any product references is blocked by the delete-safety check (line 76-81, and VariablesTab.tsx:99-115 for the chip on the card). There is no rename input, no hex re-picker on an existing chip, and no edit affordance anywhere on VariablesTab — the chip only carries a remove button (VariablesTab.tsx:142-150). `hex` is stored per unit (`ColorUnit.hex`) and used to paint the swatch in the product form (ProductFormPage.tsx:143, 467).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin adds colour "Ivory" and mis-picks the swatch as black. Three products are saved with variant attribute `color: ivory`. They return to Settings ▸ Variables to fix the swatch: the chip has only an ✕, clicking it says "In use by 3 products — cannot remove", and adding "Ivory" again in the modal says "That unit already exists." The wrong swatch is now permanent unless someone edits Firestore by hand.
findings.fix: Make the unit chips editable — click a chip to reopen name/hex in the modal, writing back the same `id` (rename changes only `name`, never the id, so product attributes stay valid). Re-derive `code` on rename with the same collision check.

verdict.reason: Confirmed at every cited line. AddUnitsModal.tsx only supports add (lines 49-67, duplicate id refused because unitId() is name-derived) and remove (69-88, blocked when countProductsUsingUnit > 0); existing chips at 150-175 render a static swatch and an ✕ only — no name field, no color re-picker, no click-to-edit. VariablesTab.tsx's chip() (142-150) likewise exposes only onDel, and its delete-safety guards (99-115, 118-134) block removal of in-use units. Refutation attempts failed: saveVariables (api/variables.ts:38) has exactly one caller file, the updateSettingsVariables callable referenced in functions/src/index.ts:73 does not exist (functions/src/catalog/ has only inventory.ts), and web/ and app/ never read settings/variables, so there is no other surface, no server-side re-check, and no fallback. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. One nuance: hex itself is admin-only cosmetics (consumed just by ProductFormPage.tsx:143/467), and a tedious workaround exists (clear the attribute on referencing products, delete, re-add the same name — the id regenerates identically), so "permanent unless someone edits Firestore" is overstated. But the same missing update path makes the unit NAME uncorrectable, and names are functional: ProductFormPage.tsx:249 snapshots them into variant.label (customer-facing on web ProductDetail.tsx:128 and app product_details_screen.dart:433) and unitCode(name) feeds the SKU at line 246. So it is a real, fixable broken-CRUD defect; a fix must keep the unit id stable on rename since products reference it.

findings.title: Categories list re-runs one count query per category on every snapshot and swallows failures silently
findings.detail: The effect depends on `[categories]`, which is a brand-new array reference on every Firestore snapshot from `useLiveCollection` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts maps `snap.docs` fresh each time). So every write to any category document — hiding one, deleting one, another admin's edit, or the initial listener settle — refires N `getCountFromServer` aggregation queries (categories.ts:41-46). The whole chain ends in `.catch(() => undefined)` (line 38), so a permission or network failure leaves `counts` empty with no error surfaced; the column silently falls back to `c.productCount ?? 0` (line 124), which is always 0 for admin-created categories.
findings.failure_scenario: With 12 categories, an admin toggling Hide on one category fires 12 aggregation queries; toggling five categories in a row fires 60. If any of those reject (offline, backend hiccup), the Products column silently shows 0 for every category and the operator believes the catalogue is empty — then hits "reassign them first" when they try to delete, with no clue why the two numbers disagree.
findings.fix: Key the effect on a stable value (e.g. `categories.map(c => c.id).join(',')`), and surface failures — set an error flag and render "—" with a retry rather than the misleading 0.

verdict.reason: Claim holds on every checkable point. useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts) rebuilds the array via snap.docs.map on each snapshot, so the effect at CategoriesListPage.tsx:31-42, keyed on [categories], refires N getCountFromServer aggregation queries per category snapshot — in fact ~2N per admin write, since an updateDoc with serverTimestamp yields both an optimistic and a server-ack snapshot. emit() clones only the snapshot wrapper (data reference preserved), so unrelated re-renders do not refire, but any category write does. The .catch(() => undefined) at line 38 swallows every failure with no error state, and the fallback c.productCount ?? 0 at line 124 is confirmed always 0: saveCategory writes productCount: 0 at creation (categories.ts:94) and no Cloud Function ever maintains it — app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:63 states this outright ("never maintained by any Cloud Function (it's always 0)"); only scripts/seed.ts writes non-zero. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no memoization, cache, or guard exists. Severity is lower than the report implies: the destructive path is independently guarded — askDelete (line 52) re-fetches the count server-side before opening the confirm dialog, so an empty counts map cannot cause an accidental delete, and N is small (seed has 4 categories). But redundant network round-trips plus a silently-wrong 0 in the Products column is a real, two-line-fixable defect, not a cosmetic one.

findings.title: Sub-categories screen shows a Products column that nothing ever writes — always 0
findings.detail: The table renders `{s.productCount ?? 0}`. `SubCategory.productCount` is written as the literal `0` when a sub is created — SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:83 — and no code path in admin, web, app, functions or the scheduled sweeps ever updates it (grep for `productCount` returns only these writers plus the seed's hardcoded 1). Meanwhile the delete-safety guard right below it computes the real number with `countSubCategoryProducts` (categories.ts:49-58), so the screen already has access to the truth and doesn't use it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens Perfumes ▸ sub-categories to decide which sub to retire. Every row shows "1" (seeded value) or "0" (anything they created), regardless of the 40 products actually attached. They click ✕ on a sub showing 0 and get "Oud has 12 products — reassign them first" — the column flatly contradicts the guard.
findings.fix: Populate the column from `countSubCategoryProducts` (one aggregation per sub on mount, or one grouped pass over the category's products) and stop persisting the dead `productCount: 0` field on the embedded objects.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. Repo-wide grep for `productCount` (admin, web, app, functions, packages/shared, scripts, no node_modules) finds only: the two type declarations (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:11,26), three literal-`0` initializers (SubCategoriesPage.tsx:42, CategoryFormPage.tsx:83, categories.ts:94), hardcoded seed values (scripts/seed.ts:293,300; add-back-to-school.ts:72,79), and three reads. No Cloud Function, trigger, sweep, or Flutter/web code ever updates SubCategory.productCount when a product is created, deleted, or reassigned, so the value is frozen at its creation-time literal. The sibling screen proves the intended pattern and shows this one is the outlier: CategoriesListPage.tsx:30-42 runs a getCountFromServer aggregation effect and renders `counts[c.id] ?? c.productCount ?? 0`, explicitly demoting the stale field to a fallback with the comment "Live product counts via aggregation (no denormalization trigger needed)". SubCategoriesPage.tsx:131 renders the bare `s.productCount ?? 0` with no such effect. The correct value is already reachable in-file: countSubCategoryProducts (admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:49-58) is imported at line 11 and used by askDelete at line 61, and products genuinely carry subCategoryId (packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts:63, seed.ts:355), so the guard's "N products — reassign them first" toast will contradict a column reading 0. Not covered by the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; the path is reachable via /categories/:id/sub. Only inaccuracy is the title's "always 0" — seeded subs render the hardcoded 1 — which the claim body already concedes and which does not affect the defect.

findings.title: StockHistoryModal turns any read failure into 'No stock changes recorded yet.'
findings.detail: `getStockHistory(productId).then(...).catch(() => alive && setEntries([]))` — the catch collapses a permission-denied, offline or index error into the same empty array used for 'genuinely no history', and the modal then renders the definitive empty copy at line 54. There is no error branch and nothing is logged or toasted. `getStockHistory` (api/inventory.ts:168-173) is also an unbounded `getDocs` over stockAdjustments for the product with no limit, sorted client-side.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose custom claim has gone stale (or is simply offline for a moment) opens 'View stock history' on a product that has 40 recorded adjustments. The modal states 'No stock changes recorded yet.' The admin concludes the ledger never recorded their earlier corrections and re-applies them, double-counting stock.
findings.fix: Track a third state (`error`) in the modal and render 'Couldn't load stock history — retry', and add a `limit(100)` with a 'load more' to getStockHistory.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. StockHistoryModal.tsx:25 catches every rejection from getStockHistory and sets entries to [], which line 53 renders as the definitive "No stock changes recorded yet." There is no error branch, no log and no toast, and nothing above it compensates: InventoryListPage.tsx:164-170 only mounts the modal, and admin/src has no ErrorBoundary, componentDidCatch or onunhandledrejection handler. The path is reachable — firestore.rules:230 gates stockAdjustments reads on isAdmin(), so a stale claim or a transient offline/unavailable getDocs rejection lands in the catch. This is also an outlier against the codebase's own convention: hooks/firestoreCache.ts threads FirestoreError through CollectionState (lines 21, 95, 117-118, 147-148) and features/reports/api/reports.ts:119 keeps cached data while surfacing the error; StockHistoryModal is the only place in admin/src that collapses a read failure into a success-shaped empty value. The secondary point also holds: getStockHistory (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:168-172) is an unbounded getDocs with client-side sort and no limit. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared) reads or writes stockAdjustments in a way that mitigates it. Severity is lower than the reporter suggests — the inventory list shows current stock, so an admin would probably notice their earlier correction is already reflected before re-applying it — but the misleading definitive-empty-on-error state on an audit ledger is a real, cheaply fixable functional defect (add a distinct error state alongside null/rows).

findings.title: A sub-admin without inventory.edit sees and can use the whole Adjust stock flow; the server's rejection message is thrown away
findings.detail: There is no route- or control-level permission gate: router.tsx:71-72 mounts /inventory and /inventory/adjust behind RequireAuth only (RequireAuth.tsx checks `admin` truthiness, nothing else), and the 'Adjust stock' button (line 79) plus the row menu item (line 127) render for every admin. Only the Sidebar filters by `modulePermissions[item.module].view` (Sidebar.tsx:12). Server-side both adminAdjustStock (`requireModule(req,'inventory','edit')`, functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:26) and the stockAdjustments rule (`can('inventory','edit')`, firestore.rules:235) correctly deny — but AdjustStockPage's catch discards `e.message` and shows the generic 'Could not save adjustments.' (line 100). The same swallowing hides the CF's carefully written stale-SKU message ('N SKUs no longer exist … Nothing was adjusted — reload the page and try again.', inventory.ts:109-112).
findings.failure_scenario: A catalogue sub-admin with inventory.view but not inventory.edit opens /inventory, clicks 'Adjust stock', spends five minutes setting deltas across 20 SKUs, hits Save and gets 'Could not save adjustments.' with no hint that it is a permissions problem — and their work is still on screen with no way to make it succeed. The same opaque toast appears when the real cause is a concurrently deleted variant.
findings.fix: Gate the button/menu item on `admin.role === 'super_admin' || admin.modulePermissions?.inventory?.edit` (as QuickActions.tsx:42 already does for create), redirect /inventory/adjust for anyone lacking it, and surface `(e as FirebaseError).message` in the toast for 'permission-denied' and 'not-found' codes.

verdict.reason: Could not refute the core of it. Confirmed: router.tsx:71-72 mounts /inventory and /inventory/adjust behind RequireAuth only, and RequireAuth.tsx checks nothing but `ready`+`admin`; a grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is consulted only in Sidebar.tsx:12 (.view) and QuickActions.tsx:42 (.create), so the 'Adjust stock' button (InventoryListPage.tsx:79) and row menu item (:127) do render for every admin. The decisive, non-refutable part is the error swallowing: the admin already has a shared helper /home/h/barkath/admin/src/lib/cfError.ts that maps permission-denied to "You don't have permission to …" and passes through failed-precondition/invalid-argument messages, and it is used in ~15 other CF-calling screens (OrderDetailPage, ReturnsListPage, AffiliateListPage, CustomerProfilePage, SubAdminList/Form, AllocateAffiliatePage, ConfirmDialog). AdjustStockPage.tsx:100 ignores that convention and hard-codes 'Could not save adjustments.', discarding both the permission-denied code and the CF's deliberately worded not-found stale-SKU message (functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:109-112). No interceptor rescues it: lib/firebase.ts is a plain getFunctions instance and adjustStock (features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:97) lets the callable rejection propagate untouched (only the ledger batch failure is wrapped as LedgerWriteError). Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (that entry covers adminAdjustStock returning before/after) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL. Caveat that lowers severity: the 'permission' framing overstates it — requireModule(req,'inventory','edit') and the firestore.rules stockAdjustments rule both deny correctly, so there is no privilege escalation, and no admin page anywhere gates edit-level controls, making the missing UI gate a codebase-wide pattern rather than an inventory-specific bug. The real, fixable defect is the swallowed message at AdjustStockPage.tsx:100 (should call cfError), with the missing disabled/hidden control as a secondary UX fix.

findings.title: Stock is clamped to zero server-side but the ledger row still records the full delta, producing before + delta ≠ after
findings.detail: adminAdjustStock computes `after = Math.max(0, before + delta)` for both the base stock (line 81) and each variant (line 92) and reports that clamped value back. The admin then writes the audit row with the ORIGINAL requested `delta` alongside the clamped before/after (api/inventory.ts:116-126, addLedger writes `before`, `delta`, `after` independently). The clamp is silent — no warning, no partial-application report — while the client's only guard is `if (current + next < 0) return d` against the possibly stale local stock (AdjustStockPage.tsx:41).
findings.failure_scenario: A SKU shows 8 units in the admin's open tab; a customer buys 6 in the meantime. The admin records damage of −8. The transaction clamps 2 − 8 to 0 and the ledger stores before:2, delta:−8, after:0 — an audit row that doesn't add up, and 6 units of damage that were never actually deducted, with the admin told 'Stock adjusted for 1 SKU'.
findings.fix: Either reject the adjustment when `before + delta < 0` (consistent with the batch-rejects-on-unresolved-SKU behaviour already implemented at line 108), or return an `appliedDelta` per SKU and have the client write that value into the ledger and warn the operator.

verdict.reason: Verified in code and could not refute it. functions/src/catalog/inventory.ts:81 and :92 clamp with Math.max(0, before + delta) and return only {before, after} — there is no rejection, no applied-vs-requested signal. admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:116-126 then passes the server's r.before/r.after alongside the client's original a.delta into addLedger, which writes all three verbatim (lines 149-164), so a clamped adjustment stores before + delta != after. The clamp is reachable: the page's only guard (AdjustStockPage.tsx:41) fires at bump time against a live-updating r.stock and is never re-checked at save, while checkout.ts:570 / cancel.ts:126 move stock concurrently via FieldValue.increment. It is also user-visible, not dead data — StockHistoryModal.tsx:81-86 renders Change (delta) next to After (after), so a clamped row reads "-8 / After 0" implying a prior stock of 8 that never existed; and the toast at AdjustStockPage.tsx:91 reports payload.length (requested), so a partially applied batch still reads as full success. adminAdjustStock has only this one call path. Not on the already-fixed list (that item was about returning {before,after}, which is what introduced the mismatch) nor the intentional list. Confidence is medium rather than high only because actual stock remains correct — the impact is a false audit row plus silent partial application, not data corruption — but it is a real, one-line-fixable defect (delta should be r.after - r.before, ideally with a server-side clamp signal for the toast).

findings.title: Rider phone is silently discarded when the rider name is blank
findings.detail: `const rider = name ? { name, phone: clean(riderPhone), currentDistanceKm } : null;` — if riderName is empty the entire Rider object is set to null, dropping the phone the admin just typed. The callable still returns {ok:true} and the admin UI toasts 'Shipment details saved' (OrderDetailPage.tsx:115). Because `shipDirty` compares riderPhone against `order.rider?.phone ?? ''` (line 103), the Save button stays enabled forever after the failed save.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin has only the delivery driver's number, types 9812345678 into 'Rider phone', leaves 'Rider' blank, clicks Save shipment. Toast says saved; the phone is never persisted (rider stays null), the field still shows the typed number and the Save button never goes back to disabled, so the admin clicks it repeatedly with no effect. Clearing an existing rider's name to correct a typo likewise wipes the stored phone.
findings.fix: Build the rider object when a name OR a phone is present (`riderName || riderPhone`), or reject the payload with invalid-argument when a phone is supplied without a name so the admin sees a real error.

verdict.reason: Confirmed real defect. functions/src/orders/shipment.ts:40-48 builds the Rider object only when the cleaned riderName is truthy, so a phone-only submit (or clearing an existing name) writes rider: null and silently discards the phone, while the callable returns {ok:true} and the audit meta records only the name. Refutation attempts all failed: (a) the shared type packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:26 declares name as string|null, so {name:null, phone} is a legal shape — the guard is not protecting a type invariant; (b) both customer surfaces already tolerate a null name (web track page line 120 renders under order.rider?.name &&; app order_tracking_screen.dart:239-240 guards rider != null && isNotEmpty), so no consumer requires the name gate; (c) rider.phone is not a dead field — OrderDetailPage.tsx:61 reads it back to seed the admin's "Rider phone" input, and grep across functions/, admin/, web/, app/, packages/shared and scripts/seed.ts shows adminAssignRider is its only writer, so nothing else re-persists it; (d) the stuck-Save consequence is real because the seeding effect (OrderDetailPage.tsx:44,55-62) uses a shipSeeded ref to seed inputs once per order id and deliberately ignores later live snapshots, so riderPhone keeps the typed value while order.rider?.phone ?? '' is '', leaving shipDirty (line 103) true and the Save button (line 229) permanently enabled after a toast that claims success; (e) the path is reachable and wired (exported functions/src/index.ts:23, called from admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:137) with no required-field validation in the UI; (f) it is not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists. Severity is moderate (phone is admin-internal, not shown to customers) but it is genuine silent data loss with a broken dirty-state, fixable with `const rider = name || phone ? {...} : null`.

findings.title: Firestore errors on the orders list and detail are swallowed and rendered as 'No orders yet' / 'Order not found'
findings.detail: Both screens destructure only `{ data, loading }` from the live hooks (OrdersListPage.tsx:26; OrderDetailPage.tsx:26,30,31) and never read `error`, even though useLiveCollection/useLiveDoc surface it. On a snapshot error the cache sets `{data: [], loading: false, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121, 147-150), so the list falls into its empty branch (line 124 'No orders yet.') and the detail into `!order` → 'Order not found.' (line 74).
findings.failure_scenario: A rules deployment, an expired token, or a sub-admin whose read is denied opens /orders and is told 'No orders yet.' — an admin will reasonably conclude the store has no orders rather than that the read failed. Same on a detail page: a permission-denied read reports 'Order not found', tempting the admin to re-place the order.
findings.fix: Surface the error state on both screens (an error row/panel with a retry) instead of collapsing it into the empty state.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. OrdersListPage.tsx:26 and OrderDetailPage.tsx:26,30,31 destructure only {data, loading} from useLiveCollection/useLiveDoc, both of which do expose `error` (firestoreCache.ts:96,130). On a snapshot error the cache emits {data: [], loading:false, error} (firestoreCache.ts:117-121) and {data:null, loading:false, error} (147-150), so the list falls to its empty branch ('No orders yet.', line 124) and the detail to !order → 'Order not found.' (line 74). Nothing compensates: no error boundary, no toast in the cache, and useOrdersList/useOrder (features/orders/api/orders.ts:18-26) are thin pass-throughs. This is not intentional in-repo style — ReturnsListPage.tsx:105-118 implements exactly the missing banner with the comment "Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state" plus a permission-denied message, and PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:13,69 also reads error, so the orders screens are the outlier. Reachable: firestore.rules:69 gates orders reads on isAdmin(), which depends on the mirrored `role` custom claim, while admin sign-in (auth/api/auth.ts:39-50) only checks the admins doc and refreshes the token — a missing/stale claim or a rules deploy yields permission-denied while RequireAuth still admits the user. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Only caveat: the "reviews-only sub-admin" variant is weak since any sub_admin satisfies isAdmin(); the token/claim and rules-deploy paths carry the finding.

findings.title: /orders is reachable by any signed-in admin regardless of orders.view, and orders.edit actions are only hidden client-side
findings.detail: Routes under RequireAuth check only that an admin is signed in (RequireAuth.tsx:18-22); nothing checks modulePermissions. Only the Sidebar filters links (Sidebar.tsx:12). firestore.rules:69 grants order reads to `isAdmin()` — any admin role, not `can('orders','view')` — unlike the direct-write collections which use can()/canWrite(). Conversely the Update-status menu, Save shipment and Invoice buttons are rendered unconditionally on the detail page (no permission check anywhere in OrderDetailPage.tsx), while the callables enforce orders.edit (status.ts:54, shipment.ts:22, invoice.ts:23).
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin provisioned for reviews only types /orders in the address bar (or follows the 'New order' notification deep link, seed.ts:856): the page loads and streams every order with customer names, phone numbers and full delivery addresses, because the rules allow any admin to read orders. The reverse also bites: a sub-admin with orders.view but not orders.edit sees an enabled 'Update status' button, clicks Delivered, and gets a generic 'You don't have permission…' toast after the round trip.
findings.fix: Gate the route on modulePermissions.orders.view (a RequirePermission wrapper), tighten firestore.rules orders/payments reads to can('orders','view'), and disable/hide the status, shipment and invoice controls when orders.edit is false.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. RequireAuth.tsx:18-22 only checks that an admin is signed in; router.tsx puts every page behind that single guard, and a full grep of admin/src shows modulePermissions is consulted in exactly 4 places (Sidebar.tsx:12 nav filtering, QuickActions.tsx:42, SubAdminFormPage, AccountDialogs) — no route guard, no PermissionGate/403 component exists. OrderDetailPage.tsx has zero references to useAuthStore/role/permission, so Update status, Save shipment and Invoice render unconditionally. firestore.rules:68-69 gates order reads on isAdmin() (line 12: role in {super_admin, sub_admin}), which ignores modulePermissions and even the active-status check that can() (line 23-29) performs. Since packages/shared/src/enums.ts:276 defines a real 'view' action that the sub-admin form toggles and the Sidebar honours, a seeded catalog-only sub-admin (scripts/seed.ts:113-118, orders.view=false) can navigate to /orders and stream every order with customer name, phone and full delivery address — a genuine, fixable privilege-separation gap not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Partial refutation: the second half of the scenario is cosmetic only — functions/src/orders/status.ts:54, shipment.ts:22 and invoice.ts:23 all call requireModule(req,'orders','edit'), which re-reads the admin doc rather than trusting claims, so no unauthorized write is possible; the defect is the read exposure plus the missing client-side disable, not a write hole. Confidence is medium rather than high because every read rule in the file uses isAdmin() uniformly, so read-openness could be a deliberate posture (the can() helper's own comment scopes it to direct-write collections) — but that contradicts the advertised per-module view toggle.

findings.title: Generated invoice is never invalidated — a cancelled, refunded order still offers a tax invoice for the full amount
findings.detail: The Invoice button is enabled at every status; the first click calls adminGenerateInvoice, which renders the GST invoice and stamps invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt on the order (invoice.ts:67). Afterwards the handler short-circuits on `order.invoiceUrl` (line 124) and only reopens the stored URL — it can never be regenerated. performCancellation (cancel.ts:227-234) updates status/paymentStatus/cancellationReason but leaves invoiceUrl untouched, and the storage object stays live behind its download token. Both customer clients treat a non-null invoiceUrl as 'invoice ready': web renders a Download PDF button (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108) whose fallback copy is 'Your PDF invoice generates once the order is delivered', and the app shares it (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24).
findings.failure_scenario: Admin clicks Invoice on an order that is still 'accepted' (to check the formatting), then cancels the order and the customer is refunded ₹1,299 to their wallet. The customer's Invoice page still shows 'Download PDF' and serves a tax invoice for ₹1,299 on a cancelled, fully refunded order — and the admin has no way to regenerate or revoke it.
findings.fix: Clear invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt (and delete the storage object) inside performCancellation, restrict generation to delivered orders (matching the customer-facing copy), and let the button regenerate/refresh an existing invoice instead of only reopening it.
