verdict.reason: Every assertion checks out and I found no guard anywhere. admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:123-138 short-circuits on order.invoiceUrl and only reopens the stored URL; the Invoice button (line 176) has no disabled state at any status (the `cancelled` flag at line 98 only gates the shipment fields at 217-229). functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:18-68 gates solely on requireModule(req,'orders','edit') with NO order-status precondition, writes invoices/{shortId}.html with a firebaseStorageDownloadTokens token, stamps invoiceUrl/invoiceGeneratedAt (line 67), and freezes the payment state into the HTML footer (`Payment: ${o.paymentMethod} · ${o.paymentStatus}`), so a post-refund invoice still reads "paid". A repo-wide grep for invoiceUrl finds exactly one writer (invoice.ts:67) plus the initial nulls in checkout.ts:666 and seed.ts:632 — nothing ever clears it. performCancellation (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts), the single funnel for both customer and admin cancels, updates status/paymentStatus/restock/wallet-refund/commission-reversal/payments row but never touches invoiceUrl or the Storage object; the approved-return path doesn't either. firebase/storage.rules:26 denies direct client reads but its own comment states the tokened URL bypasses rules, and no token rotation or delete exists, so the object stays live. Both clients key on the field alone: web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108-119 renders "Download PDF" whenever invoiceUrl is non-null, and app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:24-28 shares it; neither hides the Invoice entry point for cancelled orders (web .../orders/[id]/page.tsx:231, OrderCard.tsx:91, app order_detail_screen.dart:104). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, reachable in one click, and fixable in a few lines (clear invoiceUrl in the cancellation transaction and/or allow regeneration — the Storage path is deterministic so it would simply overwrite). One qualifier that does not refute the claim: the web invoice page also renders its own on-screen invoice card for any status independent of invoiceUrl, so a complete fix needs status-awareness there too.

findings.title: Profile tabs ignore loading and error from their queries — a failed query renders a permanent, wrong empty state
findings.detail: `AffiliateTab` (line 386), `WalletTab` (line 290) and `OrdersTab` (line 256) each destructure only `{ data }` from the hooks, discarding the `loading` and `error` fields that `useLiveCollection` returns (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets `{data: previous, loading:false, error}` on failure). The commissions query is `where('affiliateUid','==',uid) + orderBy('accruedAt','desc')` (customers.ts:46), which needs the composite index in firebase/firestore.indexes.json:50 — if that index is missing in an environment, or if rules deny the read, the tab renders 'No affiliate earnings yet.' forever with the FirestoreError only in the console.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens a top affiliate's profile → 'Affiliate wallet' tab. The header shows ₹3,200 confirmed balance (read from the customer doc) but the table says 'No affiliate earnings yet.' because the commissions listener failed with failed-precondition (index) or permission-denied. The admin concludes the commissions were never accrued. The same tab also flashes the empty state for a beat on every open, even on success.
findings.fix: Read `loading`/`error` in all three tabs: render a spinner while `loading && data.length===0`, and an explicit error row ('Couldn't load commissions — retry') when `error` is set.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code and not refutable. OrdersTab (CustomerProfilePage.tsx:256), WalletTab (:290) and AffiliateTab (:386) each destructure only `{ data }` from useLiveCollection, which returns `{data, loading, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:99-121; the error callback sets `{data: previous, loading:false, error}`). Tabs mount lazily (lines 216-218), so every first click on a tab starts a cold cache entry (`loading:true, data:[]`) and renders 'No orders yet.' / 'No wallet activity.' / 'No affiliate earnings yet.' for the whole round trip — the exact empty-state flash the cache's docstring was written to prevent — and any listener error leaves that wrong empty state permanently with only a console FirestoreError. This is a deviation from the established house pattern, not the house pattern: SubAdminListPage.tsx:123-127 renders an explicit 'Loading…' row then a 'Couldn't load admins. Please try again.' error row, and OrdersListPage:117, PaymentsListPage:100, InventoryListPage:109, AdjustStockPage:133 all guard with `loading && rows.length === 0`; CouponsListPage, ReturnsListPage, BannerListPage, NotificationsListPage and SpinnerListPage all read `error`. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two corrections to the claim, which is why confidence is medium rather than high: (1) the commissions composite index (affiliateUid ASC + accruedAt DESC) IS declared in firebase/firestore.indexes.json (~line 72, not line 50), so failed-precondition only occurs in an environment where indexes were not deployed; (2) permission-denied is unlikely for the admin panel since firestore.rules:110-113 grants the read to any isAdmin() (super_admin or sub_admin) with no module gate. Also the OrdersTab query is equality-only (customers.ts:31) and needs no composite index, so the error half of the claim is weak there. The unconditional, always-reproducible half is the missing loading guard.

findings.title: Customers list renders 'No customers yet.' when the Firestore query fails
findings.detail: The page takes `{ data: customers, loading }` and drops `error` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117 sets `loading:false, error` on the snapshot error path). The empty branch at line 112-114 therefore prints 'No customers yet.' for a permission-denied / unavailable / index error, and the header at line 74 confidently prints '0 registered · 0 affiliates'.
findings.failure_scenario: Rules are redeployed with the customers read tightened, or the admin's session loses its role claim. Every admin opening /customers sees a clean 'No customers yet.' and a '0 registered' header, and reports that the customer database was wiped; the actual permission-denied error is silently swallowed.
findings.fix: Surface `error` from `useCustomersList()` as a distinct error state ('Couldn't load customers') and keep the count header blank while erroring.

verdict.reason: Claim verified. CustomersListPage.tsx:19 destructures only {data, loading} from useCustomersList(); the two 'error' tokens in the file are toast.error calls in the affiliate-toggle handler, not the read path. firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: previous ([] on first attach), loading:false, error} on the snapshot error callback, so a permission-denied read exits the loading branch at line 108 and falls into line 113 printing 'No customers yet.', with the header at line 74 asserting '0 registered · 0 affiliates'. Nothing else surfaces the error: the hook does not toast/log/throw, and there is no ErrorBoundary anywhere in admin/src (grep for ErrorBoundary|componentDidCatch returns nothing). The path is reachable: RequireAuth.tsx gates on the admins doc in the auth store, while firestore.rules:157 (allow read: isOwner(userId) || isAdmin()) evaluates request.auth.token.role, so a stale/missing role claim denies the read while the page still renders. Not on the already-fixed list ('auth listener has an error path' refers to the authStore listener, not collection subscriptions) and not on the known-intentional list. Not cosmetic — the page asserts a false fact ('0 registered') rather than just looking odd. The codebase's own convention confirms this is treated as a defect elsewhere: BannerListPage.tsx:77-78, CouponsListPage.tsx:124-126, plus spinner, returns, subadmin, notifications, reviews and products list pages all consume the same hook's error and render an error row; customers (with orders and payments) is the anomaly. Severity is moderate (misleading state, not data loss) and the fix is a small error branch mirroring CouponsListPage.tsx:124.

findings.title: PaymentsListPage swallows the Firestore listener error and renders the empty state instead
findings.detail: `useLiveCollection` surfaces `{data, loading, error}` (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets `error` on the snapshot error callback) but line 22 destructures only `{ data: payments, loading }` and the render (lines 100-103) has no error branch: on error `loading` becomes false and `payments` stays `[]`, so the table falls through to `payments.length === 0 ? 'No payments yet.'`. Other screens in the app (DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:118, PaymentGatewayTab.tsx:69) do render an error card, so this is an omission, not a house style.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose custom claims haven't propagated, or any rules/index failure on the `payments` orderBy query, opens /payments and is told "No payments yet." — an authoritative-looking statement that the store has taken zero money. Nothing is logged to the user and the header confidently prints "₹0 this month · 0 failed".
findings.fix: Destructure `error` and render a "Couldn't load payments. Please refresh." card, matching the settings tabs.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx:22 destructures only {data, loading} from usePaymentsList(), and the file contains zero references to `error` (grep -c error = 0), so the tbody at lines 100-103 renders 'No payments yet.' and the header at line 78 renders '₹0 this month · 0 failed' when the listener fails. useLiveCollection does surface the error (hooks/firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: prev ?? [], loading:false, error}). This is an omission, not house style: CouponsListPage:124, NotificationsListPage:74, SpinnerListPage:89, BannerListPage:77, SubAdminListPage:30, ReturnsListPage, ReviewsListPage and ProductsListPage all read and render `error`; only Payments and OrdersListPage:26 do not. No global error boundary or snapshot-error toast catches it. I did partially refute the reporter's stated trigger: a sub-admin with unpropagated claims can never reach /payments, because initAuthListener→loadAdminDoc reads admins/{uid}, which firestore.rules:196-198 gates on the role claim, so such a user is bounced to /login; and the 'missing index' trigger is implausible since orderBy('createdAt','desc') is a single-field auto-indexed query and firestore.indexes.json has "fieldOverrides": []. But the defect survives via reachable paths: payments read requires isAdmin() (rules:83), so a session whose role claim is revoked or admin suspended mid-session (token refreshes hourly) that then opens Payments for the first time gets a cold-start permission-denied, as does any resource-exhausted/quota error — both render the authoritative-looking 'No payments yet.' plus ₹0 revenue on the one screen where a false zero matters most. Real, fixable, one-line-plus-error-row change mirroring CouponsListPage. Medium confidence only because the trigger is narrow and the severity is UI-state rather than data corruption.

findings.title: Return refunds never settle the payments/{orderId} document, unlike the cancellation path
findings.detail: The approve transaction updates orderRequests, the order (refundedPaise, paymentStatus, embedded items), the customer wallet, the product soldCount and commissions — but never touches payments/{orderId}. functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:79-80,219-223 does exactly the opposite: it reads payments/{orderId} up front and settles it to status 'refunded' precisely so "the admin Payments page doesn't keep showing a captured/pending payment". The admin Payments list renders that document's status directly (admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:9-29, PaymentsListPage.tsx:106). Additionally, decisions.ts:159-162 flips order.paymentStatus to 'refunded' only when the refund is full AND wallet-mode, and 'partial_refund' is never written by any Cloud Function (grep: it exists only in packages/shared/src/enums.ts:70 and in the two admin pill mappers, payments.ts:25 and orders/api/orders.ts:73), so the entire partial-refund pill is dead code.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin approves a ₹899 return on a fully captured ₹899 online order. Orders list now shows the order as 'Refunded'; the Payments list still shows that transaction as 'Success/Captured' with the full amount and no refund trace, so the two Operations screens disagree and the payments export used for reconciliation overstates net collections. For a partial return (one item of three) neither screen shows anything at all.
findings.fix: Read payments/{orderId} inside the approve transaction and update it to 'refunded' or 'partial_refund' based on refundedPaise vs amountPaise, mirroring cancel.ts:219-223.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:157 updates the order (refundedPaise, paymentStatus, items), wallet, soldCount and commissions but never touches payments/{orderId}; grep shows the only writers of that doc are checkout.ts (placeOrder/markPaymentFailed/verifyPayment) and cancel.ts:219-223, which settles it to 'refunded' specifically so the admin Payments page stops showing a captured payment. There are no Firestore triggers in the repo (zero onDocumentWritten/Updated/Created hits) and no client writer (only firestore.rules:91 and the read-only usePaymentsList), so nothing reconciles it later. Impact is functional, not cosmetic: PaymentsListPage.tsx:29-41 sums amountPaise for status==='captured' into the "this month" KPI and onExport(true) filters the GST-invoice CSV on 'captured', so a fully wallet-refunded return stays in both while the Orders list shows the order as Refunded. The partial_refund sub-claim also holds — occurrences are only packages/shared/src/enums.ts:70, admin payments.ts:25, orders/api/orders.ts:73 and reports.ts:226 (all consumers); seed.ts never writes it. Partial mitigation exists but only in Reports: reports.ts:242-249 derives isRefunded from refundedPaise/orderRequests as well, so the refund-rate KPI is fine; the Payments module has no such fallback. Not on the already-fixed list (which names placeOrder/verifyPayment/cancel and pointedly omits returns) nor the intentional list. Minor nuance: with autoRefundToWallet OFF the order also stays 'captured', so the divergence is specific to the default wallet-auto-refund path.

findings.title: Opening Refunds streams the entire customers collection live, purely to map uid → name
findings.detail: ReturnsListPage calls useCustomersList(), which attaches an unbounded real-time listener to `query(collection(db,'customers'), orderBy('createdAt','desc'))` (admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:10-13) with no limit, solely to build nameByUid (line 47) for the 10 rows on screen. orderRequests itself is also fetched whole with no limit (api/returns.ts:25-27) — defensible per its documented rationale, but it grows without bound and every admin session re-downloads all history. Unlike orders, which denormalise customerName onto the doc (used by OrdersListPage), orderRequests carries no customer name, forcing this join. The customers listener's error state is also discarded (only `data` is destructured), so a failed/denied customers read silently degrades every row and the CSV export to raw uids with no warning.
findings.failure_scenario: On a store with 40k customers, an admin clicking 'Refunds' to review one pending return downloads and keeps live 40k customer documents; the page takes seconds to become useful and Firestore bills 40k reads per visit. If that read fails, the table and barkath-refunds.csv show 28-character uids in the Customer column with no error shown, and the search box stops matching customer names.
findings.fix: Denormalise customerName (and customerPhone) onto the orderRequests doc in requestReturnOrReplacement the way orders already do, and drop the useCustomersList() join; failing that, fetch only the uids on the current page and surface the customers-read error.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. ReturnsListPage.tsx:38 attaches the unbounded live customers query (admin/src/features/customers/api/customers.ts:10-13, no limit) solely to build nameByUid (line 47) for the 10 visible rows, the search filter, the CSV and the drawer text. There is no global prefetch of CUSTOMERS_KEY, and firestoreCache.ts tears the listener down at zero refs while lib/firebase.ts initialises Firestore with the default memory cache (no persistentLocalCache), so each visit to Refunds re-downloads the whole collection. This is an outlier, not the house pattern: Order.customerName and Review.customerName (packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:138,192) and WithdrawalRequest.customerName are denormalised, so Orders/Reviews/Affiliate lists do no join; only OrderRequest (commerce.ts:160-186) omits it, forcing this one join. The fix is cheap and server-side: functions/src/returns/requests.ts already holds the order doc inside its transaction (it reads o.shortId, o.subtotalPaise, o.discountPaise) and could write customerName at creation, with the uid fallback kept for old docs. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Caveat: the secondary error-swallow point is weak — firestore.rules:157 lets any admin read customers, so there is no sub-admin permission-denied path and the failure degrades gracefully to uids; the perf severity also scales with customer count and is invisible on seed data.

findings.title: getCoupon rejection is unhandled — deep-linking an edit page can hang on the spinner forever
findings.detail: `getCoupon(routeId!).then(...)` has no `.catch`, and `setLoading(false)` lives only inside the fulfilled branch (line 111). `loading` is initialised to `!isNew && !seed` (line 65), so on a cold cache (hard refresh or a pasted URL) the page renders only the Spinner (lines 187-193). Any rejection — offline, a rules denial, a transient Firestore error — leaves the component stuck on the spinner and produces an unhandled promise rejection. There is no error UI and no retry.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin pastes /coupons/coupon_2 into a fresh tab on a flaky connection. The getDoc rejects; the screen shows a spinning loader indefinitely with no message, no toast and no way out except the sidebar, and the console logs an uncaught rejection.
findings.fix: Chain `.catch((e) => { toast.error('Could not load this coupon.'); navigate('/coupons'); })` (or render an inline error + Retry) and move `setLoading(false)` into a `.finally`.

verdict.reason: Claim verified line-by-line and I could not refute it. CouponFormPage.tsx:90 has no .catch and setLoading(false) exists only in the fulfilled branch (line 111); loading initialises to !isNew && !seed (line 65) where seed comes from the module-level in-memory cache in admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts, which is empty on a hard refresh or pasted URL; the loading branch (lines 187-193) renders only a Spinner with no error or retry state. Nothing handles it elsewhere: /coupons/:id is a plain deep-linkable route (admin/src/app/router.tsx:87), no route has an errorElement, there is no ErrorBoundary/componentDidCatch anywhere in admin/src, and main.tsx registers no unhandledrejection handler (and an error boundary would not catch a promise rejection anyway). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two caveats that lower severity but do not refute: the rules-denial vector is mostly unavailable because firestore.rules:74 grants coupons read to any signed-in user, so the realistic trigger is an offline/transient getDoc rejection; and the same un-caught load pattern exists in ProductFormPage.tsx:109, BannerFormPage.tsx:60 and CategoryFormPage.tsx:54, making this a systemic robustness gap rather than a coupon-specific regression. The admin can still leave via the sidebar, so it is a stuck-view/no-feedback defect, not data loss. Real and trivially fixable (catch -> setLoading(false) + error UI), so refuted=false at medium confidence given the modest severity.

findings.title: Usage limit accepts 0 (and fractions), producing a coupon that is dead on arrival
findings.detail: The Usage limit input (lines 281-288) has no validation entry in `FormErrors` and `onSave` maps it as `maxUsesTotal: usageLimit === '' ? null : Number(usageLimit)` — only an empty string means unlimited. A typed 0 is stored as 0. Server side, functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:164-166 does `const maxTotal = c.maxUsesTotal == null ? null : Number(c.maxUsesTotal); if (maxTotal !== null && Number(c.usesCount ?? 0) >= maxTotal) throw 'This coupon has reached its usage limit.'` — with maxTotal 0 and usesCount 0 that is `0 >= 0`, always true. The same comparison in web/offers.ts:64 and checkout.ts:275/513 also hides it from every offer list. Fractional and negative values typed into the number input are likewise stored unvalidated.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates DIWALI50 and types 0 in Usage limit meaning 'no limit'. It saves with a green 'Coupon created' toast and shows Status = Active, Used = 0 in the list. Every customer who enters DIWALI50 gets 'This coupon has reached its usage limit.' and it never appears in any offer list. Nothing in the admin UI explains why.
findings.fix: Validate the field: reject values < 1 and non-integers with an inline error, and/or treat 0 as null (unlimited) in onSave. Add a helper line saying 'Leave blank for unlimited'.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. CouponFormPage.tsx:46-51 has no FormErrors entry for the usage limit and onSave (122-156) never validates it; line 166 maps only '' to null, so a typed 0 (or 2.5, or a negative — min/step on the number input at line 404-412 are advisory, there is no form-level validity check) is stored verbatim. coupons.ts:129 writes it through unclamped and computeStatus still yields 'active'; firestore.rules:74 has no field validation. Server-side every consumer treats 0 as a hard limit rather than unlimited — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:184-187 (code entry), :294-295 (autoBestOffer), :580-583 (placeOrder) and web/src/components/checkout/offers.ts:63-64 all do `maxUsesTotal == null ? null : Number(...)` then `usesCount >= maxTotal`, i.e. 0 >= 0 is always true. grep across packages/shared, web, app, functions and scripts shows no normaliser anywhere; the Flutter app never reads the field. Admin gives zero feedback: CouponsListPage.tsx:164 renders usesCount only, never the limit, and the badge stays Active. The codebase's own sibling field uses the opposite convention (checkout.ts:188 treats maxUsesPerUser 0 as unlimited), which makes '0 = no limit' a very natural admin assumption and strengthens the trap. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Real, functional (coupon is unusable and invisible in every offer list), and fixable with a validation entry.

findings.title: "Activate" on an expired campaign reports success but leaves it dead
findings.detail: `onToggleStatus` reads `loadedRef.current.status`, which is the *effective* status from `useSpinCampaign` → `withEffectiveStatus` (api/spinner.ts:42-45, 60-64). For a campaign past `endsAt` this is `'ended'`, so `isActive` is false, the button renders "Activate", and clicking it writes `status:'active'` and toasts "Campaign activated" (lines 256-260). But `effectiveSpinStatus` immediately recomputes `'ended'` from the unchanged `endsAt`, so the badge flips straight back; `executeSpin` still rejects with "This spin campaign has ended." (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:62, checked *before* status) and both the app (spin_repository.dart:39-46) and admin list keep hiding it.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin opens a campaign that ended yesterday, sees the "Activate" button, clicks it, gets a green "Campaign activated" toast — and nothing changes. No customer can spin, and the admin is never told that the end date is the blocker.
findings.fix: Disable the button (or relabel it "Extend & activate") when `effectiveSpinStatus(campaign) === 'ended'`, and either refuse the write or push `endsAt` forward as part of the same action.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Verified end to end:

1. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:36-45 — `effectiveSpinStatus` returns 'ended' when `status === 'active'` and `endsAt < now`; `withEffectiveStatus` is applied by BOTH `useSpinCampaignsList` (60-64) and `useSpinCampaign` (73-78). So the detail page receives the *derived* status, not the stored one.

2. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CampaignDetailPage.tsx:141 — `loadedRef.current = campaign` stores that same derived object; line 256 `const next = loaded.status === 'active' ? 'paused' : 'active'` and line 286 `const isActive = campaign.status === 'active'` therefore both read the derived value. For a campaign past `endsAt` the button renders "Activate" (line 297) and clicking writes `{status:'active'}` via `setCampaignStatus` (api/spinner.ts:181) then toasts "Campaign activated" (line 260) unconditionally on write success. There is no `endsAt` guard, no `disabled`, and the write is a literal no-op when the stored status is already 'active' (only `updatedAt` moves). The next snapshot re-derives 'ended' and the button label flips right back to "Activate".

3. No guard elsewhere. `setCampaignStatus` has exactly one call site in the whole admin (grep over admin/src): CampaignDetailPage.tsx:259. The list page has no activate action; CreateCampaignPage's "Activate immediately" is a different path.

4. Server and customer surfaces confirm the campaign stays dead: functions/src/spin/execute.ts:62 checks `now > endsAt` BEFORE the stored status and throws 'This spin campaign has ended.'; app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart `activeCampaign()` filters `status == 'active'` and then re-applies `_isLive()` on startsAt/endsAt, so the wheel still never renders.

Checked the exclusion lists: the ALREADY-FIXED entry "Spin campaign expiry computed on read" is precisely what introduced this asymmetry (the read is window-aware, the write path is not), so it does not cover this. Nothing in KNOWN+INTENTIONAL applies. Not cosmetic — the admin is told the campaign is live when no customer can spin, and the real blocker (end date) is never surfaced. Reachable, real, and fixable (guard on `endsAt`/use the stored status for the toggle and prompt to extend the window).

findings.title: Nothing prevents multiple simultaneously-active campaigns; the web picks an arbitrary one and ignores the schedule window
findings.detail: Neither `createCampaign` (api/spinner.ts:139-160, with "Activate immediately" defaulting to `true` at CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33) nor `setCampaignStatus` (api/spinner.ts:181) deactivates any other campaign, and the list page happily shows several "Active" cards. The web reads `query(collection(db,'spinCampaigns'), where('status','==','active'))` with no `orderBy` and no window filter, then takes `campaigns.data[0]` (lines 54-58). The app is stricter — it filters `startsAt…endsAt` in `_isLive` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:39-46) — so the two surfaces can serve different campaigns, and the web can serve a scheduled-but-not-started or already-ended one.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin creates "Eid Mega Spin" starting next month with "Activate immediately" left on (the default), while "Ramadan Spin" is still running. On the web rewards page the customer may be shown the Eid wheel (Firestore returns it first), and every click on Spin returns `failed-precondition: This spin campaign hasn't started yet.` — while the app correctly shows the Ramadan wheel. In the admin the new campaign shows the badge "Scheduled", giving no hint it is live to web users.
findings.fix: Enforce single-active in the admin (deactivate other campaigns when one is activated, or block activation with a clear error), and add the `startsAt/endsAt` window filter + a deterministic sort to the web query so it matches the app and `executeSpin`.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading all four surfaces. web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:54-58 queries spinCampaigns with only where('status','==','active'), no orderBy, no window filter, and takes campaigns.data[0]; useCollection (web/src/lib/useCollection.ts) applies no sorting, so the pick is arbitrary (__name__ order). No later guard in the file checks startsAt/endsAt — spin() only guards !campaign and spinsLeft<=0, and its catch handles only 'resource-exhausted', so a 'failed-precondition' window rejection surfaces as the generic WALLET_CF_MSG toast. This is the only spinCampaigns read in web/. By contrast app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:26-46 does filter the window in _isLive, with a doc comment stating "status alone is not enough: nothing ever flips it when the campaign's window opens/closes" — so the surfaces provably diverge. functions/src/spin/execute.ts:56-64 checks the window before status and throws the exact "This spin campaign hasn't started yet." message; it rejects rather than falling back. On the admin side, createCampaign (admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:139-160) writes status:'active' when activateImmediately and setCampaignStatus (line 181) is a bare single-doc updateDoc — neither deactivates siblings, and firestore.rules:61 is a plain canWrite('spinnerCampaigns') with no uniqueness enforcement. CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33 is useState(true), so "Activate immediately" is the default, with editable dates defaulting to today→+30d. effectiveSpinStatus/statusBadge compute 'ended'/'Scheduled' on read but live only in admin/ and are never imported by web. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list: the compute-on-read spin-expiry fix reached admin, app and the callable but skipped the web rewards page, and the stated architecture rule (campaign expiry is compute-on-read, sweeps best-effort) makes an unfiltered status=='active' read a genuine violation. Impact is functional, not cosmetic: wrong slices rendered and every spin dead-ends in a generic error. Only minor overstatement is that the admin does badge a future campaign "Scheduled" — but that badge is admin-local and does not prevent the web from serving it.

findings.title: "Activate immediately" publishes the hardcoded starter wheel before the admin has configured anything
findings.detail: `createCampaign` writes `status:'active'` when the toggle is on — and it defaults to on (CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33) — together with `starterSlices()`: a hardcoded `₹10 off` / `10% off` / `Better luck next time` wheel (api/spinner.ts:125-132) with weights 40/30/30 and `minCartValuePaise: 0`. The doc is live to customers the instant it is written (app spin_repository.dart:26-35 streams `status=='active'` and `startsAt` is set to today 00:00), i.e. before the admin has reached the wheel editor that the success toast ("Campaign created — configure the wheel") tells them to go configure.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin fills in the name "Eid Mega Spin", leaves the defaults, clicks "Create & configure". Between that click and finishing the wheel editor, customers on the app can already spin and win real ₹10-off and uncapped 10%-off coupons from a placeholder wheel the admin never chose.
findings.fix: Always create as `draft`, and move activation to the detail page after the wheel is saved (or default the "Activate immediately" toggle to off and only allow it once slices are configured).

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — every link in the chain checks out, and no guard, fallback or server re-check exists.

1. Write side (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/api/spinner.ts:139-160): `createCampaign` writes `status: v.activateImmediately ? 'active' : 'draft'`, `startsAt = new Date(`${startDate}T00:00:00`)` and `slices: starterSlices()` in one `setDoc`. `starterSlices()` (lines 125-132) is a hardcoded placeholder wheel: `₹10 off` (flat 1000 paise, weight 40), `10% off` (weight 30, `discountMaxCapPaise: null`, i.e. UNCAPPED), `Better luck next time` (weight 30), all with `minCartValuePaise: 0`, `validityDays: 7`.

2. Default is on: /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/spinner/routes/CreateCampaignPage.tsx:33 `const [activate, setActivate] = useState(true)` and line 29 `startDate = isoDate(today)`, so `startsAt` is today 00:00 — already in the past. `onCreate` (37-70) does only name/date validation, then writes and toasts "Campaign created — configure the wheel", i.e. the flow itself admits the wheel is not configured yet.

3. It is immediately visible to customers on both surfaces: app `/home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:26-35` streams `where('status', isEqualTo: 'active')` and `_isLive()` only checks the startsAt/endsAt window (both satisfied); web `/home/h/barkath/web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:54-58` does `query(collection(db,'spinCampaigns'), where('status','==','active'))` and takes `campaigns.data[0]`. Rules (/home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:61) allow any signed-in user to read spinCampaigns.

4. Server-side does NOT re-check configuration: /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts validates window, `camp.status !== 'active'`, `slices.length === 0`, and eligibility — the starter slices satisfy all of them — then issues a real `customers/{uid}/coupons` doc with `discountMaxCapPaise: null`, `minCartValuePaise: 0`, `status: 'active'`. So a customer really can win an uncapped 10%-off coupon from a wheel the admin never chose.

5. Nothing reverts it: `CampaignDetailPage.tsx` only pauses/activates on an explicit click (line 256) and saves slices on explicit save (line 237); there is no create-time draft downgrade. The claim is not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (only "Spin campaign expiry computed on read" touches this feature) nor on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list.

Only nuance worth noting: `starterSlices()` is deliberate scaffolding ("so a freshly-created campaign is already configurable"), so the defect is really the combination of it with `activate` defaulting to `true` — the fix is either defaulting the toggle off, forcing `draft` until the wheel is saved, or making the starter prizes non-issuing (weight 0 / better_luck only). Either way it is a real, cheaply fixable defect with actual financial exposure.

findings.title: `executeSpin` reads the customer's entire `spinHistory` on every spin (unbounded, grows forever)
findings.detail: `db.collection('spinHistory').where('customerId','==',uid).get()` fetches every spin the customer has ever taken — across all campaigns, all time — then filters to today's campaign in memory (lines 103-108). There is no `createdAt` bound and no `limit`. The same unbounded pattern is mirrored client-side by live listeners: web `query(collection(db,'spinHistory'), where('customerId','==',uid))` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:61-64) and app `_history` (app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:47-52), both `snapshots()`/live with no bound.
findings.failure_scenario: A daily-spinner customer after a year has ~365 `spinHistory` docs; each spin costs a 365-doc read server-side plus a 365-doc realtime listener on the client, and both grow without limit. Nothing in the admin ever prunes `spinHistory` (no admin surface reads or writes that collection at all).
findings.fix: Add `.where('campaignId','==',campaignId).where('createdAt','>=', Timestamp.fromMillis(istMidnightMs))` with the composite index (or store a per-day counter doc such as `customers/{uid}/spinCounters/{campaignId}_{yyyymmdd}`), and bound the client listeners the same way.

verdict.reason: Verified accurate at /home/h/barkath/functions/src/spin/execute.ts:103: `db.collection('spinHistory').where('customerId','==',uid).get()` has no limit, no createdAt bound, and no campaignId filter — it reads the customer's entire lifetime spin history on every spin and filters to today's campaign in memory (lines 104-108). The inline comment (94-99) only justifies running the query outside the transaction and avoiding a composite index; it never claims the read is bounded, and firebase/firestore.indexes.json shows composite indexes are routinely added for orders/commissions, so the index argument is a choice, not a constraint. No mitigation exists elsewhere: functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts (the only scheduled file) never touches spinHistory, firestore.rules sets `allow write: if false` on it, and repo-wide the only readers are the two client listeners, which mirror the same unbounded pattern as live subscriptions (web/src/app/(shop)/account/rewards/page.tsx:60-63 and app/lib/features/spin/data/spin_repository.dart:47-52). Nothing ever prunes the collection. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (the prior spin finding in audit/findings.json is the unrelated spinsRemaining gating bug, which is already fixed in the current file) nor on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. Severity is modest — growth is linear per-customer (~365 docs/year for a daily spinner), so it is a cost/latency scalability defect rather than a correctness break — but it is real and cheaply fixable by adding a createdAt >= IST-midnight bound (or orderBy+limit) plus the matching composite index, mirrored in both clients. Confidence is medium only because the impact is bounded per-user rather than catastrophic.

findings.title: Custom URL deep link accepts any string — no scheme or format validation on either side
findings.detail: The Link URL input (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:214-222) is a plain text field; validate() only checks `!target.trim()` (lines 79-81). The CF schema is `target: z.string().nullable().optional()` (broadcast.ts:16) — any string passes. The app deliberately refuses anything that isn't http/https: notifications_screen.dart:188-194 does `Uri.tryParse(target)` and only launches when `uri.scheme == 'http' || 'https'`, otherwise the tap does nothing at all (no error, no fallback). The placeholder "https://…" is the only hint the admin gets.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin types `www.barkath.com/eid-sale` (no scheme) or `barkath://spin` into Link URL and sends. Every validation passes, the broadcast is recorded Sent, and every customer who taps the notification card gets absolutely nothing — the card stays inert with no error, and the admin has no way to tell from the Opened column that the destination was malformed.
findings.fix: Validate in the create form (and mirror it in the zod schema): require the URL to parse and its protocol to be http: or https:, e.g. reject in validate() with 'Enter a full https:// URL'; optionally offer an in-app-route picker instead of free text for internal destinations.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all three surfaces. Admin (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:214-222) renders the Link URL as a plain <input> with no type="url"/pattern and outside any <form>; validate() (lines 72-84) only rejects an empty target, so `www.barkath.com/sale` or `barkath://spin` passes. The CF schema (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:16) is `target: z.string().nullable().optional()` with no refine and no normalization — it persists the string verbatim to broadcasts/{id} and to every customers/{uid}/notifications doc and marks status 'sent'. The app (app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:169-196) launches only when Uri.tryParse yields scheme http/https, and its own comment states this restriction is a deliberate security guard, so it will not be loosened; a scheme-less or custom-scheme target makes the card silently inert (no error, no fallback to home). Grep over web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared and admin/ shows the Flutter screen is the sole consumer of this deepLink object (the shared `deepLink: string` fields are the unrelated admin NotificationBell shape). The 'url' option is live in DEEP_LINK_TYPES, so the path is reachable. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and not cosmetic: the fan-out is irreversible and Opened still increments on read (markBroadcastOpened fires when the inbox marks read, not on tap), so the admin gets no signal the destination is dead. Real, fixable validation defect — add an http(s) scheme check in validate() and a matching zod refine for type==='url' server-side.

findings.title: Web inbox ignores deepLink and never reports opens, so the admin's Opened column undercounts
findings.detail: The admin sends a deepLink on every broadcast and the app honours it, but the web inbox renders each row as a non-interactive <div> with no onClick and no use of `deepLink` (page.tsx:118-146) — grepping web for `deepLink` returns zero hits. Worse for the stats: web marks every unread row `read: true` in a batch on unmount (page.tsx:70-78) but never calls the `markBroadcastOpened` callable — that call exists only in the Flutter app (app/lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:96-109). Because markBroadcastOpened is the only writer of `broadcasts.opened` (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:133) and the app only reports opens for rows it is flipping from unread→read (notifications_repository.dart:82), a row already marked read by web can never be counted afterwards.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer opens the broadcast on the website: the row is silently marked read, the deep link is never offered so they can't reach the promoted product, and `broadcasts.opened` is not incremented. They later open the app, where the notification already shows as read, so no open is reported there either. The admin's Notifications list shows Sent=1,240 / Opened=90 when far more people actually read it, and the campaign is judged a failure.
findings.fix: Make the web rows clickable using the same type→route mapping the app uses (home/product/category/url), and have the web page call the `markBroadcastOpened` callable with the `broadcastId`s of the rows it is about to flip to read, in the same effect that batches the read update.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all points. web/src/app/(shop)/account/notifications/page.tsx renders rows as non-interactive divs and never touches deepLink — grep for deepLink|markBroadcastOpened|broadcast across all of web/src returns zero hits, so it is genuinely dead on that surface even though the admin always sends a deepLink (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:91-98, defaulting to type:'home' but supporting product/category/url) and the CF persists it onto each inbox doc (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:52). The stats half is worse and unambiguously a defect: broadcasts.opened is written only twice — initialised to 0 at broadcast.ts:46 and incremented at broadcast.ts:133 inside markBroadcastOpened — and there are NO Firestore triggers anywhere in functions/src (grep onDocumentUpdated/onDocumentWritten is empty), so nothing server-side backfills opens from the read flag. markBroadcastOpened is guarded only by requireCustomer (guards.ts:28-31, just req.auth) and web/src/lib/firebase.ts:23 exports a configured asia-south1 functions instance, so web could call it and simply does not. Meanwhile web's unmount effect (page.tsx:70-78) batch-sets read:true on every unread row, and the app only attributes opens for rows it flips from unread (markAllRead queries where read==false; markRead guards on wasUnread), making the loss permanent. The admin surfaces the undercount directly at NotificationsListPage.tsx:101 (num(b.opened)). Not on the exclusion lists: the ALREADY-FIXED note 'broadcasts.opened counted' landed only in the Flutter app plus the callable; web was never wired and actively poisons later counting. Extra detail for the fixer: packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:197 types deepLink as a string and omits broadcastId entirely, while the CF writes an object {type,target,label}, so a web fix must read raw doc fields or the shared type must be corrected first.

findings.title: "Send similar" row action prefills nothing — it just opens a blank create form
findings.detail: The only item in the per-row DropdownMenu is `{ label: 'Send similar', onClick: () => navigate('/notifications/create') }` (NotificationsListPage.tsx:111-119). It passes no router state, no query string and no id, and NotificationCreatePage initialises every field to empty/default (`useState('')`, audience 'all', linkType 'home' — NotificationCreatePage.tsx:37-41) with no location.state or param reading anywhere in the file. So the action is indistinguishable from the header's "+ Create notification" button.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin finds last month's best-performing broadcast in the list, opens the row menu and clicks "Send similar" expecting the title, message, audience and deep link to be copied in for a quick tweak. They land on a completely blank form and must retype everything — and since the list never displays the old body or deep link, they cannot even copy it from the previous row.
findings.fix: Pass the source broadcast through router state (`navigate('/notifications/create', { state: { from: b } })`) and seed the create page's useState initialisers from `useLocation().state?.from` (title, body, audience, deepLink.type/target).

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. NotificationsListPage.tsx:111-119 contains a single row-menu item labelled 'Send similar' whose onClick is `navigate('/notifications/create')` — no state, no query string, no id — identical to the header's '+ Create notification' (line 47) and the dashboard QuickAction. NotificationCreatePage.tsx:37-41 initialises every field blank (title/body '', audience 'all', linkType 'home', target '') and the file contains no useLocation/useParams/useSearchParams/store read, so nothing can hydrate it; router.tsx:100 registers only the parameterless '/notifications/create' route. Attempts to refute failed: the control is reachable (DropdownMenu portals and fires onClick normally) and the flow is live (adminSendBroadcastNotification is exported at functions/src/index.ts:55 / notifications/broadcast.ts:33); no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared) implements a duplicate/template mechanism; and the item is not cosmetic because the list shows no body or deepLink column, so the promised values are unrecoverable from the UI. It is trivially fixable since the Broadcast row already carries title, body, audience, audienceLabel and deepLink (api/notifications.ts:19-36). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.

findings.title: 'Enable affiliate wallet access' toggle writes a field nothing reads
findings.detail: The toggle sends `walletEnabled` to adminAllocateAffiliate, which persists it as `affiliate.walletEnabled` (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:57 — the code comment itself says 'at least persist what the admin chose'). Grepping all four surfaces, the only other `walletEnabled` hits are settings/paymentGateway.walletEnabled (web checkout, admin PaymentGatewayTab) which is an unrelated field. Nothing gates on `affiliate.walletEnabled`: `requestWithdrawal` checks only `aff.enabled` (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:36), the web affiliate/withdraw pages check only `affiliate.enabled`, and the Flutter AffiliateInfo model (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_models.dart:24-31) doesn't even parse it — it isn't in the shared `AffiliateInfo` type either. The adjacent 'Wallet / Affiliate wallet' field (lines 104-110) is a plain div with a chevron icon that looks like a select but has no handler at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Admin allocates an affiliate with 'Enable affiliate wallet access' switched OFF and confirms a dialog that says '…with a 5% commission rate' (wallet clause omitted). The affiliate nevertheless sees the affiliate wallet, the withdrawable balance and can submit a withdrawal request immediately. The admin also has no screen anywhere that shows the flag back, so the mistake is invisible.
findings.fix: Either enforce `affiliate.walletEnabled` in requestWithdrawal (and hide the wallet on web/app when false, adding it to the shared AffiliateInfo type), or delete the toggle and the fake 'Wallet' field.

verdict.reason: Could not refute. `walletEnabled` from AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:55/115 is persisted by adminAllocateAffiliate as `affiliate.walletEnabled` (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:57) and read by nothing: a repo-wide grep across admin/, web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared and scripts/ returns only this page, the admin request type (admin/src/features/affiliate/api/affiliate.ts:61), the CF write itself (whose only "read" is its own carry-forward fallback), and the unrelated settings/paymentGateway.walletEnabled used by web checkout (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:239), Flutter checkout (app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:207) and PaymentGatewayTab. Every affiliate consumer gates on `affiliate.enabled` only: requestWithdrawal (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:36 `if (!aff?.enabled)`), web account/affiliate/page.tsx:90 and account/affiliate/withdraw/page.tsx:84; the Flutter AffiliateInfo model (app/lib/features/affiliate/data/affiliate_models.dart:23-31) does not parse the field at all. So switching the toggle OFF still leaves the affiliate with full wallet/withdrawal access, while the confirm dialog (line 130) implies the choice matters, and no admin screen surfaces the flag afterwards. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers only the optional commissionRate) nor the known-intentional list; the CF comment "at least persist what the admin chose" concedes it is write-only. Real, fixable defect — either enforce it in requestWithdrawal/the customer surfaces or drop the toggle. Minor caveat: the adjacent "Wallet / Affiliate wallet" pseudo-select (lines 103-109) is genuinely cosmetic filler, but that is a side note, not the substance of the claim.

findings.title: Firestore errors on the affiliate screen are swallowed — the page shows 'No withdrawal requests yet'
findings.detail: `useLiveCollection` returns `{data, loading, error}` and sets `error` on the snapshot error callback (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts:113-117). AffiliateListPage destructures only `data`/`loading` at lines 36-37 and never renders the error, unlike every comparable screen (returns ReturnsListPage.tsx:37/106, subadmin SubAdminListPage.tsx:30/125, coupons, spinner). On error the data array stays `[]` and `loading` becomes false, so the table falls into the `withdrawals.length === 0` branch (line 157) and the stat cards render 0/₹0.
findings.failure_scenario: A sub-admin whose Firebase custom claim hasn't propagated (or any permission-denied / missing-index / offline condition) opens Affiliate Program and sees '0 affiliates · ₹0 pending payout', four zeroed stat cards and 'No withdrawal requests yet.' They conclude nobody has requested a payout while real pending requests are sitting in Firestore, and nothing in the UI or a toast hints at a failure.
findings.fix: Destructure `error` from both hooks and render the standard inline error banner (as ReturnsListPage does) instead of the empty state when `error && data.length === 0`.

verdict.reason: The core code fact holds: firestoreCache.ts:117-121 sets {data: [], loading:false, error} on the snapshot error callback, and AffiliateListPage.tsx:36-37 destructures only data/loading, so a read error renders the 'No withdrawal requests yet.' branch (line 161) plus zeroed stat cards with no toast or banner. The repo explicitly treats this as a defect elsewhere (ReturnsListPage.tsx:105 'Read error — surfaced instead of a misleading empty state', SubAdminListPage.tsx:125, SpinnerListPage.tsx:89, CouponsListPage.tsx:51), and the fix is a small, established pattern on a money-critical screen. Two parts of the claim are overstated, however. (a) 'unlike every comparable screen' is false — CustomersListPage.tsx:19, OrdersListPage.tsx:26, PaymentsListPage.tsx:22 and ReviewsListPage.tsx:30 ignore `error` identically, so this is a shared gap, not an affiliate-specific outlier. (b) The stated trigger is mostly unreachable: firestore.rules:215 gates admins/{uid} on the role claim and initAuthListener (authStore.ts) catches a failed loadAdminDoc and signs the user out to /login, so an unpropagated sub-admin claim bounces to login rather than showing a silent affiliate page; plain offline does not fire the onSnapshot error callback, and both queries are indexed (indexes.json:100-107; affiliate.enabled == is single-field). Reachable triggers reduce to mid-session claim revocation (onAuthStateChanged does not re-fire on token refresh), a rules redeploy, or resource-exhausted. Real and fixable, but lower severity and less unique than claimed.

findings.title: settings/affiliate is unmanageable from the admin panel; commission rates are a hardcoded 3/5/7/10 list
findings.detail: `RATE_OPTIONS` is a hardcoded array and the form defaults to '5' without ever reading `settings/affiliate.defaultCommissionRate` — which the CF falls back to (functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts:42) and which the admin already has a hook for: `useAffiliate()` in admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 is defined and never imported anywhere. There is no Affiliate tab in SettingsPage (VALID = variables/delivery/gateway/storefront/support/content, admin/src/features/settings/routes/SettingsPage.tsx:13), so `minWithdrawalPaise`, `processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise`, `maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise` and `defaultCommissionRate` — all read live by requestWithdrawal (functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:25-28) and by the web withdraw screen — can only ever be set by re-running scripts/seed.ts or bootstrap-real.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: Ops decides the minimum withdrawal should rise from ₹500 to ₹1,000 and the processing fee should become 1%. There is no screen in the admin panel to change either, so the values stay at whatever seed wrote; and an admin who wants to allocate an affiliate at 4% or 15% cannot — the dropdown only offers 3/5/7/10.
findings.fix: Add an Affiliate settings tab wired to the existing `useAffiliate()` hook (default rate, min withdrawal, fee type/value/min, max per day) and seed RATE_OPTIONS / the default selection from `defaultCommissionRate`, or make the rate a free numeric percent input.

verdict.reason: Real, fixable gap. Verified: RATE_OPTIONS at admin/src/features/affiliate/routes/AllocateAffiliatePage.tsx:14 is a hardcoded 3/5/7/10 list with a '5' default and no settings read; useAffiliate() at admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:25 is defined and imported nowhere in admin/src; SettingsShell's SettingsTabId/SETTINGS_TABS have no affiliate tab and no AffiliateTab route file exists; the only writers of settings/affiliate in the repo are scripts/seed.ts:206 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:116. Meanwhile the doc is live-read in production by functions/src/affiliate/requests.ts:24-28 (minWithdrawalPaise, processingFeeType/Value/MinPaise on every withdrawal), by functions/src/affiliate/withdrawals.ts (defaultCommissionRate fallback), and by the web withdraw screen via useAffiliateSettings — so ops genuinely cannot change the minimum withdrawal or processing fee without re-running a seed script. firestore.rules:56 already allows canWrite('settings'), so nothing blocks a fix. Aggravating: the allocate screen filters to customers with !affiliate.enabled, so an existing affiliate's rate cannot be edited from admin at all. Not on the already-fixed list (that entry only made the CF accept an optional commissionRate, which is what makes arbitrary rates legal server-side) and not on the intentional list (that covers manual payouts / no bank API, not settings management). Two minor over-claims that do not change the verdict: maxWithdrawalPerDayPaise is read by no runtime code (dead config, only seed/bootstrap/type), and defaultCommissionRate is only a fallback since the admin form always sends an explicit rate.

findings.title: Top products silently ignores legacy orders that keep line items in orders/{id}/items — an explicit architecture-rule violation
findings.detail: `computeTopProducts` iterates only `o.items ?? []` (l.387). The comment on l.385-386 admits it: 'Legacy orders that predate the embedded array keep their lines in the orders/{id}/items subcollection, which a pure function can't read, so they contribute nothing here.' The project rule is that readers must handle BOTH shapes, and the rest of the stack does — `functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:68-74` and `functions/src/returns/requests.ts` both fall back to `orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}`, and the shared type documents the fallback (packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts:41-45). Reports is the one reader that skips it, and it skips it without any indication in the UI.
findings.failure_scenario: An order placed before the embedded-items migration is delivered for ₹80,000 inside the reporting window. 'Total revenue' includes the full ₹80,000 (it reads `totalPaise` off the order doc), the revenue-by-month bar includes it, but the products on that order contribute ₹0 to 'Top products'. The two panels on the same screen disagree, and a product that only ever sold on legacy orders never appears in the top-5 no matter how much it sold.
findings.fix: Either fetch the missing lines (collection-group query on `items`, or a per-order subcollection read for orders where `items` is absent, feeding the result into the memoized computation), or — if legacy orders are genuinely gone — remove the dead fallback contract and assert `items` is always present. Silently dropping them while still counting their revenue elsewhere is the defect.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:387 reads only the embedded `o.items` array, and the in-code comment at lines 382-386 admits legacy subcollection orders contribute nothing. Every other reader in the stack honours the documented dual-shape contract: admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:35-45 (useOrderItems falls back to orders/{id}/items), functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:68-74, web/src/components/account/orders.ts:123 and :282, and packages/shared/src/types/orders.ts states readers must fall back. No server-side aggregate, guard, or alternate source covers Reports; itemsSummary is not used and holds no money. Because revenue KPI and the trend bars read totalPaise off the order doc (reports.ts:253, :348), a legacy order counts fully toward revenue but zero toward Top products, so the two panels on the same screen disagree, and ReportsPage.tsx (157-175) shows no caveat. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Fixable with the existing pattern: hydrate orders missing `items` from their subcollection in useReportOrders before the pure compute. Confidence is medium only because reachability depends on legacy pre-migration orders existing inside the report window (the seed writes embedded items only), not because the code behaviour is in doubt.

findings.title: Top-products revenue uses gross lineTotalPaise while Total revenue uses net totalPaise — the two money definitions do not reconcile
findings.detail: l.391 computes each row as `item.lineTotalPaise ?? quantity * offerPricePaise`. `functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:89` writes `lineTotalPaise: offerPricePaise * l.qty` — the pre-discount line total — and l.624 writes `discountAppliedPaise: 0` unconditionally, so the per-item discount is never allocated. Coupon and spin discounts live only at order level (`discountPaise`), and `totalPaise` is `subtotal - discount + delivery + codSurcharge + tax` (checkout.ts:343-363). So the 'Top products' column, rendered with the same `formatMoneyCompact` and the same gold styling as the revenue KPI, is gross-of-discount money that can exceed the 'Total revenue' figure sitting directly above it. Note the returns CF does the allocation correctly (`functions/src/returns/requests.ts:47-52` pro-rates `orderDiscount` across lines by line total) — reports just doesn't.
findings.failure_scenario: A campaign runs a 60%-off coupon. In a month with ₹4,00,000 of realised revenue, the admin sees Top products listing five items summing to ₹9,50,000 — more than double the 'Total revenue' KPI on the same screen — and exports both numbers into the same CSV under headings that both say 'Revenue (INR)'.
findings.fix: Pro-rate the order-level `discountPaise` (and `spinRewardPaise`) across lines by line-total share, exactly as `functions/src/returns/requests.ts:47-52` already does, before accumulating into `acc`; or relabel the column 'Gross sales' so it is not read as revenue.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end and could not refute it. admin/src/features/reports/api/reports.ts:391 sums item.lineTotalPaise, which functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:109 writes as offerPricePaise * qty (pre-discount), with checkout.ts:703 hardcoding discountAppliedPaise: 0 on every embedded item; that is the only code path writing orders.items, and no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, seed) ever populates a per-item discount. Meanwhile reports.ts:252-253 computes Total revenue from o.totalPaise, which is net of discountPaise. So Top products is gross-of-discount money rendered with the same formatMoneyCompact styling on the same screen (ReportsPage.tsx:191) and exported under a numeric 'Revenue (INR)' CSV column (reports.ts:440-443) alongside the net KPI. Decisively, the repo already contains the correct allocation and documents why the gross figure is wrong: functions/src/returns/requests.ts:89-102 pro-rates orderDiscount across lines by line total (refundAmountPaise = lineTotal - discountShare) — so this is an internal inconsistency with an in-repo precedent, not a deliberate GMV metric. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists; the path runs on every Reports render; the fix is well-defined and uses data already on the order doc. Caveats that do not change the verdict: the claimed magnitude is exaggerated (needs a ~60% blanket discount, and the two numbers never reconcile exactly anyway since top-5 is a subset and totalPaise includes delivery/tax/COD surcharge), and the returns citation should be requests.ts:89-102, not 47-52. Scope note: the identical gross aggregation exists at admin/src/features/dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:364 (categoryPerformance), so a fix should cover both.

findings.title: The date-range subtitle prints the end date's year for both ends, so the 12M/30D labels state a wrong start date — and that wrong label is written into the CSV
findings.detail: `rangeLabel` (l.47-52) formats `from` and `to` with `{ day:'numeric', month:'short' }` — year deliberately omitted — then appends a single `to.getFullYear()`. Whenever the window crosses a year boundary (always, for 12M) the start date is captioned with the wrong year. It is rendered as the page subtitle (ReportsPage.tsx:94) and embedded verbatim in the export header (`Range,${range} (${rangeLabel(range)})`, reports.ts:427).
findings.failure_scenario: On 23 Jul 2026 with the default 12M preset, `rangeStart` returns 1 Aug 2025 but the header reads '1 Aug – 23 Jul 2026'. An admin reading it left-to-right sees a range starting in August 2026 — i.e. the future — or assumes the report covers Aug 2026 to Jul 2026. Selecting 30D on 5 Jan 2026 gives '7 Dec – 5 Jan 2026' when the window actually starts 7 Dec 2025. The exported CSV carries the same wrong range string, so the misstatement survives into any spreadsheet built on it.
findings.fix: Include the year on the start date whenever `from.getFullYear() !== to.getFullYear()`: e.g. `${day(from)}${sameYear ? '' : ' ' + from.getFullYear()} – ${day(to)} ${to.getFullYear()}`.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly by executing the real rangeStart/rangeLabel logic: on 23 Jul 2026 the default 12M preset yields the label "1 Aug – 23 Jul 2026" while the window actually starts 1 Aug 2025; 30D on 5 Jan 2026 yields "7 Dec – 5 Jan 2026" for a window starting 7 Dec 2025. Both of the claim's scenarios match character-for-character. Refutation attempts all failed: rangeLabel has only two call sites (ReportsPage.tsx:94 subtitle and reports.ts:427 CSV header) with no guard, wrapper or alternate date row — that string is the CSV's only statement of the period; the path is reachable on every visit since ReportsPage defaults to '12M'; it is not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and the JSDoc's same-year example ("1 Jan – 16 Jul 2026") shows the cross-year case was overlooked rather than deliberate. It is display-only — the analytics window itself is computed correctly — but a wrong start-date year printed as the report period and embedded in the exported CSV is incorrect information, not styling. One caveat: the claim's "always, for 12M" is slightly overstated, since in December the 12M window starts 1 Jan of the same year and the label is correct; that does not change the substance. Fix is a one-liner: append the year to `from` when from.getFullYear() !== to.getFullYear(). Confidence is medium only because the impact is confined to a label/export string with no effect on computed figures.

findings.title: Content pages missing an `order` field are invisible in the settings rail and can never be edited
findings.detail: `useContentPages()` queries `query(collection(db,'content'), orderBy('order','asc'))` (content.ts:24-26). Firestore excludes documents that lack the orderBy field, so any content doc without `order` never appears. scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:121-124 — the script used to bootstrap the real project — writes `content/privacyPolicy` and `content/termsConditions` with only `{id, title, body, bodyHtml, version, lastEditorUid, publishedAt, updatedAt}`: no `order`, no `slug`, no `published`, no `sections`, no `system`. The rail in SettingsShell.tsx:99-118 renders from that same query, and SettingsPage.tsx:44-46 resolves `?tab=content&id=…` against it, falling back to `pages[0]` and then to `<VariablesTab/>` (SettingsPage.tsx:65-74) when the list is empty. There is no unordered fallback and no 'no pages' empty state.
findings.failure_scenario: On the real (bootstrapped, non-seeded) project an admin opens Settings to edit the Privacy policy. The chip rail shows only the five built-in tabs and '+ New page'; clicking a bookmarked /settings?tab=privacy silently renders the Variables tab. The two existing content docs are unreachable and un-editable from the admin, and the storefront also hides them (`published` is missing → falsy). The admin's only recourse is to create duplicate pages.
findings.fix: Query the collection unordered and sort by `(order ?? 0)` client-side (the web already sorts in memory — web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:66-75), and/or backfill order/slug/published/sections in bootstrap-real.ts.

verdict.reason: Confirmed; I could not refute it. admin/src/features/settings/api/content.ts:23-27 uses query(collection(db,'content'), orderBy('order','asc')), and Firestore silently omits docs lacking the orderBy field. The repo's own production bootstrap — scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:121-124, wired as scripts/package.json "bootstrap": "tsx bootstrap-real.ts" and called from seedSettings()/main(), targeting the real project barkath-25607 — writes content/privacyPolicy and content/termsConditions with only {id,title,body,bodyHtml,version,lastEditorUid,publishedAt,updatedAt}: no order, slug, published, sections or system. scripts/seed.ts:232-258 does write the full schema but is emulator-only (FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST guardrail), which is why the bug never appears in dev/e2e. No fallback exists in admin: SettingsShell.tsx:99-118 renders the rail straight from that list, and SettingsPage.tsx:44-46 resolves ?id= only via pages.find(p => p.id === requestedId), falling back to pages[0] and then to <VariablesTab/> (SettingsPage.tsx:64-74), so an absent doc can never reach <ContentPageTab/> even though useContentPage(docId) would fetch it by id; the legacy map privacy→privacyPolicy / terms→termsConditions (SettingsPage.tsx:19-22) points at exactly those two docs, so those bookmarks render Variables. Decisive corroboration that admin is the outlier: both other surfaces deliberately avoid orderBy and sort in memory with a missing-field tolerance — web/src/lib/siteSettings.ts:73-80 sorts with (a.order ?? 0), and app/lib/features/settings/data/content_repository.dart:15-23 sorts in memory "matching the web". No backfill/migration script exists (scripts/ contains only backfill-return-item-status.mjs, unrelated), useLiveCollection (admin/src/hooks/firestoreCache.ts) has no unordered retry, and nothing on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists covers content pages. Severity caveat: impact is bounded — the admin can still create fresh pages (createContentPage always writes order/slug/published, and web resolves by slug), so the harm is two permanently unreachable orphan docs plus dead legacy bookmarks rather than a broken storefront. Still a real, functional, one-line-fixable defect (drop the orderBy and sort client-side like web/app; also complete the bootstrap write).

findings.title: Tax form writes businessCity, businessCountry and hsnCodes that no surface reads
findings.detail: DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:152-153 renders 'Business city' and 'Business country' inputs and line 92-93 writes `businessCity` / `businessCountry` to settings/tax; line 95 also round-trips `hsnCodes`. Grepping all four surfaces, `businessCity` and `businessCountry` appear only in packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:60-61, scripts/seed.ts:196-197 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:115 — no read in web/src, app/lib, functions/src or anywhere else in admin/src. `hsnCodes` is the same (types + seed only) and has no editor at all, so it is preserved forever but never editable and never rendered. By contrast the sibling fields on the same card ARE read: `legalName` and `gstin` by app/lib/features/orders/orders_repository.dart:43-47 (invoice issuer), `gstRate`/`gstEnabled`/`pricesIncludeTax` by all three checkout paths.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin relocates the business, updates 'Business city' from Bengaluru to Chennai and saves. Nothing changes on the invoices in the app, the web account pages, or any export — the invoice issuer line only prints legalName + GSTIN. The admin believes the address on customer invoices has been corrected.
findings.fix: Either surface businessCity/businessCountry on the invoice issuer block (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:116-117 and the web equivalent) alongside legalName/gstin, or remove the two inputs and the hsnCodes field from the schema.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. admin/src/features/settings/routes/DeliveryTaxTab.tsx:152-153 renders editable 'Business city'/'Business country' fields and lines 92-93 persist them to settings/tax, but an exhaustive grep across functions/src, web/src, app/lib, admin/src and packages/shared finds no reader: the only hits are the type (packages/shared/src/types/settings.ts:60-61), DEFAULT_TAX (admin/src/features/settings/api/settings.ts:119-120), scripts/seed.ts:196-197 and scripts/bootstrap-real.ts:115. Each settings/tax consumer was checked individually — functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:465, web/src/components/checkout/checkout.ts:45 and app/lib/features/checkout/data/checkout_repository.dart:186 read only gstRate/gstEnabled/pricesIncludeTax; app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:43-53 fetchIssuer() returns only legalName+gstin and app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:147-148 prints just 'name · GSTIN'. The server invoice (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:52-64) doesn't read settings/tax at all — it hardcodes the BARAKATH header and prints only the customer's Bill-to address. So the failure scenario holds: an admin editing Business city sees no change on any invoice or export. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Caveat on scope: the hsnCodes half of the report is weak — the `hsnCodes: tax?.hsnCodes ?? {}` round-trip is correct preservation (saveTax uses merge:true), and the missing editor is a feature gap, not a defect; the real, fixable issue is the two dead admin inputs, which should either be removed or wired into the invoice issuer.

findings.title: createSubAdmin leaves an orphan Auth user and permanently burns the email if the Firestore write fails
findings.detail: auth.createUser() runs first (line 34), then setCustomUserClaims (38) and the admins/{uid} doc write (40-46) with no transaction, no rollback and no try/catch. If any step after createUser fails, the Auth account exists with no admin doc. Worse, the create is wrapped in a bare `catch { throw new HttpsError('already-exists', 'An account with that email already exists.') }` — every createUser failure (quota, network, invalid password policy) is reported to the operator as a duplicate email.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator fills Create sub admin and hits Create admin; the Auth user is created, then the Firestore write fails (transient/rules/quota) and the toast shows a generic failure. They retry with the same email: createUser now throws for real and the UI says "An account with that email already exists." — but no row appears in the Sub Admin list, so the email is unusable forever and an Auth account exists that can authenticate yet is rejected by signInAdmin ("Not authorized to access admin panel") with no admin-panel way to see or delete it.
findings.fix: Wrap the post-createUser steps in try/catch and `auth.deleteUser(user.uid)` on failure; distinguish the real `auth/email-already-exists` code from other createUser errors instead of a blanket catch.

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:32-46 creates the Auth user, then sets claims and writes admins/{uid} with no try/catch and no compensating auth.deleteUser, and the bare `catch` at 35-37 discards the real error (no logging) and reports every createUser failure as 'already-exists'. No mitigation exists elsewhere: no getUserByEmail / beforeUserCreated / auth onCreate trigger anywhere in functions/src, so nothing back-fills the admins doc; the Sub Admin list (admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:19) reads only collection('admins'), so an orphan Auth user is invisible; and deleteSubAdmin (subAdmins.ts:109-110) throws not-found before reaching auth.deleteUser when the admins doc is missing, so the orphan cannot be removed from the panel. signInAdmin (admin/src/features/auth/api/auth.ts:38-42) rejects it with 'Not authorized to access admin panel.' exactly as described. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; sibling handlers in the same file explicitly tolerate partial failure (lines 91, 113) while the create path does not. Confidence is medium only because zod pre-validation makes the non-duplicate createUser failure a transient/quota window rather than a deterministic path — that lowers likelihood, not validity, and the fix (rollback on failure + map only auth/email-already-exists) is small.

findings.title: Permission and role changes never reach an already-open sub-admin session — the auth store snapshot is read once
findings.detail: initAuthListener calls loadAdminDoc(uid) once per onAuthStateChanged event (a one-shot getDoc, features/auth/api/auth.ts:52-55) and stores the plain object; there is no onSnapshot on admins/{uid}. Sidebar.tsx:11 and QuickActions.tsx:42 read that frozen object, so a permission edit made by updateSubAdmin is invisible to the target until they hard-reload the tab, while firestore.rules `can()` re-reads the live doc on every write.
findings.failure_scenario: A super admin removes the Coupons module from a sub-admin who is signed in. The sub-admin's sidebar still shows Coupons; they open a coupon, edit the discount cap and hit Save — the direct Firestore write is rejected by canWrite('coupons') and they get a generic failure toast on a screen they are still being shown, with no indication their access was revoked.
findings.fix: Subscribe to admins/{uid} with onSnapshot in initAuthListener and push updates into the store (also signing the user out when status flips to 'suspended').

verdict.reason: Confirmed. authStore.ts:27-56 loads admins/{uid} via a one-shot getDoc (auth.ts:76-79) inside onAuthStateChanged, which fires only on sign-in/sign-out, and no onSnapshot on admins/{uid} exists anywhere in admin/src (grep for onSnapshot yields only NotificationBell and firestoreCache). The store is only otherwise rewritten by LoginForm.tsx:40 and AccountDialogs.tsx:62 (own-profile save), neither of which covers a super-admin permission edit. No fallback guard rescues it: RequireModule.tsx:21 reads the very same frozen object, so the route guard is stale exactly like Sidebar.tsx:11 and QuickActions.tsx:42. Server-side enforcement is real but is what creates the dead end — firestore.rules can()/canWrite() (lines 29-40) get() the live doc on every write, coupons are a direct client write (coupons.ts:141,153), and CouponFormPage.tsx:181 surfaces the raw "Missing or insufficient permissions" as a generic toast. updateSubAdmin (functions/src/admin/subAdmins.ts:51-74) sets custom claims but never calls revokeRefreshTokens — only suspendSubAdmin (line 92) does, which is why suspension self-corrects and permission edits do not. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and no UI copy warns that changes need a re-login. Rules line 214-216 let a sub_admin read their own doc, so an onSnapshot fix is legal and small. Mitigating note: this is not a privilege-escalation hole — impact is stale nav, lost work, and an opaque error until a hard reload.
